# Lufia Design System (full)

> The complete agent-facing documentation of the package in one file: consuming guide, motion rules, then one spec per component. The index is in llms.txt.

## Consuming @lufia/design-system

How to use the package from an application. This is the guide an agent should read before it writes UI with these
components. For one component, read its spec in `docs/ai/components/<Name>.md` (or `components.json` for the typed API).

### Install

npm publishing is on hold. Install from a git tag; the package builds itself on install:

```bash
npm install github:luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system#<latest-tag>
```

Use the latest release tag listed in the changelog. Peer dependencies: React 19 and React DOM 19.

### Set up once, at the root of the app

```tsx
import "@lufia/design-system/tokens.css";
import "@lufia/design-system/themes/default.css";
```

- Light and dark follow `prefers-color-scheme`. Force one with `data-lufia-mode="light"` or `"dark"` on `<html>`.
- Pick a named theme with `data-lufia-theme="<name>"`.
- A brand is a CSS file in the consuming app that defines the semantic `--lufia-color-*` properties (and, optionally,
  `--lufia-font-family-*`). Do not fork components to rebrand.
- Wrap the app in `LufiaProvider` to set the link component (for client-side routing) and the aria-only labels.

```tsx
import { LufiaProvider } from "@lufia/design-system/components/LufiaProvider";
```

### Importing

- Import each component from its own subpath: `@lufia/design-system/components/<Name>`. Hooks live in the same place
  (`@lufia/design-system/components/useDismiss`).
- Motion primitives come from `@lufia/design-system/motion`.
- Token data is available as `@lufia/design-system/tokens` (typed map) and `@lufia/design-system/tokens.json`.
- The root export `@lufia/design-system` re-exports everything, but the subpaths keep bundles small.

### Live Storybook MCP for local agents

The official Storybook MCP addon is enabled for the development server:

```bash
npm run storybook
# Connect an MCP-capable agent to http://127.0.0.1:6006/mcp
```

Use `docs-list` and `docs-show` to discover components, real prop APIs and documented examples. The MCP dev toolset also supports Storybook development flows. The `test-run` toolset is intentionally disabled until an addon-vitest integration is configured and verified. Never connect a development MCP endpoint to an untrusted public network.

The GitHub Pages documentation remains **static**: it serves the machine-readable Lufia files at `/components.json` and the separate Storybook-native manifest at `/manifests/components.json`, but **not** `/mcp`. To connect a remote agent, run a trusted compatible MCP host rather than treating GitHub Pages as a live server.

### Coding agents: version-matched lookup

The installed package ships the AI docs of **its own version** (`node_modules/@lufia/design-system/dist/ai/`: `components.json`, one
spec per component, `llms.txt`) and a `lufia-ai` command that reads them offline, with no server and no network. Prefer it to
the published site, which always documents the latest version.

```bash
npx --no-install lufia-ai search "searchable async select"   # ranked components for a task (--json, --limit 8)
npx --no-install lufia-ai show Combobox                      # import path, props, example, accessibility (--json)
npx --no-install lufia-ai list                               # every component
npx --no-install lufia-ai version                            # the installed version
```

`lufia-ai mcp` starts a local stdio [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server with three read-only tools:
`search_components` (`query`, optional `limit`), `get_component` (`name`) and `list_components`. Each returns JSON text.
Register it in your agent. The package must be installed in the project: always pass `--no-install`, because a bare `npx lufia-ai` that finds no local copy downloads and runs whatever package of that name exists on npm (and without a terminal it does not ask first).

Claude Code, `.mcp.json` at the project root (or `claude mcp add --transport stdio --scope project lufia -- npx --no-install lufia-ai mcp`):

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "lufia": { "command": "npx", "args": ["--no-install", "lufia-ai", "mcp"] } } }
```

Cursor, `.cursor/mcp.json`:

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "lufia": { "command": "npx", "args": ["--no-install", "lufia-ai", "mcp"] } } }
```

VS Code (Copilot agent mode), `.vscode/mcp.json`; note the top-level key is `servers`, not `mcpServers`:

```json
{ "servers": { "lufia": { "type": "stdio", "command": "npx", "args": ["--no-install", "lufia-ai", "mcp"] } } }
```

The server must start in the project root, where `node_modules` lives. VS Code defaults to the workspace folder; if your host does not, set `"cwd": "${workspaceFolder}"` (VS Code) or the equivalent for the host.

The raw files are also importable, for example `@lufia/design-system/ai/components.json`.

### AI agent workflow

For coding agents, use **progressive disclosure** rather than loading the entire manifest into every prompt:

1. Start with [`llms.txt`](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/llms.txt) to select a component from its category and description.
2. Read that component's generated `/ai/components/<Name>.md` specification for the real subpath, explicit prop types, required fields, usage example and accessibility notes. Use `components.json` when structured machine-readable data is needed.
3. Never guess prop names, variants, imports or relationships from another React design system. If a native HTML prop is not explicitly shown, verify against the TypeScript declaration before using it.
4. Compare the **when to use** and **when not to use** sections of nearby alternatives before choosing. Keep text translation and brand themes in the consuming app.
5. Compile/typecheck and test the resulting UI. The static AI docs are guidance, not proof that generated JSX is correct.

The same lookup is available through `lufia-ai` above. Contributors with the repository checked out can run `npm run ai:search -- "task"` and `npm run ai:show -- Button` to retrieve only the relevant manifest data. The JSON flag (`--json`) is intended for agent tooling.

### Rules when you use components

- **Every user-facing string is a prop.** The package has no i18n. Translate in the app and pass the result in.
  Examples in the specs use plain English literals only for brevity.
- **No router inside.** Links render through the `linkComponent` given to `LufiaProvider`.
- **Server Components:** static components carry no `"use client"` and work in a Server Component. Interactive ones start with
  `"use client"`; from a Server Component, pass them only serialisable props (event handlers must come from a client
  component).
- **Style with tokens.** Use `--lufia-*` semantic custom properties in your own CSS. Never copy raw colour values and never
  read the primitive palette.
- **Respect status.** `alpha` and `beta` components may change in a minor release before 1.0. Read the changelog when you
  upgrade.
- **Accessibility is part of the API.** Icon-only controls need an accessible name; use `FormField` to wire a label, hint and error to a control;
  tone and colour never carry meaning alone. Follow the keyboard and accessibility notes in each spec.
- **Motion** follows the rules in `docs/MOTION.md`: only `transform` and `opacity`, never over 300 ms in application UI,
  and everything honours `prefers-reduced-motion`. Use the primitives from `@lufia/design-system/motion` instead of
  writing keyframes, and check your own source with the `lufia-verify-motion` CLI.

### Where things are

| Need                         | Read                                                      |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Index of everything          | `llms.txt` on the documentation site                      |
| Everything in one file       | `llms-full.txt` on the documentation site                 |
| Typed API of every component | `components.json` (props, types, defaults, status)        |
| One component                | `docs/ai/components/<Name>.md`                            |
| Motion rules                 | `docs/MOTION.md`                                          |
| Live examples                | The Storybook site (the link is in the repository README) |

## Motion

The rules for motion in `@lufia/design-system` and in the apps that use it. They are enforced where a machine can enforce
them (`lufia-verify-motion`, below) and reviewed where it cannot. Live demos are in Storybook under **Foundations →
Motion**.

### Principles

1. **Continuity over decoration.** A transition exists to keep the person oriented: where something opened from, where it
   went, what just changed. If it does not do that, leave it out.
2. **Never a blank flash or a jump.** A loading placeholder has the shape of the content that replaces it. Scroll position
   and focus survive. Persistent chrome (headers, sidebars) never re-animates.
3. **Never in the way.** Input is never blocked by an animation, and a second tap mid-animation goes straight to the new
   state. Nothing in application UI is longer than 300 ms, and exits are shorter than entrances.
4. **Only real state changes animate.** Not first paint, not every re-render, not every data refresh. CSS entrance
   animations run when a node is created; script-driven ones compare with the previous value first.
5. **One direction language.** Forward is right or up, back is left or down. Sheets rise from the bottom; dialogs scale
   from the centre.
6. **Compositor-friendly only.** Animate `transform` and `opacity` (also `clip-path` and SVG stroke). Never `width`,
   `height`, `top`, `left`, margins or padding. The approved exception is the `Collapse` primitive. Add `will-change` only
   while an animation runs. Do not animate anything on top of a full-viewport `backdrop-filter`.
7. **Respond on the press, not on the response.** What the person clicked shows as chosen at once; the page follows when
   it arrives.
8. **Reduced motion is respected everywhere**, and motion never carries meaning alone.
9. **Restrained.** Never hijack scroll and never move an interactive control the person is aiming at.

### Tokens

All defined in `tokens/` (DTCG) and built to `--lufia-motion-*` in `tokens.css`.

| Token                                      | Value                            | Use                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `--lufia-motion-duration-instant`          | 120 ms                           | Hover, press, colour changes                        |
| `--lufia-motion-duration-fast`             | 180 ms                           | Small control motion, chevrons                      |
| `--lufia-motion-duration-enter`            | 240 ms                           | Anything entering: dialogs, toasts, steps, page in  |
| `--lufia-motion-duration-exit`             | 160 ms                           | Anything leaving (always shorter than its entrance) |
| `--lufia-motion-duration-medium` / `-slow` | 380 / 640 ms                     | Large surfaces, number counts, marketing reveals    |
| `--lufia-motion-easing-out`                | `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)` | Entrances                                           |
| `--lufia-motion-easing-in`                 | `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1)`     | Exits                                               |
| `--lufia-motion-easing-in-out`             | `cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1)` | Movement between two resting places                 |
| `--lufia-motion-easing-drawer`             | `cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1)` | Large travel such as sheets                         |
| `--lufia-motion-distance-nudge`            | 0.25 rem                         | Small controls and indicators                       |
| `--lufia-motion-distance-rise`             | 0.375 rem                        | Content and page entrances                          |
| `--lufia-motion-distance-slide`            | 0.5 rem                          | List rows and panels                                |
| `--lufia-motion-distance-travel`           | 1 rem                            | Sheets and full-screen surfaces                     |

Write durations and easings as `var(--lufia-motion-*)`. A literal fails `lufia-verify-motion`. Distances are in `rem`.

### Reduced motion

Under `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`, `tokens.css` sets every `--lufia-motion-duration-*` to `0.01ms` and every
`--lufia-motion-distance-*` to `0rem`. So:

- **Token-driven CSS needs no extra work.** The end state is reached at once. The duration is `0.01ms` and not `0` so that
  `transitionend` and `animationend` still fire.
- **Entrances fill `backwards`, never `both` or `forwards`.** A forwards fill keeps the animation's `transform` applied
  after it ends, even as an identity matrix. That makes the element the containing block and a stacking context for any
  `position: fixed` descendant rendered inside it, so a sheet or popover is positioned against the element and not the
  viewport. `backwards` applies the first frame during the delay and nothing afterwards, so the resting state is
  `transform: none`. The one exception is `NavSheet`, which rests on its own drag transform
  (`translateY(var(--lufia-sheet-drag, 0))`); it sits inside a fixed root, so nothing is affected. Exits (`*-out`) may hold their last frame because the element is about to unmount. A test
  (`src/test/animationFill.test.ts`) fails on any entrance that animates `transform` and fills forwards.
- **Keyframes animate `from` only**, so the resting state is the end state and a disabled animation leaves the content
  visible.
- **Endless loops (spinners, shimmer) are stopped, not shortened.** A near-zero endless loop is a strobe. Give them a
  `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` rule (`animation: none`, or hide the moving part). Endless loops are the one
  case where a literal duration is accepted, because they keep their own pace.
- **Script-driven motion** (`requestAnimationFrame`, the Web Animations API) checks `usePrefersReducedMotion()` (or
  `matchMedia`) and renders the final state.
- **Reduced motion means less motion, not less information.** Show the new value; do not hide the change.

### Primitives

| Primitive                 | Use for                                    | Reduced motion               |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------- |
| `Reveal`                  | Content that appears or disappears         | Appears and unmounts at once |
| `Collapse`                | Content that expands to its natural height | Snaps open and closed        |
| `Skeleton`                | Placeholder for content that is loading    | Shimmer stops, shape stays   |
| `AnimatedNumber`          | A figure that changes while visible        | New value at once            |
| `ChangeHighlight`         | Pointing at a value that updated by itself | No flash                     |
| `Stagger`                 | A group that enters on mount, in sequence  | Children are simply there    |
| `RouteTransition`         | The content region when the page changes   | Nothing is marked            |
| `usePrefersReducedMotion` | Anything CSS cannot switch off             | n/a                          |

Import from `@lufia/design-system/motion`. All are `beta`.

The chart components (`Sparkline`, `BarList`, `BulletBar`, `ProgressBar`, `StackedBar`) draw in once on mount with
`--lufia-motion-duration-medium` (380 ms), on `transform` or stroke only. It is a one-time entrance of a drawing, not an
interaction, which is why it is longer than the 300 ms an interactive control may take. It is removed under reduced motion.

### Checklist for a new screen

- [ ] Durations and easings are tokens; no literal times, no `ease`/`cubic-bezier`.
- [ ] Nothing animates a layout property (use `Collapse` for height). No `will-change` at rest.
- [ ] Loading states use skeletons shaped like the real content; layout shift on swap is negligible.
- [ ] Entrances are longer than exits; nothing is longer than 300 ms in application UI.
- [ ] Only real changes animate. First paint does not.
- [ ] Checked with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`: everything still works and nothing is hidden.
- [ ] Checked on a throttled CPU (DevTools 4x slowdown): no dropped frames in transitions.
- [ ] `lufia-verify-motion` passes.

### `lufia-verify-motion`

A command-line check for the rules a machine can verify. It ships in the package (`bin`) and reads your CSS, and the
inline styles and animation calls in your scripts. No dependencies beyond Node 22.

```bash
npx lufia-verify-motion src
```

| Rule             | Flags                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `duration`       | A literal time in `transition` or `animation` (shorthand or longhand). Delays, `1ms` steps and `infinite` loops are exempt.                                                                                                                                               |
| `easing`         | `ease`, `ease-in`, `ease-out`, `ease-in-out` or `cubic-bezier()` in a transition or animation. `linear` and `steps()` are fine.                                                                                                                                           |
| `layout`         | `width`, `height`, `top`, `left`, `inset`, margins, paddings, `font-size`, `grid-template-*`, `all` and similar in `transition` or in `@keyframes`.                                                                                                                       |
| `reduced-motion` | A stylesheet with literal-duration or endless motion and no `prefers-reduced-motion` rule (and no global one in the scan). A script that calls `requestAnimationFrame` or `.animate()` without `usePrefersReducedMotion`, `useReducedMotion` or `prefers-reduced-motion`. |

Token-only, finite CSS motion is accepted without a media query, because the tokens collapse by themselves. A global
kill-switch (a `*` selector that resets `animation` or `transition` inside the reduced-motion query) satisfies the rule
for the whole scan.

Options:

```text
lufia-verify-motion [paths...]
  --baseline <file>      ratchet file (below)
  --init                 create the baseline from today's violations
  --update               rewrite the baseline after fixing violations (refuses to add any)
  --ignore <prefix>      skip paths that start with this prefix (repeatable)
  --token-prefix <p>     extra custom-property prefix that counts as a motion token (repeatable)
```

Tests (`*.test.*`, `*.spec.*`), `.d.ts` files and `node_modules`, `dist`, `build`, `coverage`, `.next` are skipped. Exit code
`0` is ok, `1` is violations, `2` is a usage error.

#### Deliberate exceptions

Put `lufia-motion-allow <rule>` in a comment on the same line or the line above (CSS `/* */`, scripts `//`). It silences that
rule only, for the next declaration. Use it with a reason; `Collapse` is the model:

```css
/* The one place a layout property is animated, on purpose: 0fr to 1fr reaches height: auto. */
/* lufia-motion-allow layout */
transition: grid-template-rows var(--lufia-motion-duration-enter) var(--lufia-motion-easing-in-out);
```

#### Adopting it in an existing codebase: the ratchet

An app with existing violations records them once and from then on may only improve:

```bash
npx lufia-verify-motion src --baseline motion-baseline.json --init     # once
npx lufia-verify-motion src --baseline motion-baseline.json            # in CI
npx lufia-verify-motion src --baseline motion-baseline.json --update   # after fixing some
```

The baseline stores violation counts per file and rule. A count above the baseline fails (all findings of that file and
rule are printed, since the counts cannot tell which one is new); a lower count passes and tells you the baseline can
shrink. `--update` refuses to write anything bigger than what is recorded, and `--init` refuses to overwrite.

#### Limits

It is a static, line-based check, not a CSS parser. It does not follow `var()` values, preprocessor mixins or class
composition, and it does not see animation set through the Web Animations API options. Passing it is necessary, not
sufficient: the checklist above still applies.

# Component specs

## ActionIcons

> A small, consistent set of stroke icons for common row and page actions.

- Status: beta
- Category: Actions
- Import: `import { ACTION_ICONS, DeleteIcon, DuplicateIcon, EditIcon, OpenIcon, PendingIcon, ReportIcon } from "@lufia/design-system/components/ActionIcons"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/ActionIcons](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/ActionIcons)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-actions-actionicons--docs)

### Purpose

Six small outline icons for action menus and row actions: `DeleteIcon`, `EditIcon`, `DuplicateIcon`, `PendingIcon`,
`OpenIcon` and `ReportIcon`. They share a 16x16 grid, a 1.4 stroke and round caps, and inherit `currentColor`.

### When to use

- Beside a visible text label in menus and buttons (decorative).
- As the only content of an icon button, with an accessible name on the button.

### When not to use

- As the only carrier of meaning without a name. If the icon stands alone, give it `aria-label`.

### Exports

| Name | Kind |
| --- | --- |
| `ACTION_ICONS` | constant |
| `DeleteIcon` | component |
| `DuplicateIcon` | component |
| `EditIcon` | component |
| `OpenIcon` | component |
| `PendingIcon` | component |
| `ReportIcon` | component |

### API

#### `DeleteIcon`, `DuplicateIcon`, `EditIcon`, `OpenIcon`, `PendingIcon`, `ReportIcon`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `number` | no |  | Rendered width and height in px. |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `IconProps`: `Omit<SVGProps<SVGSVGElement>, "width" | "height" | "viewBox" | "children"> & { size?: number | undefined; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { DeleteIcon } from "@lufia/design-system/components/ActionIcons";

<button type="button">
  <DeleteIcon /> Delete
</button>;
```

### Accessibility

- **Decorative by default**: `aria-hidden="true"` and `focusable="false"`, so assistive technology skips it.
- **Meaningful on request**: `aria-label` switches to `role="img"` with that name. Prefer labelling the surrounding button instead, so the name is announced once.
- Icons inherit `currentColor`; contrast is the responsibility of the text colour they sit in (3:1 for non-text content).
- Keyboard and focus behaviour belong to the enclosing control.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Its stylesheet reads no `--lufia-*` tokens directly (no CSS module, or it composes other components).

### Content guidelines

Icons carry no text. Localised labels are supplied by the app next to the icon.

### Stories

- `components-actions-actionicons--default`
- `components-actions-actionicons--gallery`
- `components-actions-actionicons--sizes`
- `components-actions-actionicons--meaningful`
- `components-actions-actionicons--all-themes`

## ActivityList

> A feed of what happened with its time, optionally on a timeline rail.

- Status: beta
- Category: Data display
- Import: `import { ActivityList } from "@lufia/design-system/components/ActivityList"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/ActivityList](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/ActivityList)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-data-display-activitylist--docs)

### Purpose

A feed of what happened, newest first: a title, a line of context, the time and an optional action per entry, with an optional timeline rail.

### When to use

- Recent changes to a workspace, a record or an account.
- A feed where each entry is one event with a time.

### When not to use

- Things that need a decision: use `AttentionList`.
- The states of one obligation, with deadlines and inputs: use `StatusTimeline`.
- Long histories: link to a full page or a table.

### API

#### `ActivityList`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `readonly ActivityItem[]` | yes |  |  |
| `timeline` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Draws a rail with a marker per entry, for a feed read as a sequence. Plain rows by default. |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `ActivityItem`: `{ id: string; title: ReactNode; meta?: ReactNode; time: ReactNode; dateTime?: string | undefined; tone?: ActivityTone | undefined; toneLabel?: string | undefined; action?: ReactNode; }`
- `ActivityListProps`: `Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLOListElement>, "children"> & { items: readonly ActivityItem[]; timeline?: boolean | undefined; }`
- `ActivityTone`: `"neutral" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "info"`

### Example

```tsx
import { ActivityList } from "@lufia/design-system/components/ActivityList";

<ActivityList
  aria-label="Recent activity"
  timeline
  items={[
    {
      id: "1",
      title: "Report published",
      meta: "By Ana",
      time: "2 h ago",
      dateTime: "2026-03-12T10:00:00Z",
      tone: "success",
    },
    { id: "2", title: "Export failed", time: "Yesterday", tone: "danger", toneLabel: "Failed" },
  ]}
/>;
```

### Accessibility

- It is an ordered list (`ol`): the order is the meaning. Name it with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
- Pass `dateTime` (ISO 8601) and the time renders as a `<time>` element. `time` itself is already formatted, in your language.
- The rail and markers are decorative (`aria-hidden`); the tone is reinforcement. Set `toneLabel` so a state such as "Failed" is read before the title.
- The rail uses logical properties, so it flips in right-to-left layouts.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-border-width-thick`, `--lufia-border-width-thin`, `--lufia-color-accent-default`, `--lufia-color-bg-surface`, `--lufia-color-border-strong`, `--lufia-color-border-subtle`, `--lufia-color-status-danger-solid`, `--lufia-color-status-success-fg`, `--lufia-color-status-warning-fg`, `--lufia-color-text-default`, `--lufia-color-text-muted`, `--lufia-color-text-subtle`, `--lufia-font-family-mono`, `--lufia-font-line-height-normal`, `--lufia-font-size-sm`, `--lufia-font-size-xs`, `--lufia-radius-full`.

### Stories

- `components-data-display-activitylist--default`
- `components-data-display-activitylist--timeline`
- `components-data-display-activitylist--single-entry`
- `components-data-display-activitylist--long-text`
- `components-data-display-activitylist--empty`
- `components-data-display-activitylist--inside-card`
- `components-data-display-activitylist--phone-320`
- `components-data-display-activitylist--right-to-left`
- `components-data-display-activitylist--all-themes`

## AnimatedNumber

> Counts a number to its new value and respects reduced motion.

- Status: beta
- Category: Motion
- Import: `import { AnimatedNumber } from "@lufia/design-system/motion"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/motion/AnimatedNumber](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/motion/AnimatedNumber)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-motion-animatednumber--docs)

### Purpose

A number that counts to its new value when `value` changes. It uses `requestAnimationFrame`, no animation library.

### When to use

- Headline figures that can change while visible: totals, counters, progress percentages.

### When not to use

- Values that should not look like they are being computed (identifiers, dates, anything people copy exactly).
- Numbers that change many times per second. Show them directly.

### API

#### `AnimatedNumber`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `number` | yes |  |  |
| `format` | `(value: number) => string` | no | `String` | Turns the running number into text. Pass a locale-aware formatter; the default is `String`. |
| `duration` | `number` | no |  | Milliseconds. Defaults to the `--lufia-motion-duration-medium` token, which is ~0 under reduced motion. |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `AnimatedNumberProps`: `Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLSpanElement>, "children"> & { value: number; format?: ((value: number) => string) | undefined; duration?: number | undefined; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { AnimatedNumber } from "@lufia/design-system/motion";

const money = new Intl.NumberFormat(locale, { style: "currency", currency: "EUR" });

<AnimatedNumber value={total} format={(n) => money.format(n)} />;
```

### Accessibility

- It is not a live region. If the change matters to someone using a screen reader, announce it yourself (for example "Total updated to 1,280 euros" in a polite live region), or pair it with [ChangeHighlight](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-motion-changehighlight--docs).
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the new value appears at once; there are never intermediate numbers.
- Formatting and locale are yours: pass a formatter built with the user's locale.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Its stylesheet reads no `--lufia-*` tokens directly (no CSS module, or it composes other components).

### Stories

- `components-motion-animatednumber--default`
- `components-motion-animatednumber--formatted`
- `components-motion-animatednumber--slow`
- `components-motion-animatednumber--all-themes`

## AppShell

> The application frame: sidebar, content area and the phone navigation sheet.

- Status: beta
- Category: Navigation
- Import: `import { APP_SHELL_BREAKPOINT, AppShell, MobileFloatBar, MobileFloatBarButton, MobileFloatBarSeparator, NavSheet, RouteProgress, SHELL_COUNT_CAP, ShellFooter, ShellFooterItem, ShellNavigation, ShellPrimaryActionSlot, Sidebar, SidebarGroup, SidebarItem, findActiveNavKey, formatShellCount, parseShellState, serializeShellState, useSheetDrag, useShellPrimaryAction } from "@lufia/design-system/components/AppShell"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/AppShell](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/AppShell)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-navigation-appshell--docs)

### Purpose

The frame of an application. On wide screens a sidebar with groups that open and close and that can shrink to a rail. On
phones a sticky top bar, a floating bar within thumb reach, and a navigation sheet that rises from the bottom. The
navigation is data, so both layouts always agree.

### When to use

- A signed-in application with a handful of top-level areas, on both phones and desktops.

### When not to use

- A marketing site (use a header), or navigation that is only a few peer views of one page (use `PeerNav`).

### Exports

| Name | Kind |
| --- | --- |
| `APP_SHELL_BREAKPOINT` | constant |
| `AppShell` | component |
| `MobileFloatBar` | component |
| `MobileFloatBarButton` | component |
| `MobileFloatBarSeparator` | component |
| `NavSheet` | component |
| `RouteProgress` | component |
| `SHELL_COUNT_CAP` | constant |
| `ShellFooter` | component |
| `ShellFooterItem` | component |
| `ShellNavigation` | component |
| `ShellPrimaryActionSlot` | component |
| `Sidebar` | component |
| `SidebarGroup` | component |
| `SidebarItem` | component |
| `findActiveNavKey` | function |
| `formatShellCount` | function |
| `parseShellState` | function |
| `serializeShellState` | function |
| `useSheetDrag` | hook |
| `useShellPrimaryAction` | hook |

### API

#### `AppShell`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `groups` | `readonly ShellNavGroup[]` | yes |  | The navigation, as data. It renders in the sidebar and again in the phone sheet. |
| `currentPath` | `string` | no |  | The path being shown: the matching item is current (`aria-current="page"`). |
| `isActive` | `(item: ShellNavItem) => boolean` | no |  | Takes over from `currentPath`. Return true for the current item. |
| `labels` | `AppShellLabels` | yes |  |  |
| `brand` | `Slot` | no |  | Brand or workspace switcher, at the top of the sidebar, the sheet and the phone top bar. A function gets the rail state. |
| `context` | `Slot` | no |  | Between the brand and the search, in the sidebar, and above the navigation in the sheet: the workspace, company or account the person is in, and a switcher for it. A function gets the surface (see `AppShellSlotState`), so a switcher can open as a dropdown in the sidebar and inline in the sheet. Rendered once per surface, so do not give its parts a fixed `id`. |
| `footer` | `Slot` | no |  | Bottom of the sidebar, and of the sheet: account, help and sign-out links. |
| `topBarEnd` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Right side of the phone top bar: a workspace chip, a status. |
| `search` | `AppShellSearch` | no |  | A search entry in the sidebar and on the floating bar. |
| `searchTrigger` | `Slot` | no |  | Replaces the sidebar's search entry with your own (a function gets the rail state). The floating bar's entry still comes from `search`. |
| `primaryAction` | `AppShellPrimaryAction` | no |  | The main action when no page registers its own with `useShellPrimaryAction`: on the floating bar, and in any `ShellPrimaryActionSlot`. |
| `desktopPrimaryFallback` | `boolean` | no | `true` | Whether wide screens show the shell's `primaryAction` in `ShellPrimaryActionSlot` while no page has registered its own. Default `true`. Set `false` when the default makes sense only on phones (the floating bar still shows it), so a hard load never flashes an action the page is about to replace or remove. |
| `menuData` | `FloatBarDataAttributes` | no |  | `data-*` attributes for the floating bar's menu button. |
| `navigationPending` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Shown in place of the navigation, in the sidebar and in the sheet, while the next route loads: a skeleton. The navigation landmarks are `aria-busy` meanwhile. Leave it out when the navigation is ready. |
| `topBar` | `ReactNode` | no |  | A bar above the page, beside the sidebar, at every width: a unit or context picker. |
| `statusRow` | `ReactNode` | no |  | A row between `topBar` and the page: sync state, a notice. Give it the live-region semantics it needs. |
| `sheetAs` | `"portal" \| "dialog"` | no | `"portal"` | `portal` (default) or a native `<dialog>` for the phone navigation sheet (`NavSheet` `renderAs`). |
| `menuOpen` | `boolean` | no |  | The phone navigation sheet is open. Controlled: open it from your own control (a context chip in the top bar) and hear it close through `onMenuOpenChange`. Leave it out and the menu button drives it. |
| `onMenuOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` | no |  |  |
| `hideSheetNavigation` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Hide the navigation inside the phone sheet and leave the `context` slot and footer: a switcher that takes over the sheet while it is open. The sidebar is not affected. |
| `collapsed` | `boolean` | no |  | Sidebar as a rail. Controlled. |
| `defaultCollapsed` | `boolean` | no | `false` |  |
| `onCollapsedChange` | `(collapsed: boolean) => void` | no |  |  |
| `openGroups` | `readonly string[]` | no |  | Keys of the open collapsible groups. Controlled; the owner then also decides what arriving on a page opens. |
| `defaultOpenGroups` | `readonly string[]` | no |  |  |
| `onOpenGroupsChange` | `(keys: readonly string[]) => void` | no |  |  |
| `fixedSidebar` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Hide the rail button. Default `false`. |
| `routeKey` | `string` | no |  | Identifies the page being shown, usually the pathname. When it changes, the page inside `<main>` enters with a short fade and rise (`RouteTransition`), the route progress bar finishes, and the navigation skeleton gives way. A search-param change or a refresh keeps the key and plays nothing; neither does the first load. Nothing remounts for it. Pass the pathname, not the query string. Wrapping the page adds one element around `children`. |
| `routePending` | `boolean` | no |  | A navigation to another route has started and the page is not there yet: drives a thin progress bar at the top of the window. Needs `routeKey`. The bar appears only when the wait outlasts 150 ms, so fast navigations do not flash, and, unless you pass this prop, a plain click on a link to another path starts it by itself. |
| `routeProgress` | `boolean` | no | `true` | Draw the progress bar when `routeKey` is given. Default `true`. |
| `mainPending` | `ReactNode` | no |  | A skeleton shown in `<main>` in place of the page while a slow navigation loads. The page stays mounted but hidden, so its state and the providers around it survive, and `mainStart` stays visible. `<main>` is `aria-busy` meanwhile. Decide when to show it (most apps wait a few hundred milliseconds so fast navigations never flash one) and give it the shape of the page it stands in for. |
| `floatScrim` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Fade the page out behind the floating bar on phones, so content scrolling under it does not end in a hard edge. Default `false`: nothing is drawn unless asked for. |
| `mainProps` | `AppShellMainProps` | no |  | Attributes for the `<main>` the shell owns: `id` (the skip link follows it), `className`, `data-*`, `tabIndex`, ARIA. `className` is added to the shell's own. |
| `mainKey` | `Key` | no |  | Remounts the `<main>` and everything in it when it changes, as React's `key` does: a workspace or scope switch that must drop the page's state. Leave it out for a page change, which `children` handles. |
| `mainStart` | `ReactNode` | no |  | The first thing inside `<main>`, before `children`: banners that belong to the page area and scroll with it (a trial notice, a cookie or install hint). Unlike `topBar` and `statusRow`, which sit beside `<main>` and stay put, this remounts with `mainKey` and takes the page's padding. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | The page. The shell renders the one `<main>` landmark around it. |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

##### Variants

The props are a union of forms; `href` selects the form. Only the props that differ between forms are listed: a prop with the same type and requirement in every form is not repeated.

#### `RouteProgress`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `routeKey` | `string` | yes |  | Identifies the page being shown (the pathname). When it changes, the navigation has arrived and the bar finishes. `AppShell` passes its own `routeKey`. |
| `pending` | `boolean` | no |  | A navigation has started and not arrived. Set it from the router's pending state, or from your own click handler for a programmatic navigation. Going back to `false` without a new `routeKey` (a cancelled navigation) finishes the bar. When you pass it (even as `false`) the app is in charge, and link clicks no longer start the bar by themselves. |
| `trackLinks` | `boolean` | no | `true` | Without `pending`, also start on a plain click on a same-origin link that leads to another path (`<a href>`, which includes a router's links). Not for modified clicks, `target` other than `_self`, downloads, the current path or a link that only changes the query string or hash. A run started this way ends when `location.href` changes, when `routeKey` changes, or after 10 seconds, whichever comes first. Default `true`. |
| `revealDelay` | `number` | no | `ROUTE_PROGRESS_REVEAL_DELAY_MS` | Milliseconds to wait before showing the bar. Default 150. |
| `className` | `string` | no |  |  |

#### `findActiveNavKey`

The key of the item that `currentPath` belongs to, or `undefined`. A path belongs to an item when it is equal to the item's `href` or below it (`/settings/billing` belongs to `/settings`); when several match, the most specific wins, so two items are never current at once. `exact` items match only themselves. Query strings and hashes are ignored.

```ts
findActiveNavKey(groups: readonly ShellNavGroup[], currentPath: string | undefined, isActive?: ((item: ShellNavItem) => boolean) | undefined): string | undefined
```

#### `formatShellCount`

The text of a count badge: `undefined` for nothing to show (not a number, zero or negative), the number itself up to `cap`, and `"99+"` (with the cap) above it.

```ts
formatShellCount(count: number | undefined, cap?: number): string | undefined
```

#### `parseShellState`

Reads what `serializeShellState` wrote, on the server (from the request's cookie) or in the browser, and returns the values to hand to `defaultCollapsed` and `defaultOpenGroups` so the first paint is already right. A missing or malformed value gives the defaults: expanded, groups undecided.

```ts
parseShellState(raw: string | null | undefined): ShellState
```

#### `serializeShellState`

Turns the person's sidebar choices into a short cookie value (`c=1&g=insights&g=admin`), for the app to store. The package never stores anything itself; see "Remembering the rail and the groups" in the docs. Pass `openGroups` as `undefined` to leave the groups to their defaults.

```ts
serializeShellState(state: ShellState): string
```

#### `useSheetDrag`

Swipe-down-to-dismiss for a bottom sheet, on pointer events. Spread the returned handlers on the drag zone only (the grabber and the header), never on the scrolling body: that keeps the list scrollable without any gesture arbitration. The zone needs `touch-action: none` so the browser does not claim the gesture for scrolling or pull-to-refresh. While dragging, the offset is written to the `--lufia-sheet-drag` custom property on the enclosing `[role="dialog"]` (or native `dialog`) and `data-dragging` is set on it; the panel's CSS turns that into a `transform`. A release past the threshold, or a quick flick, calls `onDismiss` (the sheet then slides the rest of the way out); anything shorter springs back. Escape and the close button remain the keyboard route, so the gesture is never the only way out.

```ts
useSheetDrag(onDismiss: () => void, enabled?: boolean): { onPointerDown(event: PointerEvent<HTMLElement>): void; onPointerMove(event: PointerEvent<HTMLElement>): void; onPointerUp(event: PointerEvent<HTMLElement>): void; onPointerCancel(event: PointerEvent<HTMLElement>): void; }
```

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onDismiss` | `() => void` | yes |  |
| `enabled` | `boolean` | no |  |

Returned members:

| Member | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onPointerDown` | `(event: PointerEvent<HTMLElement>) => void` | yes |  |
| `onPointerMove` | `(event: PointerEvent<HTMLElement>) => void` | yes |  |
| `onPointerUp` | `(event: PointerEvent<HTMLElement>) => void` | yes |  |
| `onPointerCancel` | `(event: PointerEvent<HTMLElement>) => void` | yes |  |

#### `useShellPrimaryAction`

Hands the page's one main action to the shell, which shows it on the floating bar (phones) and wherever a `ShellPrimaryActionSlot` sits (wide screens). Pass `null` to register nothing. When several pages are mounted at once the latest registration wins, and the previous one comes back when it unmounts. Returns whether a shell hosts the action. When it does, leave your own trigger out; outside a shell keep it. The shell re-registers when `label` or `href` change; `icon` and `data` are read at that moment, `onSelect` is always the latest.

```ts
useShellPrimaryAction(action: AppShellPrimaryAction | null): boolean
```

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `action` | `AppShellPrimaryAction \| null` | yes |  |

### Types

- `AppShellLabels`: `{ skipToContent: string; navigation: string; menu: string; floatBar: string; collapseSidebar: string; expandSidebar: string; }`
- `AppShellMainProps`: `Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>, "children"> & ShellDataAttributes`
- `AppShellPrimaryAction`: `{ label: string; icon?: ReactNode; href?: string | undefined; onSelect?: (() => void) | undefined; onIntent?: (() => void) | undefined; data?: FloatBarDataAttributes | undefined; }`
- `AppShellSearch`: `{ label: string; onSelect: () => void; shortcut?: string | undefined; keyShortcuts?: string | undefined; opensDialog?: boolean | undefined; data?: FloatBarDataAttributes | undefined; }`
- `AppShellSlotState`: `{ collapsed: boolean; surface: "sidebar" | "sheet" | "topBar"; closeSheet: () => void; openSheet: () => void; }`
- `FloatBarDataAttributes`: `{ [name: 'data-${string}']: string | number | boolean | undefined; }`
- `MobileFloatBarProps`: `Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>, "children"> & { label: string; children: ReactNode; }`
- `RouteProgressProps`: `{ routeKey: string; pending?: boolean | undefined; trackLinks?: boolean | undefined; revealDelay?: number | undefined; className?: string | undefined; }`
- `ShellBadgeTone`: `"neutral" | "warning" | "danger"`
- `ShellDataAttributes`: `{ [name: 'data-${string}']: string | number | boolean | undefined; }`
- `ShellFooterProps`: `Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>, "children"> & { "aria-label": string; children: ReactNode; }`
- `ShellNavGroup`: `{ key: string; label?: string | undefined; icon?: ReactNode; items: readonly ShellNavItem[]; collapsible?: boolean | undefined; defaultOpen?: boolean | undefined; }`
- `ShellState`: `{ collapsed: boolean; openGroups: readonly string[] | undefined; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { AppShell } from "@lufia/design-system/components/AppShell";

<AppShell
  groups={[
    {
      key: "workspace",
      label: "Workspace",
      items: [
        { key: "home", label: "Overview", href: "/", icon: <HomeIcon />, exact: true },
        { key: "inbox", label: "Inbox", href: "/inbox", icon: <InboxIcon />, badge: 3 },
      ],
    },
    {
      key: "insights",
      label: "Insights",
      collapsible: true,
      items: [{ key: "reports", label: "Reports", href: "/insights/reports" }],
    },
  ]}
  currentPath={pathname}
  labels={{
    skipToContent: "Skip to content",
    navigation: "Main navigation",
    menu: "Menu",
    floatBar: "Quick navigation",
    collapseSidebar: "Collapse sidebar",
    expandSidebar: "Expand sidebar",
  }}
  brand={({ collapsed }) => <Logo compact={collapsed} />}
  footer={<AccountLinks />}
  search={{ label: "Search…", shortcut: "Ctrl K", onSelect: openPalette }}
  primaryAction={{ label: "New item", icon: <PlusIcon />, onSelect: createItem }}
>
  <PageContent />
</AppShell>;
```

### Accessibility

Keyboard:

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Everywhere \| Moves through the skip link, the sidebar and the page in order |
| Enter | Link \| Follows it |
| Enter / Space | Button, group head \| Activates it; a group head toggles `aria-expanded` |
| Escape | Sheet \| Closes it; focus returns to the menu button |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Sheet \| Cycle inside the sheet; the page behind is inert |

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-border-width-thick`, `--lufia-border-width-thin`, `--lufia-color-bg-canvas`, `--lufia-color-bg-surface-raised`, `--lufia-color-bg-surface-solid`, `--lufia-color-border-strong`, `--lufia-color-border-subtle`, `--lufia-color-focus-ring`, `--lufia-color-text-default`, `--lufia-color-text-muted`, `--lufia-color-text-subtle`, `--lufia-font-family-mono`, `--lufia-font-size-2xs`, `--lufia-font-size-sm`, `--lufia-radius-control`, `--lufia-radius-xs`, `--lufia-shadow-md`, `--lufia-shell-sidebar-width`, `--lufia-space-1`, `--lufia-space-2`, `--lufia-space-3`, `--lufia-space-4`, `--lufia-space-8`, `--lufia-z-sticky`, `--lufia-z-toast`.

### Content guidelines

Item labels are one or two words. Put the rarely used areas in a collapsible group and the one thing the page is for in
`primaryAction`. The search label is a verb phrase ("Search…").

### Stories

- `components-navigation-appshell--rail`
- `components-navigation-appshell--group-open-on-arrival`
- `components-navigation-appshell--phone`
- `components-navigation-appshell--small-phone`
- `components-navigation-appshell--tablet`
- `components-navigation-appshell--phone-without-primary-action`
