## AttentionList

> A short list of items that need a decision, with a tone bar and an action.

- Status: beta
- Category: Data display
- Import: `import { AttentionList } from "@lufia/design-system/components/AttentionList"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/AttentionList](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/AttentionList)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-data-display-attentionlist--docs)

### Purpose

A short list of things that need a decision: each row has a tone bar, a title, a line of context and one action.

### When to use

- The few items that need action first, at the top of a dashboard.
- Rows where each item has one clear next step.

### When not to use

- A log of what happened: use `ActivityList`.
- Long lists to browse or filter: use a table.
- An empty list: it renders nothing, so use an `EmptyState` or leave the section out.

### API

#### `AttentionList`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `readonly AttentionItem[]` | yes |  |  |
| `barStyle` | `"edge" \| "inset"` | no | `"edge"` | `edge` (default) draws the tone bar as the row's own start border, flush with the card edge. `inset` draws a rounded bar set in from the edge. The bar width is `--lufia-attention-list-bar-width`. |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `AttentionBarStyle`: `"edge" | "inset"`
- `AttentionItem`: `{ id: string; tone?: AttentionTone | undefined; toneLabel?: string | undefined; title: ReactNode; meta?: ReactNode; action?: ReactNode; }`
- `AttentionListProps`: `Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLUListElement>, "children"> & { items: readonly AttentionItem[]; barStyle?: AttentionBarStyle | undefined; }`
- `AttentionTone`: `"danger" | "warning" | "info" | "neutral"`

### Example

```tsx
import { AttentionList } from "@lufia/design-system/components/AttentionList";

<AttentionList
  aria-label="Needs attention"
  items={[
    {
      id: "contract",
      tone: "danger",
      toneLabel: "Overdue",
      title: "Renew the supplier contract",
      meta: "3 days overdue",
      action: (
        <Button size="sm" variant="ghost">
          Open
        </Button>
      ),
    },
  ]}
/>;
```

### Accessibility

- It is a `ul`. Name it with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
- The tone bar and tint are reinforcement. Set `toneLabel` ("Overdue") and it is read before the title, so the urgency never rests on colour.
- The action is your own link or button, so it keeps its own name and focus ring. Name it so it makes sense out of context, or include the subject.
- In `forced-colors` mode the tone bar is a border and stays visible.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-attention-list-bar-inset`, `--lufia-attention-list-bar-inset-block`, `--lufia-attention-list-bar-inset-inline`, `--lufia-attention-list-bar-width`, `--lufia-border-width-thin`, `--lufia-color-accent-default`, `--lufia-color-accent-subtle`, `--lufia-color-border-strong`, `--lufia-color-border-subtle`, `--lufia-color-status-danger-bg`, `--lufia-color-status-danger-solid`, `--lufia-color-status-warning-bg`, `--lufia-color-status-warning-fg`, `--lufia-color-text-default`, `--lufia-color-text-muted`, `--lufia-font-line-height-normal`, `--lufia-font-size-sm`, `--lufia-font-size-xs`, `--lufia-radius-full`.

### Stories

- `components-data-display-attentionlist--default`
- `components-data-display-attentionlist--single-item`
- `components-data-display-attentionlist--no-actions`
- `components-data-display-attentionlist--long-text`
- `components-data-display-attentionlist--inset-bar`
- `components-data-display-attentionlist--inset-per-axis`
- `components-data-display-attentionlist--thick-bar`
- `components-data-display-attentionlist--empty`
- `components-data-display-attentionlist--inside-card`
- `components-data-display-attentionlist--phone-320`
- `components-data-display-attentionlist--right-to-left`
- `components-data-display-attentionlist--all-themes`

## Badge

> A short status or count label in a semantic tone.

- Status: beta
- Category: Data display
- Import: `import { Badge, StatusBadge } from "@lufia/design-system/components/Badge"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/Badge](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/Badge)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-data-display-badge--docs)

### Purpose

A short, non-interactive label for a category, a count or the state of a record. `StatusBadge` is the same component with a
dot on by default.

### When to use

- A status in a table row, a card header or a detail page.
- A count or category next to a heading.

### When not to use

- A message that needs to be read now: use a toast or an alert.
- Anything clickable.
- Long sentences. Past two or three words, write text instead.

### Exports

| Name | Kind |
| --- | --- |
| `Badge` | component |
| `StatusBadge` | component |

### API

#### `Badge`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | The text. Always required: the tone never carries the meaning on its own (WCAG 1.4.1). |
| `tone` | `"neutral" \| "info" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "danger" \| "ai"` | no | `"neutral"` |  |
| `dot` | `boolean` | no | `false` | A small dot before the text, for statuses that read as a state rather than a label. Decorative. |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

#### `StatusBadge`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | The text. Always required: the tone never carries the meaning on its own (WCAG 1.4.1). |
| `tone` | `"neutral" \| "info" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "danger" \| "ai"` | no |  |  |
| `dot` | `boolean` | no | `true` | A small dot before the text, for statuses that read as a state rather than a label. Decorative. |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `BadgeProps`: `Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLSpanElement>, "children"> & { children: ReactNode; tone?: BadgeTone | undefined; dot?: boolean | undefined; }`
- `BadgeTone`: `"neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "ai"`

### Example

```tsx
import { Badge, StatusBadge } from "@lufia/design-system/components/Badge";

<Badge tone="info">In review</Badge>
<StatusBadge tone="danger">Overdue</StatusBadge>
```

### Accessibility

Keyboard:

A badge is not interactive and takes no focus. If it needs to act, use a `Button` or `Link`.

- The text is always present and carries the meaning. The tone and the dot only reinforce it (WCAG 1.4.1), so never omit the text and never reuse one word for two tones.
- The dot is decorative and hidden from assistive technology.
- Every tone's text meets 4.5:1 on its own background in light and dark; the contrast check enforces the status pairs.
- In forced-colors mode the border and dot use system colours, so the shape remains.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-badge-radius`, `--lufia-border-width-thin`, `--lufia-color-accent-border`, `--lufia-color-accent-subtle`, `--lufia-color-border-subtle`, `--lufia-color-status-ai-bg`, `--lufia-color-status-ai-border`, `--lufia-color-status-ai-fg`, `--lufia-color-status-danger-bg`, `--lufia-color-status-danger-border`, `--lufia-color-status-danger-fg`, `--lufia-color-status-neutral-bg`, `--lufia-color-status-neutral-fg`, `--lufia-color-status-success-bg`, `--lufia-color-status-success-border`, `--lufia-color-status-success-fg`, `--lufia-color-status-warning-bg`, `--lufia-color-status-warning-border`, `--lufia-color-status-warning-fg`, `--lufia-color-text-accent`, `--lufia-font-family-body`, `--lufia-font-line-height-normal`, `--lufia-font-size-xs`, `--lufia-font-weight-semibold`, `--lufia-radius-full`.

### Content guidelines

One to three words, sentence case ("In review", not "IN REVIEW"). Say the state, not the colour. Long text wraps instead of
truncating.

### Stories

- `components-data-display-badge--default`
- `components-data-display-badge--with-dot`
- `components-data-display-badge--status`
- `components-data-display-badge--long-text`
- `components-data-display-badge--in-narrow-table-cell`
- `components-data-display-badge--all-tones`
- `components-data-display-badge--all-tones-with-dot`
- `components-data-display-badge--square-by-token`
- `components-data-display-badge--phone-320`
- `components-data-display-badge--all-themes`

## BarList

> Horizontal bars with the name and the value as text, on one shared scale.

- Status: beta
- Category: Data display
- Import: `import { BarList } from "@lufia/design-system/components/BarList"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/BarList](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/BarList)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-data-display-barlist--docs)

### Purpose

Horizontal bars with the name and the value as text above each track. One scale per list: the largest row fills the track.

### When to use

- Comparing a handful of categories by one measure.
- A breakdown that fits a card.

### When not to use

- More than about ten rows: use a table.
- Two measures per row: use a table, or two lists.
- Time series: use `Sparkline`.
- Nothing to show: it renders nothing, so use an `EmptyState`.

### API

#### `BarList`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | Caption of the figure, and its accessible name. |
| `summary` | `ReactNode` | no |  | A written summary of what the bars show. Shown above them. |
| `rows` | `readonly BarListRow[]` | yes |  |  |
| `total` | `{ label: ReactNode; value: ReactNode; }` | no |  | Closes the list with a total line. |
| `reference` | `{ amount: number; label: ReactNode; }` | no |  | A shared reference ("Target 500"), drawn as a dashed tick on every track, on the same scale as the bars. The `label` is printed as a legend under the list and describes the figure, so it should say what the tick means and its value. The reference counts towards the scale, so a reference above every bar still fits. Off by default. |
| `titleVisibility` | `"hidden" \| "visible"` | no | `"visible"` | `"hidden"` keeps the title as the figure's accessible name but removes it from the visual layout (screen readers only), for a list that sits under a heading of its own. Defaults to `"visible"`. |
| `valueWrap` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Lets `value` wrap onto several lines (and break inside a long word) instead of staying on one line, for a value that is text rather than a number ("12 of 40 sites checked", a range of dates). The value column then takes at most half the row and the name keeps the rest. Off by default, so numbers stay on one line. A very long note belongs in `detail`, which always wraps. |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `BarListRow`: `{ key: string; name: ReactNode; note?: ReactNode; value: ReactNode; detail?: ReactNode; amount: number; tone?: ChartTone | undefined; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { BarList } from "@lufia/design-system/components/BarList";

<BarList
  title="Items by region"
  summary="North has the most items."
  rows={[
    { key: "north", name: "North", note: "12 sites", value: "1,240", amount: 1240 },
    { key: "south", name: "South", value: "860", amount: 860, tone: "warning" },
  ]}
  total={{ label: "Total", value: "2,100" }}
/>;
```

### Accessibility

- The text is the data. It is a `figure` named by its `title`, and every name and value is a list item a screen reader reads in order. The bars are `aria-hidden` shape on top, so no separate table is needed.
- Format `value` yourself (it is what people read); the bar is drawn from `amount`.
- `reference` draws a dashed tick on every track, on the same scale as the bars (it counts towards the scale). The tick is shape only: its `label` is printed as a legend under the list and is the figure's accessible description, so write what it means and its value ("Target: 800").
- `titleVisibility="hidden"` keeps the `title` as the figure's accessible name for screen readers only.
- A written `summary` says what the bars show.
- The draw-in is `transform` only and plays once, on mount; it is removed under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- In `forced-colors` mode tracks get a border and fills use `CanvasText`.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has a `prefers-reduced-motion` branch.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-border-width-thin`, `--lufia-color-accent-default`, `--lufia-color-border-subtle`, `--lufia-color-status-danger-solid`, `--lufia-color-status-success-fg`, `--lufia-color-status-warning-fg`, `--lufia-color-text-default`, `--lufia-color-text-muted`, `--lufia-color-text-subtle`, `--lufia-font-family-display`, `--lufia-font-line-height-normal`, `--lufia-font-line-height-tight`, `--lufia-font-size-md`, `--lufia-font-size-sm`, `--lufia-font-size-xs`, `--lufia-font-weight-regular`, `--lufia-font-weight-semibold`, `--lufia-motion-duration-medium`, `--lufia-motion-easing-out`, `--lufia-radius-full`.

### Stories

- `components-data-display-barlist--default`
- `components-data-display-barlist--with-total`
- `components-data-display-barlist--tones`
- `components-data-display-barlist--long-names`
- `components-data-display-barlist--long-values`
- `components-data-display-barlist--long-values-phone-320`
- `components-data-display-barlist--with-reference`
- `components-data-display-barlist--reference-above-every-bar`
- `components-data-display-barlist--reference-long-text`
- `components-data-display-barlist--hidden-title`
- `components-data-display-barlist--all-zero`
- `components-data-display-barlist--empty`
- `components-data-display-barlist--phone-320`
- `components-data-display-barlist--right-to-left`
- `components-data-display-barlist--all-themes`

## BulletBar

> A value as a bar against a target tick, comparable across rows.

- Status: beta
- Category: Data display
- Import: `import { BulletBar } from "@lufia/design-system/components/BulletBar"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/BulletBar](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/BulletBar)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-data-display-bulletbar--docs)

### Purpose

A value as a bar against a target tick. The scale is the target, so the tick sits in the same place on every row and rows compare at a glance.

### When to use

- Progress against a target, repeated on several rows.
- A value that can pass its target.

### When not to use

- A single completion fraction with no target tick: use `ProgressBar`.
- Anything that needs exact values: print them.

### API

#### `BulletBar`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `number` | yes |  |  |
| `target` | `number` | yes |  | Where the tick sits. The scale is the target, so bars of different rows share one "percent of target" axis. |
| `headroom` | `number` | no | `1.25` | Room past the target, as a multiple of it. Defaults to 1.25. |
| `tone` | `"accent" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "danger" \| "neutral"` | no | `"accent"` |  |
| `label` | `string \| null` | yes |  | Accessible name stating the value, the target and what they mean ("Delivered 80 of 100"). Pass `null` to hide the drawing from assistive technology, only when the numbers are printed as text next to it. |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `BulletBarProps`: `Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLSpanElement>, "children" | "role" | "aria-label"> & { value: number; target: number; headroom?: number | undefined; tone?: ChartTone | undefined; label: string | null; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { BulletBar } from "@lufia/design-system/components/BulletBar";

<BulletBar value={80} target={100} label="Delivered 80 of 100" />;
```

### Accessibility

- `label` is required: `role="img"` named by a sentence with the value, the target and what they mean. Pass `null` to hide the bar only when those numbers are printed as text next to it.
- The tick is a dark mark, not a colour: it reads without colour vision.
- The draw-in is `transform` only and plays once, on mount; it is removed under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- In `forced-colors` mode the fill is `Highlight` and the tick `CanvasText`.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has a `prefers-reduced-motion` branch.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-border-width-thin`, `--lufia-color-accent-default`, `--lufia-color-border-subtle`, `--lufia-color-status-danger-solid`, `--lufia-color-status-success-fg`, `--lufia-color-status-warning-fg`, `--lufia-color-text-default`, `--lufia-color-text-subtle`, `--lufia-motion-duration-medium`, `--lufia-motion-easing-out`, `--lufia-radius-full`, `--lufia-radius-xs`.

### Stories

- `components-data-display-bulletbar--default`
- `components-data-display-bulletbar--over-target`
- `components-data-display-bulletbar--far-over-target`
- `components-data-display-bulletbar--empty`
- `components-data-display-bulletbar--no-target`
- `components-data-display-bulletbar--rows`
- `components-data-display-bulletbar--right-to-left`
- `components-data-display-bulletbar--all-themes`

## Button

> The control for an action: a native button, or a link that looks like one.

- Status: beta
- Category: Actions
- Import: `import { Button } from "@lufia/design-system/components/Button"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/Button](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/Button)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-actions-button--docs)

### Purpose

The control for an action. It renders a native `<button>`, or a link when `href` is given, and looks the same either way.

### When to use

- Anything that does something on the page: submit, open a dialog, add, save.
- With `href`, a call to action that navigates and should look like a button.

### When not to use

- Navigation inside text: use `Link`.
- A button with only an icon: use `IconButton`, which requires an accessible name.
- More than one `primary` in the same view.

### API

#### `Button`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `"primary" \| "secondary" \| "ghost" \| "danger"` | no | `"secondary"` | Visual weight. One `primary` per view; `danger` only for destructive actions. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | no | `"md"` |  |
| `loading` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Shows a spinner in place of the content and ignores activation. The button keeps its width, stays focusable and reports `aria-busy`. It is not natively disabled, so keyboard focus is not lost when the work starts. |
| `fullWidth` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Stretches to the full width of its container. |
| `iconStart` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Decorative icon before the label; hidden from assistive technology. |
| `iconEnd` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Decorative icon after the label; hidden from assistive technology. |
| `href` | `string` | no |  | When present the button renders as a link (through the `LufiaProvider` link component). |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLButtonElement> \| Ref<HTMLAnchorElement>` | no |  | Forwarded to the anchor (the link component must forward its `ref`, as plain `<a>` and router links do). |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | no |  | A link cannot be natively disabled; this marks it `aria-disabled` and ignores activation. |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

##### Variants

The props are a union of forms; `href` selects the form. Only the props that differ between forms are listed: a prop with the same type and requirement in every form is not repeated. Native element attributes (event handlers, for instance) are typed for each form's element.

###### `AsButton`

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `form` | `string` | no | Native attribute in this form. |
| `formAction` | `string \| ((formData: FormData) => void \| Promise<void>)` | no | Native attribute in this form. |
| `formEncType` | `string` | no | Native attribute in this form. |
| `formMethod` | `string` | no | Native attribute in this form. |
| `formNoValidate` | `boolean` | no | Native attribute in this form. |
| `formTarget` | `string` | no | Native attribute in this form. |
| `href` | `undefined` | no |  |
| `name` | `string` | no | Native attribute in this form. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLButtonElement>` | no | In every form; only its type differs. |
| `value` | `string \| number \| readonly string[]` | no | Native attribute in this form. |

###### `AsLink`

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `download` | `any` | no | Native attribute in this form. |
| `href` | `string` | yes | When present the button renders as a link (through the `LufiaProvider` link component). |
| `hrefLang` | `string` | no | Native attribute in this form. |
| `media` | `string` | no | Native attribute in this form. |
| `ping` | `string` | no | Native attribute in this form. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLAnchorElement>` | no | Forwarded to the anchor (the link component must forward its `ref`, as plain `<a>` and router links do). In every form; only its type differs. |
| `referrerPolicy` | `"" \| "origin" \| "no-referrer" \| "no-referrer-when-downgrade" \| "origin-when-cross-origin" \| "same-origin" \| "strict-origin" \| "strict-origin-when-cross-origin" \| "unsafe-url"` | no | Native attribute in this form. |
| `target` | `HTMLAttributeAnchorTarget` | no | Native attribute in this form. |

### Types

- `ButtonProps`: `AsButton | AsLink`
- `ButtonSize`: `"sm" | "md" | "lg"`
- `ButtonVariant`: `"primary" | "secondary" | "ghost" | "danger"`

### Example

```tsx
import { Button } from "@lufia/design-system/components/Button";

<Button variant="primary" iconStart={<PlusIcon />} onClick={create}>
  New report
</Button>
<Button href="/reports" iconEnd={<ArrowRightIcon />}>Open reports</Button>
```

### Accessibility

Follows the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices pattern: [Button](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/button/).

Keyboard:

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Moves focus to the button (a disabled one is skipped) |
| Enter / Space | Activates a button; Enter activates a link |

- Native elements, so role, focus and activation come from the browser.
- Focus shows a 2px ring with an offset in every variant. In forced-colors mode the border uses `ButtonText`.
- Icons are decorative and hidden; the label is the accessible name.
- Targets are at least 2rem tall (`sm`), and 2.75rem on coarse pointers.
- A link used as a button is marked `aria-disabled` when disabled or loading, and its activation is cancelled.
- The spinner is a rotation only and stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`; `aria-busy` and the cursor still say it is busy.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has a `prefers-reduced-motion` branch.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-border-width-thick`, `--lufia-border-width-thin`, `--lufia-color-accent-default`, `--lufia-color-accent-hover`, `--lufia-color-accent-subtle`, `--lufia-color-bg-field`, `--lufia-color-bg-surface-raised`, `--lufia-color-border-strong`, `--lufia-color-focus-ring`, `--lufia-color-status-danger-on-solid`, `--lufia-color-status-danger-solid`, `--lufia-color-text-default`, `--lufia-color-text-on-accent`, `--lufia-font-family-body`, `--lufia-font-line-height-tight`, `--lufia-font-size-md`, `--lufia-font-size-sm`, `--lufia-font-size-xs`, `--lufia-font-weight-semibold`, `--lufia-motion-duration-fast`, `--lufia-motion-duration-instant`, `--lufia-motion-duration-slow`, `--lufia-motion-easing-out`, `--lufia-opacity-disabled`, `--lufia-radius-control`, `--lufia-radius-full`, `--lufia-radius-sm`.

### Content guidelines

Start with a verb ("Save changes", "Delete record"). Keep it to one to three words; longer labels wrap instead of
truncating. Give the destructive action a specific name rather than "Yes".

### Stories

- `components-actions-button--default`
- `components-actions-button--primary`
- `components-actions-button--ghost`
- `components-actions-button--danger`
- `components-actions-button--disabled`
- `components-actions-button--loading`
- `components-actions-button--with-icons`
- `components-actions-button--icon-end`
- `components-actions-button--full-width`
- `components-actions-button--as-link`
- `components-actions-button--long-label`
- `components-actions-button--all-variants-and-sizes`
- `components-actions-button--phone-320`
- `components-actions-button--right-to-left`
- `components-actions-button--all-themes`

## Card

> A bordered surface that groups related content, optionally interactive.

- Status: beta
- Category: Data display
- Import: `import { Card } from "@lufia/design-system/components/Card"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/Card](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/Card)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-data-display-card--docs)

### Purpose

A surface that groups related content, with an optional title, header action, body and footer. With `href` the whole card
is clickable through one link.

### When to use

- A self-contained unit: a record, a report, a summary, a setting group.
- An interactive card for a list of destinations where each item has a title and a bit of context.

### When not to use

- Content people need to select or copy: use a plain `Card`.
- Page layout or grouping that has no visual boundary: use spacing.
- A card with several equal destinations inside: link them separately, and leave the card plain.
- A card whose only content is a button: use `Button`.

### API

#### `Card`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Heading of the card. With `href` it is also the text of the card's single link. |
| `headingLevel` | `2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6` | no | `3` | Heading level of `title` (2 to 6). Pick the one that fits the page outline. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` | no |  | One short line under the `title` (or on its own, when there is no title). |
| `headerAction` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Control or badge at the end of the header row. Not available together with `href` unless it is non-interactive. |
| `footer` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Pinned to the bottom of the card, separated from the body. |
| `href` | `string` | no |  | Makes the whole card clickable through one link: the `title` renders as a link whose hit area is stretched over the card. Needs a `title`, which is the link's accessible name. |
| `padding` | `"none" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | no | `"md"` | Inner spacing of every slot. Defaults to `md`. |
| `flush` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Lets the body span the full width of the card while the header and footer keep their padding. For lists and tables that draw their own row padding and dividers. |
| `divider` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Draws a rule under the header, between it and the body. Its colour is `--lufia-card-divider-color`. |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `CardPadding`: `"none" | "sm" | "md" | "lg"`

### Example

```tsx
import { Card } from "@lufia/design-system/components/Card";

<Card title="Quarterly report" headerAction={<Badge tone="info">New</Badge>} footer={<Button size="sm">Download</Button>}>
  Totals for the period.
</Card>

<Card title="Quarterly report" href="/reports/q3">Totals for the period.</Card>
```

### Accessibility

Keyboard:

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Interactive card: focuses the link. Then any control in footer |
| Enter | Follows the link |

- `title` renders as a heading (`headingLevel`, default 3). Choose the level that keeps the page outline in order.
- In the interactive variant, put nothing interactive in `headerAction` and `footer` that duplicates the link's destination.
- Contrast of text on the surface is checked in every theme. The border and focus ring use semantic tokens; in forced-colors mode the border is `CanvasText` and the ring `Highlight`.
- Hover only adds an accent border and shadow; nothing is revealed on hover alone.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-border-width-thick`, `--lufia-border-width-thin`, `--lufia-card-body-padding`, `--lufia-card-body-padding-block`, `--lufia-card-body-padding-inline`, `--lufia-card-divider-color`, `--lufia-card-header-padding`, `--lufia-card-shadow`, `--lufia-card-shadow-hover`, `--lufia-color-accent-border`, `--lufia-color-bg-surface`, `--lufia-color-border-subtle`, `--lufia-color-focus-ring`, `--lufia-color-text-default`, `--lufia-color-text-muted`, `--lufia-font-family-display`, `--lufia-font-line-height-normal`, `--lufia-font-line-height-tight`, `--lufia-font-size-md`, `--lufia-font-size-sm`, `--lufia-font-weight-semibold`, `--lufia-motion-duration-fast`, `--lufia-motion-easing-out`, `--lufia-radius-card`, `--lufia-shadow-md`, `--lufia-shadow-sm`.

### Content guidelines

A title says what the card is ("Quarterly report"). The body is one to three short lines. Do not repeat the title in the
body.

### Stories

- `components-data-display-card--default`
- `components-data-display-card--with-header-action`
- `components-data-display-card--with-footer`
- `components-data-display-card--with-description`
- `components-data-display-card--flush`
- `components-data-display-card--divider`
- `components-data-display-card--themed-by-tokens`
- `components-data-display-card--body-only`
- `components-data-display-card--interactive`
- `components-data-display-card--interactive-with-footer-button`
- `components-data-display-card--interactive-with-body-controls`
- `components-data-display-card--padding-none`
- `components-data-display-card--padding-small`
- `components-data-display-card--padding-large`
- `components-data-display-card--long-text`
- `components-data-display-card--phone-320`
- `components-data-display-card--right-to-left`
- `components-data-display-card--all-themes`

## ChangeHighlight

> Briefly highlights content that changed, so the change is noticed.

- Status: beta
- Category: Motion
- Import: `import { ChangeHighlight } from "@lufia/design-system/motion"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/motion/ChangeHighlight](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/motion/ChangeHighlight)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-motion-changehighlight--docs)

### Purpose

Flashes a soft background behind its children when `value` changes while they are on screen. Never on mount.

### When to use

- A value that updates by itself (polling, live data, a result of another action) and the person should notice where.

### When not to use

- Values the person just typed or chose: they already know.
- Whole rows or tables that refresh together. Highlight the cell that changed.

### API

#### `ChangeHighlight`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string \| number \| boolean \| null` | yes |  | Anything comparable. The highlight plays when this changes between renders, never on mount. |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `ChangeHighlightProps`: `HTMLAttributes<HTMLSpanElement> & { value: string | number | boolean | null | undefined; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { ChangeHighlight } from "@lufia/design-system/motion";

<ChangeHighlight value={order.status}>
  <Badge>{order.statusLabel}</Badge>
</ChangeHighlight>;
```

### Accessibility

- Decoration only. It is not announced and carries no meaning by itself: if the change matters, make it readable in text, or announce it in a polite live region.
- It does not play under `prefers-reduced-motion`, and is removed in `forced-colors` mode.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has a `prefers-reduced-motion` branch.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-color-accent-subtle`, `--lufia-motion-duration-slow`, `--lufia-motion-easing-out`, `--lufia-radius-xs`.

### Stories

- `components-motion-changehighlight--default`
- `components-motion-changehighlight--all-themes`

## ChartKit

> Colour of a chart mark. The tone only reinforces: the value is always printed as text next to the drawing, so a tone is never the only carrier of meaning (WCAG 1.4.1).

- Status: beta
- Category: Utilities
- Import: `import type { ChartTone } from "@lufia/design-system/components/ChartKit"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/ChartKit](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/ChartKit)

### Purpose

Colour of a chart mark. The tone only reinforces: the value is always printed as text next to the drawing, so a tone is never the only carrier of meaning (WCAG 1.4.1).

### When to use

- See the Storybook page.

### When not to use

- See the Storybook page.

### API

No runtime exports with props or parameters.

### Types

- `ChartTone`: `"accent" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "neutral"`

### Accessibility

No accessibility notes are written for this export yet; see the Storybook page.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Its stylesheet reads no `--lufia-*` tokens directly (no CSS module, or it composes other components).

## Checkbox

> A checkbox with a mixed state, for independent on/off choices.

- Status: beta
- Category: Forms
- Import: `import { Checkbox } from "@lufia/design-system/components/Checkbox"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/Checkbox](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/Checkbox)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-forms-checkbox--docs)

### Purpose

A native checkbox with a drawn box, a label that is part of the click target, an optional hint and error, and the mixed
(indeterminate) state.

### When to use

- Independent yes/no choices, and consent that is submitted with a form.
- A list where several items can be chosen at once.

### When not to use

- A setting that applies the moment it is flipped: use `Switch`.
- One choice from several: use `RadioGroup`.
- A group of checkboxes needs a group name: wrap them in a `<fieldset>` with a `<legend>`; `FormField` is for single controls.

### API

#### `Checkbox`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | The visible label, to the side of the box. Required: a checkbox without text is not understandable. |
| `hint` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Help under the label, linked with `aria-describedby`. |
| `error` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Error under the label. Marks the checkbox `aria-invalid`. |
| `indeterminate` | `boolean` | no | `false` | The mixed state of a parent whose children are partly checked. It is a display state: the native `checked` stays what it was, and the person's click sets it to a plain checked or unchecked value, so the next render should clear this prop. |
| `className` | `string` | no |  | Goes on the root element. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLInputElement>` | no |  |  |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `CheckboxProps`: `Omit<InputHTMLAttributes<HTMLInputElement>, "className" | "type" | "size"> & { label: ReactNode; hint?: ReactNode; error?: ReactNode; indeterminate?: boolean | undefined; className?: string | undefined; ref?: Ref<HTMLInputElement> | undefined; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { Checkbox } from "@lufia/design-system/components/Checkbox";

<Checkbox name="terms" label="I accept the terms of service" required error={errors.terms} />;
```

### Accessibility

Follows the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices pattern: [Checkbox](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/checkbox/).

- The label is a real `<label for>`, so the accessible name is the label text. The row is at least 44px tall.
- A mixed box exposes `aria-checked="mixed"` through the native `indeterminate` property.
- Hint and error are in the accessible description; the error has `role="alert"` and the input `aria-invalid`.
- Under `forced-colors` the checked box uses `Highlight` and its mark `HighlightText`.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-border-width-thick`, `--lufia-color-accent-default`, `--lufia-color-bg-field`, `--lufia-color-border-strong`, `--lufia-color-focus-ring`, `--lufia-color-status-danger-fg`, `--lufia-color-text-default`, `--lufia-color-text-muted`, `--lufia-color-text-on-accent`, `--lufia-font-line-height-normal`, `--lufia-font-size-md`, `--lufia-motion-duration-instant`, `--lufia-motion-easing-out`, `--lufia-opacity-disabled`, `--lufia-radius-xs`, `--lufia-space-1`, `--lufia-space-3`.

### Content guidelines

Write the label as the statement that is true when the box is checked ("Send me the weekly report"), never as a question or
a negative ("Don't send..."). Put the long legal text in the hint or a link next to the control, not in the label.

### Stories

- `components-forms-checkbox--default`
- `components-forms-checkbox--checked`
- `components-forms-checkbox--indeterminate`
- `components-forms-checkbox--with-hint`
- `components-forms-checkbox--required`
- `components-forms-checkbox--invalid`
- `components-forms-checkbox--disabled`
- `components-forms-checkbox--disabled-checked`
- `components-forms-checkbox--select-all`
- `components-forms-checkbox--long-text`
- `components-forms-checkbox--phone-320`
- `components-forms-checkbox--right-to-left`
- `components-forms-checkbox--all-themes`

## Collapse

> Animates the height of content that opens and closes.

- Status: beta
- Category: Motion
- Import: `import { Collapse } from "@lufia/design-system/motion"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/motion/Collapse](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/motion/Collapse)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-motion-collapse--docs)

### Purpose

Expands and collapses content to its natural height. It is the one place the package animates a layout property, and it
does so without measuring anything in JavaScript (`grid-template-rows` from `0fr` to `1fr`).

### When to use

- Disclosures, accordions, "show more" areas, inline filter panels.

### When not to use

- Do not animate `height` or `max-height` yourself for the same purpose. `verify-motion` flags it, and `Collapse` is the approved route.
- Content that should leave the page entirely: use [Reveal](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-motion-reveal--docs).

### API

#### `Collapse`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` | `boolean` | yes |  | Whether the content is expanded. |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `CollapseProps`: `HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement> & { open: boolean; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { Collapse } from "@lufia/design-system/motion";

<button type="button" aria-expanded={open} aria-controls="shipping" onClick={() => setOpen(!open)}>
  Shipping details
</button>
<Collapse id="shipping" open={open}>
  Orders ship within two working days.
</Collapse>;
```

### Accessibility

- The trigger is yours. It must be a button with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` pointing at the `id` you pass.
- While closed the content is `inert` and `visibility: hidden`: it cannot receive focus and is not read by screen readers, but it is still in the server-rendered HTML.
- Opening and closing are instant under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- The inner wrapper clips overflow while animating and when open; leave room for focus rings of controls at its edge.
- Browsers without `grid-template-rows` transitions (older than 2023) still work: the panel snaps open and closed.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has a `prefers-reduced-motion` branch.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-motion-duration-enter`, `--lufia-motion-duration-exit`, `--lufia-motion-easing-in-out`.

### Stories

- `components-motion-collapse--closed`
- `components-motion-collapse--open`
- `components-motion-collapse--long-content`
- `components-motion-collapse--all-themes`

## ColumnChart

> Columns on one baseline, single or stacked, with the numbers in a hidden data table.

- Status: beta
- Category: Data display
- Import: `import { ColumnChart } from "@lufia/design-system/components/ColumnChart"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/ColumnChart](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/ColumnChart)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-data-display-columnchart--docs)

### Purpose

Columns on one zero baseline, for a weekly strip or a stack of measures per period. One scale for the whole chart, so columns compare.

### When to use

- Hovering or tapping a column should explain it (a holiday, an outlier): `interactive` with `detail`.
- A short run of periods (a week, up to about twelve months) compared on one measure, or split into a few parts.

### When not to use

- Categories with long names or exact values: use `BarList`.
- A trend inside a sentence or a tile: use `Sparkline`.
- Many periods, negative values or several axes: use a chart library or a table.
- Nothing to show: it renders nothing, so use an `EmptyState`.

### API

#### `ColumnChart`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | Caption of the figure, and its accessible name. |
| `titleVisibility` | `"hidden" \| "visible"` | no | `"visible"` | `"hidden"` keeps the title as the accessible name for screen readers only. Defaults to `"visible"`. |
| `summary` | `ReactNode` | no |  | A written summary of what the columns show. Shown above them. |
| `series` | `readonly ColumnChartSeries[]` | yes |  | The measures. One series draws plain columns; several stack in this order, the first at the bottom. |
| `columns` | `readonly ColumnChartColumn[]` | yes |  | One column per entry, left to right (right to left in an RTL page). |
| `formatValue` | `(value: number) => string` | no | `String` | How a number is written in the data table ("12 h", "1,240"). Defaults to `String`. Format with your locale here. |
| `legend` | `"hidden" \| "auto"` | no | `"auto"` | The legend of a stacked chart. `"auto"` (default) shows it when there is more than one series. |
| `interactive` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Makes every column a focusable element named "<column label>: <values> · <detail>" that shows a tooltip on hover, focus and tap. Escape dismisses the tooltip. Off by default: the chart is then static and needs no client code. |
| `printValues` | `boolean \| "auto"` | no | `false` | Prints the formatted total above each column. `"auto"` prints it when there are 6 columns or fewer, so a long strip does not crowd; `true` always and `false` (default) never. The numbers repeat the data table, so they are hidden from assistive technology. |
| `bandLabel` | `string` | no | `"Range"` | Names the range row of the data table and the range in the tooltip, when a column has a `band`. Aria and tooltip text, so it has an English default. Defaults to `"Range"`. |
| `columnLabel` | `string` | no | `"column"` | What a screen reader calls each column when `interactive` is set (`aria-roledescription`), so it is announced as a "column", not as an image, which tells people the arrow keys move between columns. Aria-only text, so it has an English default. Defaults to `"column"`. |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `ColumnChartColumn`: `{ key: string; label: ReactNode; values: readonly number[]; detail?: string | undefined; band?: { low: number; high: number; } | undefined; }`
- `ColumnChartSeries`: `{ key: string; label: string; tone?: ChartTone | undefined; pattern?: "hatch" | undefined; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { ColumnChart } from "@lufia/design-system/components/ColumnChart";

// A weekly strip: one series
<ColumnChart
  title="Deliveries this week"
  series={[{ key: "done", label: "Deliveries" }]}
  columns={[
    { key: "mon", label: "Mon", values: [4] },
    { key: "tue", label: "Tue", values: [8] },
  ]}
/>

// Stacked columns: one number per series, the first series at the bottom
<ColumnChart
  title="Orders by delivery state"
  series={[
    { key: "ok", label: "On time", tone: "success" },
    { key: "late", label: "Late", tone: "danger" },
  ]}
  columns={[{ key: "w1", label: "Week 1", values: [6, 2] }]}
  formatValue={(value) => value.toLocaleString("en")}
/>;
```

### Accessibility

Keyboard:

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | Enters the columns at the last one focused (the first at first), and leaves them on the next press |
| `Arrow Right` / `Arrow Left` | Next or previous column and shows its tooltip (swapped in right-to-left) |
| `Home` / `End` | First or last column |
| `Escape` | Dismisses the tooltip; focus stays on the column |

- The data is a table. A visually hidden `table`, named by the `title`, lists every series as a row and every column label as a heading, so a screen reader reads the numbers; the drawing is `aria-hidden` shape on top of it, except when `interactive` is set, where the columns are exposed as named images. Write the numbers with `formatValue`.
- The `figure` is named by its `title`; `titleVisibility="hidden"` keeps that name for screen readers only. A written `summary` says what the columns show.
- Series are named in a visible legend (shown when there are several) and in the table, so colour never carries the meaning alone. Stacked segments are also separated by a hairline.
- The draw-in is `transform` only, plays once on mount and is removed under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Columns shrink to fit and their labels wrap, down to 320px. In `forced-colors` mode, where tones collapse to one colour, each series gets its own fill pattern (solid, diagonal stripes, dots, vertical stripes, horizontal stripes, repeating after five) in the columns and in the legend, so the legend stays matchable.
- Negative and non-finite numbers are drawn as 0, but the table shows them as given (through `formatValue`), so bad data is visible rather than hidden.
- Print the figures people need as text beside the chart: the drawing has no value labels, unless you set `printValues`.
- `interactive`: each column is a focusable `role="img"` named `<column label>: <values> · <detail>` and announced as a "column" (`aria-roledescription`, set with `columnLabel`, so people know the arrow keys move between columns) (a series is named when there are several; a `band` adds "`bandLabel` low – high"). The tooltip repeats that text visually, so it is hidden from assistive technology and there is no `aria-describedby`; the detail would be read twice. It follows the WCAG 1.4.13 conditions: Escape dismisses it (and stops there, so a dialog around the chart stays open), the pointer can move onto it, and it stays until the pointer or focus leaves. It is at most two thirds of the plot wide and anchored to the plot edge on the outer thirds, so it does not overflow, down to 320px. It fades in on `opacity`, and not at all under `prefers-reduced-motion`. A column label that is not text names the column from the label element and its values.
- `printValues`: the printed totals repeat the data table, so they are hidden from assistive technology.
- `band`: counted in the scale maximum and listed in the data table, under `bandLabel` (an English default, as it is aria text; set it in your language). It is drawn as a stem with two caps; in `forced-colors` mode it uses `CanvasText`.
- `pattern="hatch"`: diagonal stripes in the card colour over the series colour, in the columns and in the legend. In `forced-colors` mode every series already has its own fill pattern, which replaces the hatch.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has a `prefers-reduced-motion` branch.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-border-width-thick`, `--lufia-border-width-thin`, `--lufia-color-accent-default`, `--lufia-color-bg-surface`, `--lufia-color-bg-surface-raised`, `--lufia-color-border-subtle`, `--lufia-color-focus-ring`, `--lufia-color-status-danger-solid`, `--lufia-color-status-success-fg`, `--lufia-color-status-warning-fg`, `--lufia-color-text-default`, `--lufia-color-text-muted`, `--lufia-color-text-subtle`, `--lufia-column-chart-plot-height`, `--lufia-font-family-display`, `--lufia-font-line-height-normal`, `--lufia-font-line-height-tight`, `--lufia-font-size-2xs`, `--lufia-font-size-md`, `--lufia-font-size-sm`, `--lufia-font-size-xs`, `--lufia-font-weight-semibold`, `--lufia-motion-duration-instant`, `--lufia-motion-duration-medium`, `--lufia-motion-easing-out`, `--lufia-radius-md`, `--lufia-radius-sm`, `--lufia-shadow-md`, `--lufia-z-dropdown`.

### Stories

- `components-data-display-columnchart--weekly-strip`
- `components-data-display-columnchart--stacked`
- `components-data-display-columnchart--formatted-values`
- `components-data-display-columnchart--hidden-legend`
- `components-data-display-columnchart--hidden-title`
- `components-data-display-columnchart--tones`
- `components-data-display-columnchart--zero-columns`
- `components-data-display-columnchart--single-column`
- `components-data-display-columnchart--twelve-columns`
- `components-data-display-columnchart--long-portuguese-text`
- `components-data-display-columnchart--interactive`
- `components-data-display-columnchart--interactive-stacked`
- `components-data-display-columnchart--interactive-long-portuguese-text`
- `components-data-display-columnchart--interactive-phone-320`
- `components-data-display-columnchart--interactive-right-to-left`
- `components-data-display-columnchart--printed-values`
- `components-data-display-columnchart--printed-values-auto`
- `components-data-display-columnchart--printed-values-stacked`
- `components-data-display-columnchart--with-band`
- `components-data-display-columnchart--hatched-series`
- `components-data-display-columnchart--everything-on`
- `components-data-display-columnchart--phone-320`
