## Combobox

> A searchable single-select dropdown input with async options, following the APG combobox pattern.

- Status: beta
- Category: Forms
- Import: `import { Combobox } from "@lufia/design-system/components/Combobox"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/Combobox](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/Combobox)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-forms-combobox--docs)

### Purpose

A searchable single select. The person types to narrow a list and picks one option. Options can arrive asynchronously, and
the empty and loading states are part of the component.

### When to use

- A list too long to scan (more than about fifteen options), or one where people know what they are looking for.
- Data that is loaded as the person types.

### When not to use

- A short list: use `Select` (native, with the platform's picker on phones) or `RadioGroup`.
- A plain text field: use `TextInput`. Without `freeText` the box only accepts a listed option.
- Several choices at once: this is a single select.
- A search that opens a results page: use `SearchInput`.

### API

#### `Combobox`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | no |  | Submitted with the form as `name=value` (empty when nothing is chosen). The visible text is not submitted. |
| `options` | `readonly ComboboxOption[]` | yes |  | The options to offer. For async data, replace them as results arrive and set `filter={false}`. |
| `value` | `string \| null` | no |  | Chosen option value, or `null` for none. Controlled. |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| null` | no | `null` | Initial value when `value` is not given. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string \| null, option: ComboboxOption \| null) => void` | no |  |  |
| `onQueryChange` | `(query: string) => void` | no |  | Called on every keystroke with the typed text, and with `""` once the box is cleared. Use it to load options. |
| `filter` | `false \| ((option: ComboboxOption, query: string) => boolean)` | no |  | How typed text narrows the list. Default: the label contains the text, ignoring case and diacritics. Pass a function to match your own way, or `false` to show `options` as given (the server already filtered them). |
| `loading` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Options are being loaded. Shows a ring and `loadingLabel`, and sets `aria-busy`. |
| `loadingLabel` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | Shown, and announced, while `loading`. |
| `emptyLabel` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | Shown, and announced, when nothing matches. |
| `resultsLabel` | `(count: number) => string` | no |  | Announced when the list changes ("3 results"). Optional; the empty and loading texts are always announced. |
| `valueLabel` | `string` | no |  | Label of the chosen option when it is not in `options` (a value set before the options loaded). |
| `freeText` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Lets the person submit text that is not an option. The value then is the typed text, trimmed (`null` when empty, also for whitespace only) and `onValueChange` reports it with `null` as the option; it follows every keystroke, so a button that waits on the value does not stay stuck. Enter, Tab, Escape, the toggle button and blur settle the text. Enter with nothing highlighted keeps the text, closes the list and does not submit the form, and the first match is not highlighted on its own. Typed text never resolves to an option, even when it equals an option's `value`, and it wins over `valueLabel`. Choosing an option sets that option's `value`; a `value` set by the parent resolves to its option. |
| `clearable` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Shows a clear button while something is chosen. Escape clears too, when the list is closed. |
| `clearLabel` | `string` | no | `"Clear"` | Accessible name of the clear button. Aria-only. |
| `toggleLabel` | `string` | no | `"Show options"` | Accessible name of the button that opens the list. Aria-only. |
| `requiredMessage` | `string` | no |  | Message the browser shows when a `required` combobox is submitted with nothing chosen. Defaults to the browser's own "please fill out this field" in the person's language. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | no |  | Marks the control invalid without a `FormField`. |
| `className` | `string` | no |  | Goes on the root element. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLInputElement>` | no |  |  |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `ComboboxOption`: `{ value: string; label: string; description?: string | undefined; disabled?: boolean | undefined; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { FormField } from "@lufia/design-system/components/FormField";
import { Combobox } from "@lufia/design-system/components/Combobox";

<FormField label="City" error={errors.city}>
  <Combobox
    name="city"
    options={cities}
    placeholder="Search for a city"
    emptyLabel="No city matches that search."
    loadingLabel="Loading cities…"
    onValueChange={(value) => setCity(value)}
  />
</FormField>;
```

### Accessibility

Follows the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices pattern: [Combobox](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/).

- Option ids come from their `value` and do not change between renders, so assistive technology keeps its place when the list updates.
- A visually hidden status region announces the empty and loading texts, and the result count when you pass `resultsLabel`.
- A list that is empty or loading is not "expanded": there is nothing to point `aria-controls` at, so the message lives in the status region only.
- The highlighted option is shown with a fill and a bar on its start edge, and in forced-colors with the system highlight.
- A `required` combobox is invalid until an option is chosen, whatever text is typed: the browser refuses to submit, focuses the box and shows its own message (or `requiredMessage`). It also carries `aria-required`.
- A form `reset` returns it to `defaultValue`.
- It opens upward when there is little room below the box. Room is measured against the viewport and every ancestor that clips vertically (a scrollable dialog body, a table cell), taking the room they all leave, and the list is shortened to the room that is left (never under about six rem). The measure is repeated, once per frame, while the page or any container scrolls and when the window is resized; scrolling does not close the list. The list is placed inside the field and is not portaled, so a clipping parent still bounds it. A portaled list is planned as a follow-up.
- Given an `id`, the input keeps it, the list is `<id>-listbox` and each option is `<id>-option-<encoded value>`: any character of the value outside `A-Za-z0-9-` is written as `_<hex code point>_`.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-border-width-thick`, `--lufia-border-width-thin`, `--lufia-color-accent-default`, `--lufia-color-accent-subtle`, `--lufia-color-bg-surface-raised`, `--lufia-color-bg-surface-solid`, `--lufia-color-border-strong`, `--lufia-color-focus-ring`, `--lufia-color-text-accent`, `--lufia-color-text-default`, `--lufia-color-text-muted`, `--lufia-font-line-height-tight`, `--lufia-font-size-md`, `--lufia-font-size-sm`, `--lufia-font-size-xs`, `--lufia-font-weight-semibold`, `--lufia-motion-distance-nudge`, `--lufia-motion-duration-fast`, `--lufia-motion-duration-instant`, `--lufia-motion-easing-out`, `--lufia-opacity-disabled`, `--lufia-radius-control`, `--lufia-radius-full`, `--lufia-radius-md`, `--lufia-shadow-md`, `--lufia-space-1`, `--lufia-space-2`, `--lufia-space-3`, `--lufia-space-4`, `--lufia-z-dropdown`.

### Content guidelines

Labels are the thing being chosen ("City", "Assignee"), the placeholder says how ("Search for a city"). The empty text says
what to do next ("No city matches that search. Try another name."), and the loading text names what loads. Keep option labels
short and put the secondary detail (country, e-mail, code) in the description. Do not include the description in what must be
unique to tell options apart.

### Stories

- `components-forms-combobox--default`
- `components-forms-combobox--open`
- `components-forms-combobox--with-value`
- `components-forms-combobox--with-hint`
- `components-forms-combobox--required`
- `components-forms-combobox--invalid`
- `components-forms-combobox--disabled`
- `components-forms-combobox--read-only`
- `components-forms-combobox--clearable`
- `components-forms-combobox--free-text`
- `components-forms-combobox--empty`
- `components-forms-combobox--loading`
- `components-forms-combobox--async-options`
- `components-forms-combobox--long-options`
- `components-forms-combobox--many-options`
- `components-forms-combobox--inside-dialog`
- `components-forms-combobox--inside-clipping-box`
- `components-forms-combobox--phone-320`
- `components-forms-combobox--right-to-left`
- `components-forms-combobox--all-themes`

## CommandPalette

> A keyboard-first launcher that filters commands and pages.

- Status: beta
- Category: Overlays
- Import: `import { CommandPalette, filterCommands } from "@lufia/design-system/components/CommandPalette"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/CommandPalette](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/CommandPalette)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-overlays-commandpalette--docs)

### Purpose

A search-and-run overlay opened with Ctrl+K or Cmd+K: type to filter navigation targets and actions, choose with the
arrow keys, run with Enter.

### When to use

- Apps with many destinations and actions, where power users want the keyboard.

### When not to use

- As the only way to reach something: every command should also exist in the visible UI.

### Exports

| Name | Kind |
| --- | --- |
| `CommandPalette` | component |
| `filterCommands` | function |

### API

#### `CommandPalette`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` | `boolean` | yes |  |  |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` | yes |  |  |
| `items` | `readonly CommandItem[]` | yes |  |  |
| `labels` | `CommandPaletteLabels` | yes |  |  |
| `hint` | `ReactNode \| ((state: { query: string; }) => ReactNode)` | no |  | A tip about what can be searched. A node is shown while the field is empty. A function is called with the current query on every render and decides for itself (return `null` to show nothing), so a hint can show for a short query ("Type at least 2 characters"). It is not shown while `bodyOverride` is set. |
| `hintPlacement` | `"top" \| "bottom"` | no | `"bottom"` | Where the hint sits: `bottom` (default) under the results, `top` above them so it stays in view in a long list. |
| `notice` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Content above the results that does not replace them (an error from the server search, a warning about stale results). It sits in a region outside the listbox, so it is not an option, and the arrows and Enter keep working on the commands. The palette gives it no role: wrap an error in `role="alert"` and a plain note in nothing. |
| `filter` | `(item: CommandItem, query: string) => boolean` | no | `filterCommands` | Decides which commands match the query. Defaults to {@link filterCommands}: every word of the query, ignoring case and accents, must appear in the label, description, group or keywords. Pass `() => true` when `items` already comes filtered (a server search driven by `onQueryChange`). |
| `onQueryChange` | `(query: string) => void` | no |  | Called as the person types, for searches that ask a server: replace `items` with the answer, pass `filter={() => true}` so the palette does not filter it again, and set `loading` while the request runs. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | no | `false` | A search is in flight: `aria-busy` on the results, the empty message waits, so "No results" does not flash before the server answers, and `labels.loading` (when given) is shown below the commands and announced each time `loading` turns on. |
| `groupOrder` | `readonly string[]` | no |  | The order of the group headings, by name. Groups not listed follow, in the order they are first used; listed groups with no results are left out. Default: the order of first use. |
| `bodyOverride` | `ReactNode \| ((state: { query: string; }) => ReactNode)` | no |  | Replaces the results (and the empty message and hint) with your own content, such as an answer to the query. A function gets the current query. While it is set the field is not a listbox: arrows and Enter do nothing, and the results are not announced. The field keeps focus. |
| `onEscape` | `() => boolean \| void` | no |  | Called on Escape before the palette closes. Return `true` when you handled it (left a sub-mode, cleared an answer): the palette then stays open, and the next Escape closes it. Return anything else to close. |
| `shortcut` | `boolean` | no | `true` | Open on Ctrl+K and Cmd+K. Default `true`. |
| `container` | `HTMLElement \| null` | no |  | Where the palette is mounted. Defaults to `document.body`. |

#### `filterCommands`

The default matcher: every word of `query` appears, ignoring case and accents, in the label, description, group or keywords.

```ts
filterCommands(item: CommandItem, query: string): boolean
```

### Types

- `CommandItem`: `{ key: string; label: string; description?: string | undefined; group?: string | undefined; icon?: ReactNode; tone?: CommandItemTone | undefined; keywords?: string | undefined; keepOpen?: boolean | undefined; onSelect: () => void; }`
- `CommandItemTone`: `"default" | "accent" | "danger"`
- `CommandPaletteLabels`: `{ title: string; placeholder: string; empty: (query: string) => ReactNode; resultCount: (count: number) => string; loading?: string | undefined; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { CommandPalette } from "@lufia/design-system/components/CommandPalette";

<CommandPalette
  open={open}
  onOpenChange={setOpen}
  items={[
    { key: "new", label: "New document", group: "Actions", icon: <PlusIcon />, onSelect: createDocument },
    {
      key: "settings",
      label: "Settings",
      group: "Go to",
      keywords: "preferences",
      onSelect: () => router.push("/settings"),
    },
  ]}
  labels={{
    title: "Search or run a command",
    placeholder: "Type a command or search…",
    empty: (query) => `No results for “${query}”`,
    resultCount: (count) => `${count} results`,
  }}
  hint="Search by name, or choose an action."
/>;
```

### Accessibility

Follows the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices pattern: [Combobox](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/).

Keyboard:

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Ctrl/Cmd + K | Opens the palette; closes it when open (`shortcut={false}` turns it off) |
| Type | Filters; the first match is highlighted |
| Down / Up | Moves the highlight, wrapping at the ends |
| Enter | Runs the highlighted command |
| Escape | Closes; focus returns to where it was |
| Tab | Cycles between the field and the close button |

### Motion

Its stylesheet has a `prefers-reduced-motion` branch.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-border-width-thick`, `--lufia-border-width-thin`, `--lufia-color-accent-default`, `--lufia-color-accent-subtle`, `--lufia-color-bg-canvas`, `--lufia-color-bg-surface-raised`, `--lufia-color-bg-surface-solid`, `--lufia-color-border-strong`, `--lufia-color-border-subtle`, `--lufia-color-focus-ring`, `--lufia-color-status-danger-bg`, `--lufia-color-status-danger-fg`, `--lufia-color-text-accent`, `--lufia-color-text-default`, `--lufia-color-text-muted`, `--lufia-color-text-subtle`, `--lufia-font-family-mono`, `--lufia-font-size-2xs`, `--lufia-font-size-lg`, `--lufia-font-size-sm`, `--lufia-font-size-xs`, `--lufia-font-weight-medium`, `--lufia-motion-distance-rise`, `--lufia-motion-duration-enter`, `--lufia-motion-duration-exit`, `--lufia-motion-easing-in`, `--lufia-motion-easing-out`, `--lufia-radius-control`, `--lufia-radius-full`, `--lufia-radius-md`, `--lufia-radius-panel`, `--lufia-radius-xs`, `--lufia-shadow-lg`, `--lufia-space-1`, `--lufia-space-2`, `--lufia-space-3`, `--lufia-space-4`, `--lufia-space-5`, `--lufia-z-modal`.

### Content guidelines

Command labels are verbs for actions ("New document") and nouns for destinations ("Settings"). Use `keywords` for the words
people might type that the label does not contain.

### Stories

- `components-overlays-commandpalette--default`
- `components-overlays-commandpalette--open-on-load`
- `components-overlays-commandpalette--single-group`
- `components-overlays-commandpalette--long-text`
- `components-overlays-commandpalette--phone-390`
- `components-overlays-commandpalette--phone-320`
- `components-overlays-commandpalette--fixed-section-order`
- `components-overlays-commandpalette--answer-replaces-results`
- `components-overlays-commandpalette--server-side-search`
- `components-overlays-commandpalette--server-search-with-status`
- `components-overlays-commandpalette--icon-tones`

## ConfirmDialog

> A modal question that has to be answered, with a destructive variant.

- Status: beta
- Category: Overlays
- Import: `import { ConfirmDialog, useConfirmDialog } from "@lufia/design-system/components/ConfirmDialog"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/ConfirmDialog](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/ConfirmDialog)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-overlays-confirmdialog--docs)

### Purpose

A question that has to be answered before anything else can happen: "Delete invoice 2041?" It is a [Modal](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-overlays-modal--docs)
with `role="alertdialog"`, two buttons, a destructive variant and a busy state.

### When to use

- An action that is hard or impossible to undo, or whose consequence is not obvious from the button: delete, discard, publish, remove access.

### When not to use

- Routine, reversible actions. Prefer doing it and offering **Undo** in a [Toast](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-feedback-toast--docs): it is faster and does not train people to click through confirmations.
- Collecting input. Use a Modal with a form.

### Exports

| Name | Kind |
| --- | --- |
| `ConfirmDialog` | component |
| `useConfirmDialog` | hook |

### API

#### `ConfirmDialog`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` | `boolean` | yes |  | Whether the modal is shown. Controlled: the modal never closes itself, it calls `onClose`. |
| `closeLabel` | `string` | no |  | Accessible name of the close button. Defaults to the provider's `labels.close`. |
| `container` | `Element \| DocumentFragment \| null` | no |  | Where the modal is portaled. Defaults to `document.body`. Pass an element of the same document, for example a preview frame; a container inside another document (an iframe) is not supported. |
| `sheetPlacement` | `"top" \| "bottom"` | no |  | Which edge the phone sheet is anchored to. `bottom` (default) rises from the bottom; `top` hangs from `--lufia-modal-sheet-offset`. |
| `classNames` | `ConfirmDialogClassNames` | no |  | Extra class names for the parts, for an app that attaches its own styles or test selectors. Every part also carries a stable `data-lufia-part` attribute: those of `Modal`, plus `cancel` and `confirm` on the buttons. |
| `size` | `ModalSize \| (string & {})` | no | `"sm"` | Maximum width on screens wider than a phone: a step or any CSS length, as on `Modal`. Default `sm` (not `md`). |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | What is being decided, as a question or an action: "Delete invoice 2041?". |
| `message` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | The consequence, in a sentence or two. Read out when the dialog opens. |
| `confirmLabel` | `string` | yes |  | Text of the confirming button. Name the action ("Delete invoice"), not "OK". |
| `cancelLabel` | `string` | yes |  | Text of the cancelling button. |
| `onConfirm` | `() => void` | yes |  |  |
| `onCancel` | `() => void` | yes |  | Cancel button, Escape and a click on the backdrop. Not called while `busy`. |
| `destructive` | `boolean` | no | `false` | The action cannot be undone: the confirm button is styled as dangerous and focus starts on Cancel. |
| `busy` | `boolean` | no | `false` | The confirmed action is running. The dialog refuses to close (no Escape, outside click or Cancel), keeps focus where it is and marks the confirm button `aria-busy`. Clear it when the action settles. |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

#### `useConfirmDialog`

A promise-based replacement for `window.confirm()`: ```tsx const { confirm, confirmDialog } = useConfirmDialog(); if (!(await confirm({ title, message, confirmLabel, cancelLabel, destructive: true }))) return; // render {confirmDialog} once in the component's JSX ``` One at a time: a new `confirm()` while one is open settles the first with `false`. Unmounting settles it with `false`.

```ts
useConfirmDialog(): { confirm: (next: ConfirmOptions) => Promise<boolean>; confirmDialog: Element | null; }
```

Returned members:

| Member | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `confirm` | `(next: ConfirmOptions) => Promise<boolean>` | yes |  |
| `confirmDialog` | `Element \| null` | yes |  |

### Types

- `ConfirmDialogClassNames`: `ModalClassNames & { cancel?: string | undefined; confirm?: string | undefined; }`
- `ConfirmOptions`: `Pick<ConfirmDialogProps, "className" | "size" | "sheetPlacement" | "classNames"> & { title: ReactNode; message: ReactNode; confirmLabel: string; cancelLabel: string; destructive?: boolean | undefined; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { ConfirmDialog } from "@lufia/design-system/components/ConfirmDialog";

<ConfirmDialog
  open={open}
  title="Delete invoice 2041?"
  message="The invoice and its payment history are removed. This cannot be undone."
  confirmLabel="Delete invoice"
  cancelLabel="Keep invoice"
  destructive
  busy={deleting}
  onConfirm={deleteInvoice}
  onCancel={() => setOpen(false)}
/>;
```

### Accessibility

Follows the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices pattern: [Alert dialog](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/alertdialog/).

- `role="alertdialog"`, named by the title and described by the message, so a screen reader reads both when it opens.
- No close button: the two explicit choices are the way out. Escape still cancels.
- Focus returns to the control that opened it.
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the dialog appears at once and the busy spinner stops (the dimmed button and `aria-busy` still carry the state).

### Motion

Its stylesheet has a `prefers-reduced-motion` branch.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-border-width-thin`, `--lufia-color-accent-default`, `--lufia-color-accent-hover`, `--lufia-color-bg-surface-raised`, `--lufia-color-border-strong`, `--lufia-color-focus-ring`, `--lufia-color-status-danger-on-solid`, `--lufia-color-status-danger-solid`, `--lufia-color-text-default`, `--lufia-color-text-on-accent`, `--lufia-font-size-md`, `--lufia-font-weight-semibold`, `--lufia-motion-duration-instant`, `--lufia-motion-easing-out`, `--lufia-opacity-disabled`, `--lufia-radius-control`, `--lufia-radius-full`, `--lufia-space-2`, `--lufia-space-4`.

### Content guidelines

Title: the question, with the object ("Delete invoice 2041?"). Message: the consequence, one or two sentences. Buttons:
the verb ("Delete invoice" / "Keep invoice"), never "Yes" / "No" or "OK".

### Stories

- `components-overlays-confirmdialog--default`
- `components-overlays-confirmdialog--open-by-default`
- `components-overlays-confirmdialog--destructive`
- `components-overlays-confirmdialog--wide-top-sheet`
- `components-overlays-confirmdialog--part-class-names`
- `components-overlays-confirmdialog--busy`
- `components-overlays-confirmdialog--slow-confirmation`
- `components-overlays-confirmdialog--long-text`
- `components-overlays-confirmdialog--phone`
- `components-overlays-confirmdialog--promise-based`
- `components-overlays-confirmdialog--all-themes`

## DetailAttentionCard

> A high-signal card for deadlines and risk, with a tone mark and an optional action.

- Status: beta
- Category: Data display
- Import: `import { DetailAttentionCard } from "@lufia/design-system/components/DetailAttentionCard"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/DetailAttentionCard](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/DetailAttentionCard)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-data-display-detailattentioncard--docs)

### Purpose

A high-signal card for deadlines, risk and missing-data states. A tone mark, a title, optional description
and meta line, and an optional call to action.

### When to use

- A single item needs the user's attention and you can state what to do next.

### When not to use

- Routine confirmations (use a toast) or long lists of problems (use a table with status cells).
- Do not stack more than two or three on a screen; if everything is urgent, nothing is.

### API

#### `DetailAttentionCard`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tone` | `"ok" \| "warn" \| "danger" \| "critical" \| "neutral"` | yes |  |  |
| `title` | `string` | yes |  |  |
| `description` | `string` | no |  |  |
| `meta` | `string` | no |  |  |
| `action` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Call-to-action rendered under the copy (a button or link). |
| `toneLabel` | `string` | no |  | Text that names the tone for assistive technology (for example "Overdue"). The tone is otherwise conveyed by colour and a glyph only, so pass it whenever the tone carries meaning. |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `DetailAttentionCardProps`: `Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>, "title"> & { tone: DetailAttentionTone; title: string; description?: string | undefined; meta?: string | undefined; action?: ReactNode; toneLabel?: string | undefined; }`
- `DetailAttentionTone`: `"ok" | "warn" | "danger" | "critical" | "neutral"`

### Example

```tsx
import { DetailAttentionCard } from "@lufia/design-system/components/DetailAttentionCard";

<DetailAttentionCard
  tone="danger"
  toneLabel="Overdue"
  title="Subscription expired"
  action={<a href="/billing">Renew</a>}
/>;
```

### Accessibility

- Renders a `<section>` with an `<h3>`. Make sure the page's heading hierarchy fits, or wrap it in a labelled region.
- The tone is shown by colour and a glyph (`✓`, `!`, `·`) that are hidden from assistive technology. **Pass `toneLabel`** (for example "Overdue") whenever the tone carries meaning; it is prepended to the heading as visually hidden text.
- Foreground and background pairs in every tone pass AA in all theme and mode combinations (see Foundations / Colors).
- The action is a plain slot; its keyboard behaviour is the control you pass in. On narrow screens buttons and links in the slot stretch to full width.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Its stylesheet reads no `--lufia-*` tokens directly (no CSS module, or it composes other components).

### Content guidelines

All copy comes in through props, already localised. Keep titles under about 60 characters; long strings wrap. Prefer a plain imperative verb for the action label ("Renew", not "Renew now!!").

### Stories

- `components-data-display-detailattentioncard--warn`
- `components-data-display-detailattentioncard--ok`
- `components-data-display-detailattentioncard--danger`
- `components-data-display-detailattentioncard--critical`
- `components-data-display-detailattentioncard--neutral`
- `components-data-display-detailattentioncard--title-only`
- `components-data-display-detailattentioncard--long-content`
- `components-data-display-detailattentioncard--all-tones`
- `components-data-display-detailattentioncard--all-themes`

## DetailList

> Label and value pairs for the details of one record.

- Status: beta
- Category: Data display
- Import: `import { DetailList } from "@lufia/design-system/components/DetailList"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/DetailList](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/DetailList)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-data-display-detaillist--docs)

### Purpose

Key-value rows for detail panels and modals, rendered as a native description list.

### When to use

- Several short label/value facts about one record.

### When not to use

- Tabular data with many records (use a table) or editable fields (use a form).

### API

#### `DetailList`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rows` | `DetailListRow[]` | yes |  |  |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `DetailListProps`: `HTMLAttributes<HTMLDListElement> & { rows: DetailListRow[]; }`
- `DetailListRow`: `{ label: string; value: ReactNode; mono?: boolean | undefined; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { DetailList } from "@lufia/design-system/components/DetailList";

<DetailList
  rows={[
    { label: "Name", value: "Ada Example" },
    { label: "Identifier", value: "A-1042", mono: true },
  ]}
/>;
```

### Accessibility

- Uses `<dl>`, `<dt>` and `<dd>`, which expose the label-value relationship to screen readers without extra ARIA.
- The label column is capped at 40% and wraps. A long label never pushes values out of their container, so the layout reflows at 320px.
- Values may be any React node; links and buttons inside keep their own focus behaviour.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-color-text-default`, `--lufia-color-text-muted`, `--lufia-font-family-mono`, `--lufia-space-2`, `--lufia-space-4`.

### Content guidelines

Labels are short nouns without trailing colons (the grid provides the separation). Use `mono` for dates, counts and
identifiers so digits align. Localise and format values (dates, numbers) in the app: locales differ in both.

### Stories

- `components-data-display-detaillist--default`
- `components-data-display-detaillist--rich-values`
- `components-data-display-detaillist--long-label`
- `components-data-display-detaillist--empty`
- `components-data-display-detaillist--all-themes`

## DetailSectionCard

> A titled card that holds one section of a detail page.

- Status: beta
- Category: Data display
- Import: `import { DetailSectionCard } from "@lufia/design-system/components/DetailSectionCard"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/DetailSectionCard](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/DetailSectionCard)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-data-display-detailsectioncard--docs)

### Purpose

A section container for detail pages and modals with a consistent heading, optional description, icon, header action and
content area.

### When to use

- Group related read-only or editable details under one heading on a detail view.

### When not to use

- Page-level layout (it is not a page shell) or a single value (use `DetailList`).

### API

#### `DetailSectionCard`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | yes |  |  |
| `title` | `string` | yes |  |  |
| `description` | `string` | no |  |  |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Decorative icon shown before the title (hidden from assistive technology). |
| `action` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Control aligned to the end of the header, such as an "Edit" button. |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `DetailSectionCardProps`: `Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>, "title"> & { title: string; description?: string | undefined; icon?: ReactNode; action?: ReactNode; children: ReactNode; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { DetailSectionCard } from "@lufia/design-system/components/DetailSectionCard";

<DetailSectionCard title="Contact details" action={<a href="/contacts/edit">Edit</a>}>
  <DetailList rows={rows} />
</DetailSectionCard>;
```

### Accessibility

- A `<section>` with an `<h3>` title. Mind the heading level in the host page; it is fixed at 3 today.
- The icon is decorative and hidden from assistive technology; the title carries the meaning.
- The header action wraps below the title on narrow screens (`flex-wrap`) and stays reachable in tab order after the title.
- Long titles and descriptions use `overflow-wrap: anywhere`, so content reflows at 320px with no horizontal scrolling.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Its stylesheet reads no `--lufia-*` tokens directly (no CSS module, or it composes other components).

### Content guidelines

Strings arrive localised through props. Titles are nouns ("Contacts"), not sentences.

### Stories

- `components-data-display-detailsectioncard--default`
- `components-data-display-detailsectioncard--with-icon-and-action`
- `components-data-display-detailsectioncard--title-only`
- `components-data-display-detailsectioncard--long-content`
- `components-data-display-detailsectioncard--all-themes`

## EmptyState

> What to show when a list or panel has nothing yet, with the one next step.

- Status: beta
- Category: Feedback
- Import: `import { EmptyState } from "@lufia/design-system/components/EmptyState"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/EmptyState](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/EmptyState)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-feedback-emptystate--docs)

### Purpose

Placeholder for a list, table or panel that has nothing to show yet: an optional icon, a title, an explanation and a next
step.

### When to use

- First use (nothing created yet), and results that are empty after a search or filter.

### When not to use

- Errors (say what went wrong and how to recover instead) or loading states (use a skeleton or spinner).

### API

#### `EmptyState`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Decorative illustration or icon (hidden from assistive technology). |
| `title` | `string` | yes |  |  |
| `body` | `string` | no |  |  |
| `action` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Next step, usually a button or link. |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `EmptyStateProps`: `Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>, "title"> & { icon?: ReactNode; title: string; body?: string | undefined; action?: ReactNode; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { EmptyState } from "@lufia/design-system/components/EmptyState";

<EmptyState
  title="No documents yet"
  body="Documents you upload will appear here."
  action={<a href="/upload">Upload document</a>}
/>;
```

### Accessibility

- The root is `role="status"`, a polite live region. When the empty state replaces a list after a filter changes, the new message is announced. If it is present on first render it is not announced, which is the right behaviour.
- The icon is decorative (`aria-hidden`). Never put essential information only in the icon.
- Title and body use the text and muted-text tokens, which pass AA on every surface.
- The action slot keeps the keyboard behaviour of the control you pass in.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-color-text-default`, `--lufia-color-text-muted`, `--lufia-font-family-display`, `--lufia-font-size-md`, `--lufia-font-size-sm`, `--lufia-font-weight-semibold`, `--lufia-opacity-decorative`, `--lufia-space-1`, `--lufia-space-12`, `--lufia-space-2`, `--lufia-space-3`, `--lufia-space-6`.

### Content guidelines

All strings are props. Keep the title under about 40 characters and the body to one or two sentences (the body is capped
at 340px wide for readability).

### Stories

- `components-feedback-emptystate--default`
- `components-feedback-emptystate--title-only`
- `components-feedback-emptystate--no-action`
- `components-feedback-emptystate--search-no-results`
- `components-feedback-emptystate--all-themes`

## FileField

> A file picker with drag and drop, validation and a list of chosen files.

- Status: beta
- Category: Forms
- Import: `import { FileField, formatFileSize, matchesAccept } from "@lufia/design-system/components/FileField"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/FileField](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/FileField)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-forms-filefield--docs)

### Purpose

A file picker with a drop area. The native `<input type="file">` stays in the form, limits on type, size and count are checked
with messages you provide, and the chosen files are listed with a remove button each.

### When to use

- Attachments, documents and images that are submitted with a form, where people may have the files on their desktop.

### When not to use

- Importing data that needs a preview and column mapping: build that flow around a plain file input.
- Large or resumable uploads: use a dedicated uploader and show its progress.

### Exports

| Name | Kind |
| --- | --- |
| `FileField` | component |
| `formatFileSize` | function |
| `matchesAccept` | function |

### API

#### `FileField`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `chooseLabel` | `string` | yes |  | Text of the button that opens the file picker. |
| `replaceLabel` | `string` | no |  | Text of the button once a single file is chosen. Defaults to `chooseLabel`. |
| `dropLabel` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Hint inside the drop area ("or drop files here"). Hidden from assistive technology: the button does the same job. |
| `emptyLabel` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Shown in place of the list while nothing is chosen ("No file chosen"). |
| `maxSize` | `number` | no |  | Largest file in bytes. Larger files are rejected with reason `"size"`. |
| `maxFiles` | `number` | no |  | Most files at once (with `multiple`). The extra ones are rejected with reason `"count"`. |
| `formatRejection` | `(rejection: FileRejection, limits: FileLimits) => string` | yes |  | The message for a rejected file. Required: every rejection is shown to the person in their language. |
| `removeLabel` | `(file: File) => string` | no | `defaultRemoveLabel` | Accessible name of a file's remove button. Aria-only. Defaults to "Remove" and the file name. |
| `removeText` | `string` | no |  | Visible text on the remove button. Defaults to a cross icon only. |
| `describeFiles` | `(files: readonly File[]) => string` | no |  | Read out politely when the chosen files change ("2 files chosen"). Optional. |
| `locale` | `string` | no |  | Locale of the sizes. The runtime's when omitted. |
| `files` | `readonly File[]` | no |  | Controlled files. |
| `onFilesChange` | `(files: File[]) => void` | no |  | Called with the whole list after a pick, a drop or a removal. |
| `onReject` | `(rejections: FileRejection[]) => void` | no |  | Called with files that were refused, after the message is shown. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | no |  | Marks the control invalid without a `FormField`. |
| `className` | `string` | no |  | Goes on the root element. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLInputElement>` | no |  |  |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

#### `formatFileSize`

A readable file size: "820 B", "12.4 KB", "1.4 MB". Units are symbols, not words; the number follows `locale` (the runtime's when omitted), so "1,4 MB" in Portuguese.

```ts
formatFileSize(bytes: number, locale?: string | undefined): string
```

#### `matchesAccept`

The rule of the native `accept` attribute (extensions, MIME types and `type/*` wildcards, comma separated), applied by hand because a dropped file bypasses the attribute. An empty rule accepts everything.

```ts
matchesAccept(file: Pick<File, "name" | "type">, accept?: string | undefined): boolean
```

### Types

- `FileLimits`: `{ accept?: string | undefined; maxSize?: number | undefined; maxFiles?: number | undefined; }`
- `FileRejection`: `{ file: File; reason: FileRejectionReason; }`
- `FileRejectionReason`: `"type" | "size" | "count"`

### Example

```tsx
import { FormField } from "@lufia/design-system/components/FormField";
import { FileField } from "@lufia/design-system/components/FileField";

<FormField label="Attachments" hint="PDF, PNG or JPG, up to 5 MB each.">
  <FileField
    name="attachments"
    multiple
    accept=".pdf,.png,.jpg"
    maxSize={5 * 1024 * 1024}
    maxFiles={4}
    chooseLabel="Choose files"
    dropLabel="or drop files here"
    emptyLabel="No file chosen"
    formatRejection={({ file, reason }, limits) => messages[reason](file.name, limits)}
    onFilesChange={setFiles}
  />
</FormField>;
```

### Accessibility

- The real input is the control: it has the field's accessible name and description, `aria-invalid`, and `required`. The visible button is its label and is hidden from assistive technology, so the name is not read twice.
- Focus on the input draws the focus ring on the button.
- Refusals use `role="alert"` and are part of the input's description. Several are shown as a list.
- Each remove button is named after its file ("Remove report.pdf"; change it with `removeLabel`). After a removal focus returns to the input.
- Pass `describeFiles` to have a polite status announce the new count ("2 files chosen") after a pick.
- The drop area is a dashed border that fills with the accent when files are dragged over it, which is not colour alone.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-border-width-thick`, `--lufia-border-width-thin`, `--lufia-color-accent-default`, `--lufia-color-accent-subtle`, `--lufia-color-bg-field`, `--lufia-color-bg-surface`, `--lufia-color-bg-surface-raised`, `--lufia-color-border-strong`, `--lufia-color-border-subtle`, `--lufia-color-focus-ring`, `--lufia-color-status-danger-fg`, `--lufia-color-text-default`, `--lufia-color-text-muted`, `--lufia-font-size-sm`, `--lufia-font-size-xs`, `--lufia-font-weight-medium`, `--lufia-font-weight-semibold`, `--lufia-motion-duration-instant`, `--lufia-motion-easing-out`, `--lufia-opacity-disabled`, `--lufia-radius-card`, `--lufia-radius-control`, `--lufia-radius-md`, `--lufia-space-1`, `--lufia-space-2`, `--lufia-space-3`, `--lufia-space-4`.

### Content guidelines

Say what is accepted before the person chooses, in the hint: types and the size limit. Refusals say which file and why, and
what to do: "report.docx is not supported. Use a PDF.", "huge.pdf is larger than 5 MB.". Keep the button a verb phrase
("Choose files") and the drop text secondary ("or drop files here"), since many people will not drag.

### Stories

- `components-forms-filefield--default`
- `components-forms-filefield--single-file`
- `components-forms-filefield--with-files`
- `components-forms-filefield--rejected`
- `components-forms-filefield--required`
- `components-forms-filefield--invalid`
- `components-forms-filefield--disabled`
- `components-forms-filefield--long-text`
- `components-forms-filefield--phone-320`
- `components-forms-filefield--right-to-left`
- `components-forms-filefield--all-themes`

## FormField

> Label, hint and error wired to any control, so the control stays accessible by default.

- Status: beta
- Category: Forms
- Import: `import { FormField, FormFieldContext, useFormFieldControl, useFormFieldLabelId } from "@lufia/design-system/components/FormField"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/FormField](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/FormField)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-forms-formfield--docs)

### Purpose

The wrapper that turns a bare control into a field: a label, an optional hint, an optional error, and the wiring between
them. It generates the ids, points the label at the control, links the hint and the error with `aria-describedby`, sets
`aria-invalid` when there is an error, and marks a required field in text.

### When to use

- Every single-value control that has a label of its own: text, select, search, file, combobox.

### When not to use

- A group of checkboxes or radios. Those have a legend, not a label: use `RadioGroup`, or a native `<fieldset>`.
- A checkbox or switch on its own line. They carry their own label.
- A placeholder in place of a label. A placeholder disappears as soon as the person types.

### Exports

| Name | Kind |
| --- | --- |
| `FormField` | component |
| `FormFieldContext` | component |
| `useFormFieldControl` | hook |
| `useFormFieldLabelId` | hook |

### API

#### `FormField`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | no |  | Base id of the control; the hint and error ids derive from it. Generated when omitted. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | The visible label. Every control needs one. |
| `hint` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Help shown under the control, linked to it with `aria-describedby`. |
| `error` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Error text. Its presence marks the control `aria-invalid` and shows the message with an icon. |
| `required` | `boolean` | no |  | Marks the control required and shows an asterisk plus text for assistive technology. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | no |  |  |
| `requiredLabel` | `string` | no |  | Text read after the label when `required`. Aria-only: the visible mark is a glyph. Defaults to the `required` label of `LufiaProvider` ("required"), so an app sets the word once; this prop wins when given. |
| `children` | `ReactNode \| ((control: FormFieldControlProps) => ReactNode)` | yes |  | The control. A node reaches the controls of this package through context; a function receives the props to spread on any other control (a third-party input, a native element). |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

#### `FormFieldContext`

No props of its own. Native element attributes pass through.

#### `useFormFieldControl`

Merges the props a control got from its own caller with the ones of the surrounding `FormField`. Outside a field it returns the caller's props untouched, so every control works on its own. Inside a field the field's `id` wins (the label points at it), `aria-describedby` is the union of both lists, and a control is invalid, required or disabled when either side says so. Use this when building a control that should join a field; the controls of this package already do.

```ts
useFormFieldControl(own?: OwnProps): { id: string | undefined; "aria-describedby": string | undefined; "aria-invalid": true | undefined; required: true | undefined; disabled: true | undefined; }
```

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `own` | `OwnProps` | no |  |

Returned members:

| Member | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string \| undefined` | yes |  |
| `aria-describedby` | `string \| undefined` | yes |  |
| `aria-invalid` | `true \| undefined` | yes |  |
| `required` | `true \| undefined` | yes |  |
| `disabled` | `true \| undefined` | yes |  |

#### `useFormFieldLabelId`

The id of the surrounding `FormField`'s label element, for widgets that need to name a second element (a listbox, a popup) after the field. `undefined` outside a field.

```ts
useFormFieldLabelId(): string | undefined
```

### Types

- `FormFieldControlProps`: `{ id: string; "aria-describedby"?: string | undefined; "aria-invalid"?: true | undefined; required?: boolean | undefined; disabled?: boolean | undefined; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { FormField } from "@lufia/design-system/components/FormField";
import { TextInput } from "@lufia/design-system/components/TextInput";

<FormField label="Project name" hint="Shown on invoices." required error={errors.name}>
  <TextInput name="name" />
</FormField>;
```

### Accessibility

- The label is a real `<label for>`, so the control's accessible name is the label text.
- The control's accessible description is the hint followed by the error.
- `aria-invalid="true"` is present only while there is an error, so a pristine field is not announced as invalid.
- Validate on blur or on submit, not on every keystroke, so the alert does not interrupt typing.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-color-status-danger-fg`, `--lufia-color-text-default`, `--lufia-color-text-muted`, `--lufia-font-line-height-tight`, `--lufia-font-size-sm`, `--lufia-font-weight-semibold`, `--lufia-space-1`, `--lufia-space-2`.

### Content guidelines

Labels are nouns, short, in sentence case: "Project name", not "Please enter the name of your project". Hints say what is
allowed or why it is asked ("Up to 40 characters"). Errors say what to do, not what went wrong: "Enter a project name to
continue", not "Invalid input". Never rely on "required" in colour; do not write "(required)" yourself, the component adds it
for assistive technology.

### Stories

- `components-forms-formfield--default`
- `components-forms-formfield--with-hint`
- `components-forms-formfield--required`
- `components-forms-formfield--invalid`
- `components-forms-formfield--disabled`
- `components-forms-formfield--required-from-provider`
- `components-forms-formfield--long-text`
- `components-forms-formfield--phone-320`
- `components-forms-formfield--right-to-left`
- `components-forms-formfield--all-themes`

## IconButton

> A button with only an icon, which therefore requires an accessible name.

- Status: beta
- Category: Actions
- Import: `import { IconButton } from "@lufia/design-system/components/IconButton"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/IconButton](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/IconButton)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-actions-iconbutton--docs)

### Purpose

A `Button` that shows only an icon. The accessible name is required by the types, and a tooltip comes with it.

### When to use

- Compact, well-known actions where the icon is unambiguous: close, search, settings, overflow.
- Toolbars and table rows where a text label would not fit.

### When not to use

- Actions whose icon is not obvious. Use a `Button` with a label instead.
- The primary action of a view: it deserves a visible label.

### API

#### `IconButton`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `href` | `string` | no |  | When present the button renders as a link (through the `LufiaProvider` link component). |
| `aria-label` | `string` | yes |  | Defines a string value that labels the current element. Accessible name. Required: an icon alone has no name, and the types refuse a button without one. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLButtonElement> \| Ref<HTMLAnchorElement>` | no |  | Forwarded to the anchor (the link component must forward its `ref`, as plain `<a>` and router links do). |
| `title` | `string` | no |  | Tooltip text. Defaults to `aria-label`, so sighted mouse users get the same name. |
| `variant` | `"primary" \| "secondary" \| "ghost" \| "danger"` | no | `"ghost"` | Visual weight. One `primary` per view; `danger` only for destructive actions. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | no |  |  |
| `loading` | `boolean` | no |  | Shows a spinner in place of the content and ignores activation. The button keeps its width, stays focusable and reports `aria-busy`. It is not natively disabled, so keyboard focus is not lost when the work starts. |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | The icon. Decorative: the name comes from `aria-label`. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | no |  | A link cannot be natively disabled; this marks it `aria-disabled` and ignores activation. |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

##### Variants

The props are a union of forms; `href` selects the form. Only the props that differ between forms are listed: a prop with the same type and requirement in every form is not repeated. Native element attributes (event handlers, for instance) are typed for each form's element.

###### `href: undefined`

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `form` | `string` | no | Native attribute in this form. |
| `formAction` | `string \| ((formData: FormData) => void \| Promise<void>)` | no | Native attribute in this form. |
| `formEncType` | `string` | no | Native attribute in this form. |
| `formMethod` | `string` | no | Native attribute in this form. |
| `formNoValidate` | `boolean` | no | Native attribute in this form. |
| `formTarget` | `string` | no | Native attribute in this form. |
| `href` | `undefined` | no |  |
| `name` | `string` | no | Native attribute in this form. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLButtonElement>` | no | In every form; only its type differs. |
| `value` | `string \| number \| readonly string[]` | no | Native attribute in this form. |

###### `href: string`

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `download` | `any` | no | Native attribute in this form. |
| `href` | `string` | yes | When present the button renders as a link (through the `LufiaProvider` link component). |
| `hrefLang` | `string` | no | Native attribute in this form. |
| `media` | `string` | no | Native attribute in this form. |
| `ping` | `string` | no | Native attribute in this form. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLAnchorElement>` | no | Forwarded to the anchor (the link component must forward its `ref`, as plain `<a>` and router links do). In every form; only its type differs. |
| `referrerPolicy` | `"" \| "origin" \| "no-referrer" \| "no-referrer-when-downgrade" \| "origin-when-cross-origin" \| "same-origin" \| "strict-origin" \| "strict-origin-when-cross-origin" \| "unsafe-url"` | no | Native attribute in this form. |
| `target` | `HTMLAttributeAnchorTarget` | no | Native attribute in this form. |

### Types

- `IconButtonProps`: `(Omit<AsButton, "children" | "fullWidth" | "iconStart" | "iconEnd"> | Omit<AsLink, "children" | "fullWidth" | "iconStart" | "iconEnd">) & { "aria-label": string; icon: ReactNode; title?: string | undefined; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { IconButton } from "@lufia/design-system/components/IconButton";

<IconButton icon={<SettingsIcon />} aria-label="Open settings" onClick={openSettings} />;
```

### Accessibility

Follows the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices pattern: [Button](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/button/).

Keyboard:

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Moves focus to the button (a disabled one is skipped) |
| Enter / Space | Activates a button; Enter activates a link |

- `aria-label` is the accessible name. `title` shows the same text as a tooltip for mouse users; it is not relied on as the name.
- The title tooltip is not shown on touch or to keyboard users, which is why the name must not depend on it.
- The icon is hidden from assistive technology.
- The target is 2.5rem square at the default size (2rem at `sm`, 2.75rem on coarse pointers), above the WCAG 2.5.8 minimum.
- Focus ring, loading and forced-colors behaviour are those of `Button`.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Its stylesheet reads no `--lufia-*` tokens directly (no CSS module, or it composes other components).

### Content guidelines

Name the action, not the picture: "Open settings", not "Cog". Keep it to two or three words.

### Stories

- `components-actions-iconbutton--default`
- `components-actions-iconbutton--secondary`
- `components-actions-iconbutton--primary`
- `components-actions-iconbutton--disabled`
- `components-actions-iconbutton--loading`
- `components-actions-iconbutton--as-link`
- `components-actions-iconbutton--custom-title`
- `components-actions-iconbutton--all-variants-and-sizes`
- `components-actions-iconbutton--all-themes`

## Link

> Navigation inside text, routed through the adapter set on LufiaProvider.

- Status: beta
- Category: Actions
- Import: `import { Link } from "@lufia/design-system/components/Link"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/Link](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/Link)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-actions-link--docs)

### Purpose

An inline text link. It goes through the app's router link, and an external one says that it leaves the page.

### When to use

- A link inside a sentence or a short block of text.
- Any link to another site, with `externalLabel`.

### When not to use

- An action that does something on the page: use `Button`.
- A call to action that looks like a button but navigates: use `Button` with `href`.
- A whole clickable surface: use `Card` with `href`.

### API

#### `Link`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `href` | `string` | yes |  |  |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | yes |  |  |
| `externalLabel` | `string` | no |  | Marks the link as external: it opens in a new tab (`target="_blank"`, `rel="noopener noreferrer"`) and shows an indicator. The value is the visually hidden text read after the link text, such as "(opens in new tab)", so the new tab is announced. Giving the text is what makes a link external, so there is no external link without it. |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `LinkProps`: `Omit<AnchorHTMLAttributes<HTMLAnchorElement>, "children" | "href"> & { href: string; children: ReactNode; externalLabel?: string | undefined; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { Link } from "@lufia/design-system/components/Link";

<Link href="/guide">read the guide</Link>
<Link href="https://example.com" externalLabel="(opens in new tab)">the specification</Link>
```

### Accessibility

Keyboard:

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Moves focus to the link |
| Enter | Follows the link |

- Links are underlined, so colour is not the only cue (WCAG 1.4.1).
- `externalLabel` makes a link external, so an external link cannot go without the announcement. It is read after the link text, so people using a screen reader know a new tab opens before they activate it. The visible icon is decorative and mirrored in right-to-left layouts.
- External links get `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.
- Focus shows a 2px ring. In forced-colors mode the link uses `LinkText`.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-border-width-thick`, `--lufia-color-focus-ring`, `--lufia-color-text-accent`, `--lufia-motion-duration-fast`, `--lufia-motion-easing-out`, `--lufia-radius-xs`.

### Content guidelines

Make the link text meaningful on its own ("read the migration guide", not "click here"). Do not put the destination's URL in
the text unless the URL is the content.

### Stories

- `components-actions-link--default`
- `components-actions-link--external`
- `components-actions-link--long-text`
- `components-actions-link--phone-320`
- `components-actions-link--right-to-left`
- `components-actions-link--all-themes`

## LufiaProvider

> Sets the link adapter and the aria-only labels once, at the root of an app.

- Status: beta
- Category: Utilities
- Import: `import { DEFAULT_LABELS, LufiaLink, LufiaProvider, useLufia } from "@lufia/design-system/components/LufiaProvider"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/LufiaProvider](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/LufiaProvider)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-utilities-lufiaprovider--docs)

### Purpose

One place to adapt the package to an app: the **link component** that navigates, and the **aria-only labels** that
components fall back on. The package imports no router and no i18n library; this provider is the seam.

### When to use

- Once, at the root of every app that uses the package.
- Nested, to change the language or the router of one subtree.

### When not to use

- For visible copy (titles, messages, button text). Those are props on each component, so the app's own i18n layer owns them. `labels` is only text that assistive technology reads.

### Exports

| Name | Kind |
| --- | --- |
| `DEFAULT_LABELS` | constant |
| `LufiaLink` | component |
| `LufiaProvider` | component |
| `useLufia` | hook |

### API

#### `LufiaLink`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `href` | `string` | yes |  |  |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLAnchorElement>` | no |  | React 19 passes `ref` as a prop; a link component should forward it to the anchor. |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

#### `LufiaProvider`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `linkComponent` | `LinkComponent` | no |  | Renders every navigating element of the package. Defaults to a plain `<a>`. |
| `labels` | `Partial<LufiaLabels>` | no |  | Aria-only text, merged over the defaults (and over an outer provider). |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | yes |  |  |

#### `useLufia`

The link component and labels in effect. Safe outside a provider: it returns the defaults.

```ts
useLufia(): LufiaContextValue
```

Returned members:

| Member | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `linkComponent` | `LinkComponent` | yes |  |
| `labels` | `LufiaLabels` | yes |  |

### Types

- `LinkComponent`: `ComponentClass<LinkComponentProps, any> | FunctionComponent<LinkComponentProps>`
- `LinkComponentProps`: `AnchorHTMLAttributes<HTMLAnchorElement> & { href: string; ref?: Ref<HTMLAnchorElement> | undefined; }`
- `LufiaContextValue`: `{ linkComponent: LinkComponent; labels: LufiaLabels; }`
- `LufiaLabels`: `{ close: string; dismiss: string; notifications: string; required: string; }`
- `LufiaProviderProps`: `{ linkComponent?: LinkComponent | undefined; labels?: Partial<LufiaLabels> | undefined; children: ReactNode; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { LufiaProvider } from "@lufia/design-system/components/LufiaProvider";
import NextLink from "next/link";

<LufiaProvider linkComponent={NextLink} labels={{ close: "Fechar", dismiss: "Dispensar" }}>
  {children}
</LufiaProvider>;
```

### Accessibility

- The defaults are neutral English so a missing provider never leaves a control without a name. In a localised app, always override them: a Portuguese page with an English "Close" button is an accessibility defect.
- A custom `linkComponent` must render a real anchor (`<a href>`) so links keep link semantics, middle-click and "open in new tab".

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Its stylesheet reads no `--lufia-*` tokens directly (no CSS module, or it composes other components).

### Stories

- `components-utilities-lufiaprovider--default`
- `components-utilities-lufiaprovider--translated-labels`
- `components-utilities-lufiaprovider--all-themes`

## Modal

> A dialog that interrupts the page and traps focus until it is dismissed.

- Status: beta
- Category: Overlays
- Import: `import { Modal, notifyTopModalDialogChanged } from "@lufia/design-system/components/Modal"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/Modal](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/Modal)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-overlays-modal--docs)

### Purpose

A dialog that blocks the page behind it until the person answers or dismisses it. Portaled to `document.body`, with focus
containment, scroll lock, an inert background and an enter/exit motion.

### When to use

- A focused task or a decision that must be finished or abandoned before returning to the page: editing a record, picking from a list, confirming settings.
- Anything that interrupts and needs an answer: build on it with [ConfirmDialog](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-overlays-confirmdialog--docs).

### When not to use

- A message that does not need a response: use a [Toast](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-feedback-toast--docs).
- Content the person should be able to compare with the page. A side panel or an inline expansion lets them keep the context a modal hides.
- Navigation. If the content has its own URL and is more than a step, make it a page. To make a modal linkable, drive `open` with `useModalState`.

### Exports

| Name | Kind |
| --- | --- |
| `Modal` | component |
| `notifyTopModalDialogChanged` | function |

### API

#### `Modal`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` | `boolean` | yes |  | Whether the modal is shown. Controlled: the modal never closes itself, it calls `onClose`. |
| `onClose` | `() => void` | yes |  | Called when the person asks to close: the close button, Escape, or a click outside (see the policy props). |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | The dialog's accessible name and visible heading. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Optional supporting text, wired to `aria-describedby`. |
| `size` | `ModalSize \| (string & {})` | no | `"md"` | Maximum width on screens wider than a phone: a step, or any CSS length for a custom maximum inline size (`"62rem"`, `"min(100%, 70ch)"`). On a phone every size is a sheet. Default `md`. |
| `sheetPlacement` | `"top" \| "bottom"` | no | `"bottom"` | Which edge the phone sheet is anchored to. `bottom` (default) rises from the bottom; `top` hangs from `--lufia-modal-sheet-offset`. |
| `titleWrap` | `"wrap" \| "ellipsis"` | no | `"wrap"` | `wrap` (default) lets a long title wrap onto several lines; `ellipsis` keeps it on one line and truncates it. |
| `scrollShadow` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Scroll the body between the fixed header and footer and show an edge shadow where more content is hidden. |
| `keepMounted` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Keep the content mounted while the modal is closed, so typed input and component state survive. The closed modal is hidden and inert; it has no exit animation. |
| `renderAs` | `"portal" \| "dialog"` | no | `"portal"` | `portal` (default) renders a fixed-position layer in a portal. `dialog` renders a native `<dialog>` opened with `showModal()`, which sits in the browser's top layer above everything, including other fixed layers. Focus trap, Escape, scroll lock and the shared layer stack behave the same in both. Differences in `dialog` mode: the page behind is made inert by the browser, not by the package; the exit is not animated; the backdrop is the native `::backdrop`. |
| `classNames` | `ModalClassNames` | no |  | Extra class names for the parts, for an app that attaches its own styles or test selectors. Every part also carries a stable `data-lufia-part` attribute: `layer`, `backdrop`, `frame`, `panel`, `header`, `title`, `description`, `body`, `footer`, `close`. |
| `headerAction` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Extra controls placed beside the close button in the header. |
| `footer` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Content of the footer bar, usually the actions. The bar is left out when this is empty. |
| `footerLayout` | `"row" \| "stack"` | no | `"row"` | How the footer actions are laid out on a narrow phone (30rem and below). `row` (default) keeps them side by side in DOM order, so the primary action goes last, at the inline end; text actions grow to fill the bar and wrap if their labels cannot fit, while icon-only triggers keep their size. `stack` puts them in a full-width column, primary on top. |
| `closeLabel` | `string` | no |  | Accessible name of the close button. Defaults to the provider's `labels.close`. |
| `hideCloseButton` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Leave out the close button, e.g. when the footer already offers the way out. Escape and outside click still apply. |
| `busy` | `boolean` | no | `false` | An action that dismissing would not abort is in flight. Sets `aria-busy`, disables the close button and refuses every dismissal (Escape, outside click, the close button), so a refused dismissal is perceivable and not a silent no-op. |
| `closeOnEscape` | `boolean` | no | `true` | Escape calls `onClose`. Default `true`. |
| `closeOnOutsideClick` | `boolean` | no | `true` | A click on the backdrop calls `onClose`. Default `true`. Turn it off for forms with unsaved input. |
| `initialFocus` | `"container" \| "first" \| RefObject<HTMLElement \| null>` | no | `"container"` | Where focus lands on open. Default: the dialog itself (named by the title, no keyboard pops up). |
| `role` | `"dialog" \| "alertdialog"` | no | `"dialog"` | `alertdialog` for an interruption that needs an answer (see `ConfirmDialog`). Default `dialog`. |
| `container` | `Element \| DocumentFragment \| null` | no |  | Where the modal is portaled. Defaults to `document.body`. Pass an element of the same document, for example a preview frame; a container inside another document (an iframe) is not supported. |
| `scrollContainerSelectors` | `readonly string[]` | no |  | Inner scroll containers to lock instead of the document, for app shells that scroll an inner pane. |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

#### `notifyTopModalDialogChanged`

Tells the store of open modal dialogs to look again. The package calls it itself when it closes or removes a native `Modal` (`renderAs="dialog"`): a dialog React removes is detached before its `open` attribute changes, so the attribute observer cannot see it. Public for an app that opens or closes its own native `<dialog>` and wants anything following the topmost dialog (the `ToastProvider` region that moves into it) to update at once. Cheap and safe to call at any time; it does nothing when nothing is listening.

```ts
notifyTopModalDialogChanged(): void
```

### Types

- `ModalClassNames`: `{ layer?: string | undefined; backdrop?: string | undefined; frame?: string | undefined; panel?: string | undefined; header?: string | undefined; title?: string | undefined; description?: string | undefined; body?: string | undefined; footer?: string | undefined; close?: string | undefined; }`
- `ModalSize`: `"sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl"`

### Example

```tsx
import { Modal } from "@lufia/design-system/components/Modal";

<Modal
  open={open}
  onClose={() => setOpen(false)}
  title="Edit project"
  description="Rename the project or change who can see it."
  footer={
    <>
      <button onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Cancel</button>
      <button onClick={save}>Save changes</button>
    </>
  }
>
  <form>...</form>
</Modal>;
```

### Accessibility

Follows the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices pattern: [Dialog (modal)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/).

- `role="dialog"` (or `alertdialog`), `aria-modal="true"`, `aria-labelledby` the title and `aria-describedby` the description when there is one.
- The page behind is made `inert` and page scroll is locked, so neither keyboard, pointer nor screen reader can reach it. The notification region of `ToastProvider` stays live.
- The dialog is the scroll container, with the header and footer sticky. Long content scrolls with the arrow keys while focus is on the dialog, with no extra tab stop.
- Close button: 36 px on desktop and 44 px on phones. Focus is always visible. Under `forced-colors` the border uses `CanvasText`.
- Motion uses `--lufia-motion-duration-enter` (240 ms) and `-exit` (160 ms), scale on desktop and rise on phones. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` it appears and disappears at once.
- Choose the initial focus deliberately. The default (the dialog) is safe for informational content; for a destructive prompt focus the safe action (`ConfirmDialog` does).

### Motion

Its stylesheet has a `prefers-reduced-motion` branch.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-border-width-thin`, `--lufia-color-bg-canvas`, `--lufia-color-bg-surface-raised`, `--lufia-color-bg-surface-solid`, `--lufia-color-border-strong`, `--lufia-color-border-subtle`, `--lufia-color-focus-ring`, `--lufia-color-text-default`, `--lufia-color-text-muted`, `--lufia-font-family-display`, `--lufia-font-line-height-normal`, `--lufia-font-line-height-tight`, `--lufia-font-size-md`, `--lufia-font-weight-semibold`, `--lufia-modal-backdrop`, `--lufia-modal-body-padding`, `--lufia-modal-close-size`, `--lufia-modal-footer-padding`, `--lufia-modal-header-padding`, `--lufia-modal-radius`, `--lufia-modal-scroll-shadow`, `--lufia-modal-sheet-offset`, `--lufia-modal-sheet-radius`, `--lufia-modal-size`, `--lufia-modal-title-size`, `--lufia-motion-distance-rise`, `--lufia-motion-distance-travel`, `--lufia-motion-duration-enter`, `--lufia-motion-duration-instant`, `--lufia-motion-easing-out`, `--lufia-opacity-disabled`, `--lufia-radius-md`, `--lufia-radius-panel`, `--lufia-shadow-lg`, `--lufia-space-12`, `--lufia-space-2`, `--lufia-space-3`, `--lufia-space-4`, `--lufia-space-5`, `--lufia-z-modal`, `--lufia-z-overlay`.

### Content guidelines

Titles say what the dialog is for ("Edit project", "Delete invoice 2041?"), not "Are you sure?". Buttons say what they do
("Save changes"), not "OK". Put the primary action last and the cancel action before it; on phones the order reverses so the
primary action sits on top.

- `components-overlays-modal--open-by-default`
- `components-overlays-modal--with-description`
- `components-overlays-modal--small`

- `components-overlays-modal--extra-large`
- `components-overlays-modal--long-content`
- `components-overlays-modal--long-title`

- `components-overlays-modal--busy-while-saving`

- `components-overlays-modal--focus-first-element`
- `components-overlays-modal--title-ellipsis`
- `components-overlays-modal--scroll-shadow`
- `components-overlays-modal--sticky-content-under-header`
- `components-overlays-modal--custom-size`
- `components-overlays-modal--part-class-names`
- `components-overlays-modal--themed-by-variables`
- `components-overlays-modal--top-sheet-on-phone`

## MoreActions

> An overflow menu that collects the secondary actions of a row or a page.

- Status: beta
- Category: Actions
- Import: `import { MoreActions } from "@lufia/design-system/components/MoreActions"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/MoreActions](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/MoreActions)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-actions-moreactions--docs)

### Purpose

An overflow menu: a button that opens a list of less frequent actions. It follows the WAI-ARIA menu button pattern.

### When to use

- Infrequent or secondary actions for a record, a row or a page, behind one button.
- Page actions that no longer fit on a narrow screen (`PageActions` does this for you).

### When not to use

- Navigation between pages: use `PeerNav` or the app shell.
- Two or three actions that fit: show them as buttons.
- Choosing a value (a select or combobox) or a form's submit.
- The only way to reach an important action. Keep the main action visible.

### API

#### `MoreActions`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | yes |  | Accessible name of the trigger and of the menu, such as "More actions". |
| `items` | `readonly MoreActionItem[]` | yes |  |  |
| `align` | `"end" \| "start"` | no | `"end"` | Which edge of the trigger the menu lines up with. Defaults to the end. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | no | `"md"` |  |
| `variant` | `"primary" \| "secondary" \| "ghost" \| "danger"` | no | `"ghost"` |  |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Replaces the default three-dot icon. |
| `presentation` | `"popover" \| "sheet" \| "auto"` | no | `"popover"` | How the open menu is shown. `"popover"` (default) hangs it from the button. `"sheet"` shows it as a full-width sheet anchored to the bottom of the viewport, over a backdrop that covers the whole page, with the page behind made inert. `"auto"` is a sheet below 60rem (the `medium` breakpoint) and a popover from there up. |
| `narrowOnlyScope` | `"container" \| "viewport"` | no | `"viewport"` | What decides when a `narrowOnly` item shows. `"viewport"` (default) is the page width: below 48rem. `"container"` is the width of the nearest ancestor that declares `container-type: inline-size`: below 50rem. A sheet is portalled to the body and leaves that container, so in `"container"` scope a sheet always shows `narrowOnly` items. A popover is portalled too: it reads the container's width when it opens (and on resize) instead. `PageActions` sets this from its `collapse` prop. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Renders the menu open on first paint. For documentation and tests; people open it themselves. A popover opens without moving focus; a sheet is modal, so it always moves focus to its first item. |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Example

```tsx
import { MoreActions } from "@lufia/design-system/components/MoreActions";

<MoreActions
  label="More actions"
  items={[
    { key: "dup", label: "Duplicate", onSelect: duplicate },
    { key: "settings", label: "Settings", href: "/settings" },
    { key: "del", label: "Delete record", tone: "danger", onSelect: confirmDelete },
  ]}
/>;
```

### Accessibility

Follows the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices pattern: [Menu button](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menu-button/).

Keyboard:

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Enter / Space / Down arrow | Trigger \| Opens the menu and focuses the first item |
| Up arrow | Trigger \| Opens the menu and focuses the last item |
| Down / Up arrow | Menu \| Next / previous item, wrapping; disabled items are included |
| Home / End | Menu \| First / last item |
| A letter or letters | Menu \| Typeahead: jumps to the next item starting with them; resets after 0.5s |
| Enter / Space | Item \| Activates the item, closes the menu, and returns focus to the trigger |
| Escape | Menu \| Closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger |
| Tab | Menu \| Closes the menu, returns focus to the button, moves on from it |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Sheet \| Next / previous item, wrapping: focus stays in the sheet |

- The trigger is an `IconButton` named by `label`, with `aria-haspopup="menu"`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`.
