- The list is `role="menu"` with `role="menuitem"` entries; focus moves between items (roving focus) and returns to the trigger on close or selection.
- Disabled items are `aria-disabled`: they stay focusable and readable (APG) but cannot be activated.
- Choosing a link item also returns focus to the button. The popover flips to the other edge of the button when it would run past the viewport, and opens upward when there is no room below. With no items, no button is rendered.
- A destructive item (`tone="danger"`) is styled red, but its label must say what it does ("Delete record"), since colour never carries the meaning alone.
- A sheet traps focus, makes the page behind inert and restores focus to the button; the visible heading repeats the menu's name and is hidden from assistive technology. Under reduced motion it appears without the slide and fade.
- Items are at least 2.5rem tall, 3rem on narrow screens. The menu is limited to the viewport width and wraps long labels.
- In forced-colors mode the menu border is `CanvasText` and the focus ring `Highlight`. Under reduced motion the menu appears without the fade.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has a `prefers-reduced-motion` branch.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-border-width-thick`, `--lufia-border-width-thin`, `--lufia-color-accent-subtle`, `--lufia-color-bg-canvas`, `--lufia-color-bg-surface-solid`, `--lufia-color-border-subtle`, `--lufia-color-focus-ring`, `--lufia-color-status-danger-bg`, `--lufia-color-status-danger-fg`, `--lufia-color-text-default`, `--lufia-color-text-muted`, `--lufia-font-line-height-normal`, `--lufia-font-size-md`, `--lufia-font-size-sm`, `--lufia-font-size-xs`, `--lufia-motion-distance-nudge`, `--lufia-motion-duration-enter`, `--lufia-motion-easing-out`, `--lufia-opacity-disabled`, `--lufia-overlay-z`, `--lufia-radius-md`, `--lufia-radius-panel`, `--lufia-radius-sm`, `--lufia-shadow-lg`, `--lufia-sheet-backdrop`, `--lufia-sheet-max-block-size`, `--lufia-sheet-max-inline-size`, `--lufia-z-dropdown`, `--lufia-z-modal`.

### Content guidelines

Items start with a verb and are one to three words. Put the destructive item last. Descriptions are optional and one short
phrase.

### Stories

- `components-actions-moreactions--default`
- `components-actions-moreactions--open`
- `components-actions-moreactions--aligned-to-start`
- `components-actions-moreactions--secondary`
- `components-actions-moreactions--long-labels`
- `components-actions-moreactions--phone-320`
- `components-actions-moreactions--phone-390`
- `components-actions-moreactions--right-to-left`
- `components-actions-moreactions--all-themes`
- `components-actions-moreactions--sheet`
- `components-actions-moreactions--sheet-mixed-icons`
- `components-actions-moreactions--sheet-without-icons`
- `components-actions-moreactions--sheet-many-items`
- `components-actions-moreactions--auto-phone-390`
- `components-actions-moreactions--sheet-phone-320`
- `components-actions-moreactions--sheet-over-dock`
- `components-actions-moreactions--open-a-dialog-from-a-menu-item`
- `components-actions-moreactions--in-clipping-card-near-bottom`
- `components-actions-moreactions--in-clipping-card-near-top`
- `components-actions-moreactions--container-scope-narrow-host`

## NavRow

> A row that links to a destination, for lists of places and settings.

- Status: beta
- Category: Navigation
- Import: `import { NavRow } from "@lufia/design-system/components/NavRow"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/NavRow](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/NavRow)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-navigation-navrow--docs)

### Purpose

A compact, clickable list row: an optional icon, a title with an optional badge, a description and a meta line, and a
trailing chevron. It is the row used to open a detail, a sub-page or a modal from a list of destinations.

### When to use

- A list of destinations where each needs a title and a sentence of context.

### When not to use

- Tabular data (use a table), or a row with several independent actions (a row can only have one target).

### API

#### `NavRow`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | yes |  |  |
| `description` | `string` | no |  | Supporting line under the title. |
| `meta` | `string` | no |  | Quiet last line: a date, a count, a status in words. |
| `badge` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Short trailing mark beside the title, such as a count. |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Decorative icon before the text; hidden from assistive technology. |
| `href` | `string` | no |  | Makes the row a link, rendered through the configured `linkComponent`. |
| `onClick` | `(event: MouseEvent<HTMLElement, MouseEvent>) => void` | no |  | Makes the row a button when there is no `href`. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | no | `false` |  |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Example

```tsx
import { NavRow } from "@lufia/design-system/components/NavRow";

<ul>
  <li>
    <NavRow
      title="Members"
      description="Invite people"
      meta="12 active"
      badge={12}
      icon={<UsersIcon />}
      href="/members"
    />
  </li>
  <li>
    <NavRow title="Export" onClick={openExport} />
  </li>
</ul>;
```

### Accessibility

- A link row is announced as a link and a button row as a button. The accessible name is the visible text, in reading order (title, badge, description, meta), so there is no `aria-label` to drift from what people see. Pass your own `aria-label` only when it contains the visible text.
- Icon and chevron are decorative. The chevron mirrors in right-to-left layouts.
- A disabled link has `aria-disabled`, leaves the tab order and ignores clicks; a disabled button is natively disabled. Disabled rows read at reduced contrast by design; keep the reason in the meta line.
- Keyboard: Tab to reach it, Enter follows a link, Enter or Space activates a button. Focus shows a 2px ring. Minimum height is 3.5rem, well above the 24px target size.
- Put rows in a `ul` so a screen reader announces the count.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-border-width-thick`, `--lufia-border-width-thin`, `--lufia-color-bg-surface`, `--lufia-color-bg-surface-raised`, `--lufia-color-border-strong`, `--lufia-color-border-subtle`, `--lufia-color-focus-ring`, `--lufia-color-text-default`, `--lufia-color-text-muted`, `--lufia-font-size-sm`, `--lufia-font-size-xs`, `--lufia-font-weight-bold`, `--lufia-motion-duration-instant`, `--lufia-motion-easing-out`, `--lufia-opacity-disabled`, `--lufia-radius-card`, `--lufia-radius-control`, `--lufia-radius-sm`, `--lufia-space-2`.

### Content guidelines

Titles are a noun or a short verb phrase. The description adds context and is never the only place for essential
information. Meta is for facts that change (a date, a count in words).

### Stories

- `components-navigation-navrow--as-link`
- `components-navigation-navrow--as-button`
- `components-navigation-navrow--static`
- `components-navigation-navrow--title-only`
- `components-navigation-navrow--disabled`
- `components-navigation-navrow--long-text`
- `components-navigation-navrow--phone-320`
- `components-navigation-navrow--right-to-left`
- `components-navigation-navrow--in-a-list`
- `components-navigation-navrow--all-themes`

## NotificationCenter

> A bell with an unread count that opens a panel of notifications: a popover on wide pages, a sheet on narrow ones.

- Status: beta
- Category: Overlays
- Import: `import { NotificationCenter, NotificationPanel, NotificationSummary } from "@lufia/design-system/components/NotificationCenter"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/NotificationCenter](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/NotificationCenter)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-overlays-notificationcenter--docs)

### Purpose

A bell button with an unread count that opens a panel of notifications. On wide pages the panel hangs from the bell as a
non-modal popover; below 60rem it is a modal bottom sheet. The data and every string come from the caller: the package has
no i18n and no data layer.

### When to use

- A feed of things that happened or need a decision, with an unread state, reachable from anywhere in an app.

### When not to use

- A single transient confirmation: use `Toast`.
- Blocking questions: use `Modal` or `ConfirmDialog`.
- A page-length activity log with no unread state: use `ActivityList`.

### Exports

| Name | Kind |
| --- | --- |
| `NotificationCenter` | component |
| `NotificationPanel` | component |
| `NotificationSummary` | component |

### API

#### `NotificationCenter`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | yes |  | The panel's heading and, on a landmark panel, its accessible name ("Notifications"). |
| `unreadCount` | `number` | yes |  | How many notifications are unread, across every tab. Drives the badge, "Mark all as read" and the live region. |
| `unreadLabel` | `string` | yes |  | Read before the title of an unread row, so the state is not carried by the dot alone ("unread"). |
| `unreadCountLabel` | `(count: number) => string` | yes |  | Says a count in words ("4 unread"). Used for the hidden text of the badge and the live region. |
| `tabs` | `readonly NotificationTab[]` | no |  | The tabs, in order. Without them the panel is one list. Tabs are the caller's: "All", "Approvals", "Stock". |
| `activeTab` | `string` | no |  | Key of the chosen tab. Controlled. |
| `defaultActiveTab` | `string` | no |  | Initial tab when `activeTab` is not given. Defaults to the first. |
| `onTabChange` | `(key: string) => void` | no |  | Called with the key of the tab the person chose. |
| `items` | `readonly NotificationItem[]` | yes |  | Every notification, newest first. Tabs and groups pick from this one list. |
| `groups` | `readonly NotificationGroup[]` | no |  | The headings, in order. Items are placed by `NotificationItem.group`. Without groups the list has no headings. |
| `summary` | `ReactNode` | no |  | A highlight above the list, usually a `NotificationSummary`. It shows under every tab. |
| `onMarkAllRead` | `() => void` | no |  | Runs when "Mark all as read" is pressed. The button shows when this and `markAllLabel` are set. |
| `markAllLabel` | `string` | no |  | Text of the mark-all action ("Mark all as read"). |
| `footer` | `NotificationFooter` | no |  | The link or button at the bottom ("Notification settings"), with a chevron. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | no |  | Shows skeleton rows in place of the list. |
| `loadingLabel` | `string` | no |  | Name of the loading state, read once as a polite status ("Loading notifications"). |
| `empty` | `NotificationEmpty` | no |  | What to show when the chosen tab has no items. A tab's own `empty` wins. |
| `error` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Replaces the list when loading failed. It is announced as an alert; include the way to retry. |
| `open` | `boolean` | no |  | Open state. Controlled: pair it with `onOpenChange`. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Initial open state when `open` is not given. For documentation and tests; people open it themselves. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` | no |  |  |
| `presentation` | `"popover" \| "sheet" \| "auto"` | no | `"auto"` | How the open panel is shown. `"popover"` hangs it from the bell as a non-modal dialog. `"sheet"` shows it as a modal bottom sheet over a backdrop that covers the page. `"auto"` (default) is a sheet below 60rem (the `medium` breakpoint) and a popover from there up. |
| `align` | `"end" \| "start"` | no | `"end"` | Which edge of the bell the popover lines up with. Defaults to the end. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | no | `"md"` |  |
| `variant` | `"primary" \| "secondary" \| "ghost" \| "danger"` | no | `"ghost"` |  |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Replaces the default bell icon. |
| `maxCount` | `number` | no | `99` | Counts above this show as "99+". Default 99. |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

#### `NotificationPanel`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | yes |  | The panel's heading and, on a landmark panel, its accessible name ("Notifications"). |
| `unreadCount` | `number` | yes |  | How many notifications are unread, across every tab. Drives the badge, "Mark all as read" and the live region. |
| `unreadLabel` | `string` | yes |  | Read before the title of an unread row, so the state is not carried by the dot alone ("unread"). |
| `unreadCountLabel` | `(count: number) => string` | yes |  | Says a count in words ("4 unread"). Used for the hidden text of the badge and the live region. |
| `tabs` | `readonly NotificationTab[]` | no |  | The tabs, in order. Without them the panel is one list. Tabs are the caller's: "All", "Approvals", "Stock". |
| `activeTab` | `string` | no |  | Key of the chosen tab. Controlled. |
| `defaultActiveTab` | `string` | no |  | Initial tab when `activeTab` is not given. Defaults to the first. |
| `onTabChange` | `(key: string) => void` | no |  | Called with the key of the tab the person chose. |
| `items` | `readonly NotificationItem[]` | yes |  | Every notification, newest first. Tabs and groups pick from this one list. |
| `groups` | `readonly NotificationGroup[]` | no |  | The headings, in order. Items are placed by `NotificationItem.group`. Without groups the list has no headings. |
| `summary` | `ReactNode` | no |  | A highlight above the list, usually a `NotificationSummary`. It shows under every tab. |
| `onMarkAllRead` | `() => void` | no |  | Runs when "Mark all as read" is pressed. The button shows when this and `markAllLabel` are set. |
| `markAllLabel` | `string` | no |  | Text of the mark-all action ("Mark all as read"). |
| `footer` | `NotificationFooter` | no |  | The link or button at the bottom ("Notification settings"), with a chevron. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Shows skeleton rows in place of the list. |
| `loadingLabel` | `string` | no |  | Name of the loading state, read once as a polite status ("Loading notifications"). |
| `empty` | `NotificationEmpty` | no |  | What to show when the chosen tab has no items. A tab's own `empty` wins. |
| `error` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Replaces the list when loading failed. It is announced as an alert; include the way to retry. |
| `onClose` | `() => void` | no |  | Adds a close button to the header, for a panel shown as a sheet. |
| `onAction` | `(run: () => void) => void` | no |  | Receives what a row, the footer or the summary's action is about to do, so a host can close itself first and run it once focus is back where it belongs. Omit it and the action runs at once. |
| `titleId` | `string` | no |  | Id of the heading, for a host that names its dialog with it. Generated when omitted. |
| `landmark` | `boolean` | no | `true` | Whether the root is a labelled region (`<section>`). Default `true`. A host that already names the panel, such as the dialog of `NotificationCenter`, sets `false` to get a plain element. |
| `announce` | `boolean` | no | `true` | Renders the polite live region that announces changes of `unreadCount`. Default `true`; a host that has its own turns it off. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLElement>` | no |  |  |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

#### `NotificationSummary`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | yes |  | The headline ("2 proposals due today"). |
| `description` | `string` | no |  | One line under the headline. |
| `progress` | `{ done: number; total: number; label: string; valueText?: string \| undefined; }` | no |  | A segmented bar: `done` of `total` segments are filled. It is a native `progressbar`, so `label` names it. |
| `action` | `{ label: string; href?: string \| undefined; onSelect?: (() => void) \| undefined; }` | no |  | The one primary action: a link with `href`, a button otherwise. |
| `footnote` | `string` | no |  | Small print under the action ("2 due today · 6 later this week"). |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `NotificationEmpty`: `{ title: string; description?: string | undefined; icon?: ReactNode; action?: ReactNode; }`
- `NotificationFooter`: `{ label: string; href?: string | undefined; onSelect?: (() => void) | undefined; }`
- `NotificationGroup`: `{ key: string; label: string; }`
- `NotificationItem`: `{ id: string; group?: string | undefined; tab?: string | undefined; title: string; meta?: ReactNode; time?: ReactNode; icon?: ReactNode; avatar?: ReactNode; unread?: boolean | undefined; href?: string | undefined; onSelect?: (() => void) | undefined; }`
- `NotificationTab`: `{ key: string; label: string; count?: number | undefined; all?: boolean | undefined; empty?: NotificationEmpty | undefined; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { NotificationCenter, NotificationSummary } from "@lufia/design-system/components/NotificationCenter";

<NotificationCenter
  label="Notifications"
  unreadCount={5}
  unreadLabel="unread"
  unreadCountLabel={(count) => `${count} unread`}
  tabs={[
    { key: "all", label: "All", count: 8, all: true },
    { key: "approvals", label: "Approvals", count: 5 },
  ]}
  groups={[
    { key: "today", label: "Today" },
    { key: "earlier", label: "Earlier" },
  ]}
  items={[
    {
      id: "1",
      group: "today",
      tab: "approvals",
      title: "Supplier proposal needs your review",
      meta: "Procurement assistant",
      time: "07:52",
      unread: true,
      href: "/proposals/1",
    },
  ]}
  summary={
    <NotificationSummary title="2 proposals due today" action={{ label: "Review", href: "/review" }} />
  }
  markAllLabel="Mark all as read"
  onMarkAllRead={markAllRead}
  footer={{ label: "Notification settings", href: "/settings" }}
  empty={{ title: "You are all caught up" }}
/>;
```

### Accessibility

Follows the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices pattern: [Tabs](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tabs/).

Keyboard:

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Enter / Space | Bell \| Opens or closes the panel; focus moves into the panel |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Popover \| Moves through the panel's controls in order; the popover stays open |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Sheet \| Moves through the sheet's controls, wrapping: focus stays in the sheet |
| Left / Right arrow | Tabs \| Previous / next tab, wrapping; the tab is chosen as it takes focus |
| Home / End | Tabs \| First / last tab |
| Enter / Space | Row, buttons \| Activates the row (and closes the panel), "Mark all as read" or the footer |
| Escape | Popover, sheet \| Closes the panel and returns focus to the bell |

- The bell is a button named by `label` and the count, "Notifications, 4 unread", with `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`. The visible count repeats the name and is hidden from assistive technology.
- The popover is a non-modal `role="dialog"` labelled by its heading. Focus moves to it on open; Escape returns focus to the bell. The sheet is `aria-modal`, traps focus and makes the page behind inert.
- Tabs follow the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern with automatic activation and one shared `tabpanel` that lists the chosen tab's items. The arrow keys mirror in right-to-left text. A row of tabs that does not fit scrolls sideways, and the edge that hides more fades.
- Each group is a heading and a list. Unread rows say so in text (`unreadLabel`, read before the title), not by the dot or the tint alone. Rows are links or buttons, so the whole row is the target and is at least 3.5rem tall.
- A polite live region announces changes of `unreadCount` ("Notifications, 5 unread"). It says nothing on first paint.
- "Mark all as read" stays focusable and is `aria-disabled` when nothing is unread, so focus is not lost when the last one is read.
- Loading is one polite status with skeleton rows; a failure is an alert.
- In forced-colors mode the unread dot and the row's start edge use `Highlight`, the selected tab keeps its underline and the summary's progress segments draw with borders.

### Motion

Motion uses the package's tokens and primitives and only moves `transform` and `opacity`. Every piece collapses under
`prefers-reduced-motion`: the panel simply appears and disappears, and nothing is hidden.

| Moment                         | What happens                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The panel opens                | It grows out of the bell's corner (scale 0.96 to 1 with a fade). A sheet slides up, as the `MoreActions` sheet |
| The panel closes               | A shorter fade and a slight shrink (`--lufia-motion-duration-exit`), then it unmounts; it is inert meanwhile   |
| The first view of the panel    | Rows rise in a short step apart, the same sequence as the `Stagger` primitive, capped at six steps             |
| A tab changes                  | The indicator slides to the tab (`useSlidingIndicator`) and the list crossfades; rows do not re-enter          |
| The unread count changes       | The bell's badge counts with `AnimatedNumber` and pops; tab and header counts flash with `ChangeHighlight`     |
| A notification arrives         | The new row enters at the top and flashes once; nothing moves for rows that were already there                 |
| "Mark all as read"             | Each unread dot scales and fades out and the row tint fades, from top to bottom, 40 ms apart                   |
| The highlight card first shows | Its progress segments fill one after another                                                                   |

Nothing animates on first paint of a closed bell, and a re-render never replays an entrance. Try it in **Interactive**: open
the panel, switch tabs, mark everything read and simulate an arrival.

Its stylesheet has a `prefers-reduced-motion` branch.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-border-width-thin`, `--lufia-color-accent-default`, `--lufia-color-bg-canvas`, `--lufia-color-bg-surface-solid`, `--lufia-color-border-strong`, `--lufia-color-border-subtle`, `--lufia-color-text-on-accent`, `--lufia-font-family-body`, `--lufia-font-size-2xs`, `--lufia-font-weight-bold`, `--lufia-motion-distance-nudge`, `--lufia-motion-duration-enter`, `--lufia-motion-duration-exit`, `--lufia-motion-easing-in`, `--lufia-motion-easing-out`, `--lufia-overlay-z`, `--lufia-radius-full`, `--lufia-radius-panel`, `--lufia-shadow-lg`, `--lufia-sheet-backdrop`, `--lufia-sheet-max-block-size`, `--lufia-sheet-max-inline-size`, `--lufia-z-dropdown`, `--lufia-z-modal`.

### Content guidelines

Titles say what happened in one line. The meta line names the source; the time is formatted for the locale by the caller.
Keep tab labels to one word and the number of tabs to four or five. The `unreadLabel` is one word ("unread").

### Stories

- `components-overlays-notificationcenter--default`
- `components-overlays-notificationcenter--open`
- `components-overlays-notificationcenter--with-summary`
- `components-overlays-notificationcenter--loading`
- `components-overlays-notificationcenter--empty`
- `components-overlays-notificationcenter--failed`
- `components-overlays-notificationcenter--many-items`
- `components-overlays-notificationcenter--sheet-phone-390`
- `components-overlays-notificationcenter--sheet-phone-320`
- `components-overlays-notificationcenter--sheet-over-dock`
- `components-overlays-notificationcenter--dark`
- `components-overlays-notificationcenter--interactive`
- `components-overlays-notificationcenter--panel-only`

## PageActions

> The action bar of a page: one primary action, the rest collapsed on narrow screens.

- Status: beta
- Category: Actions
- Import: `import { PageActions } from "@lufia/design-system/components/PageActions"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/PageActions](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/PageActions)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-actions-pageactions--docs)

### Purpose

The action row of a page: one primary action, a few secondary ones, and an overflow menu. It is meant for the `actions` slot
of `PageHeader`.

### When to use

- The actions that apply to the whole page: create, import, share, export.

### When not to use

- Actions on one row or card: use `IconButton` or `MoreActions` there.
- More than one primary action.
- Navigation between views: use `PeerNav`.

### API

#### `PageActions`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `primary` | `PageActionItem` | no |  | The one main action of the page. Always visible. |
| `secondary` | `readonly PageActionItem[]` | no | `[]` | Frequent actions. Visible on wide screens; on narrow ones they move into the overflow menu. |
| `overflow` | `readonly MoreActionItem[]` | no | `[]` | Infrequent actions. Always in the overflow menu. |
| `moreLabel` | `string` | yes |  | Accessible name of the overflow menu button, such as "More actions". |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md"` | no | `"md"` | Size of the primary and secondary buttons and of the menu button. Defaults to `"md"`; `"sm"` suits compact headers. |
| `collapse` | `"container" \| "viewport"` | no | `"viewport"` | What collapses the secondary actions into the overflow menu. `"viewport"` (default) is the page width: below 48rem. `"container"` is the width of the nearest ancestor that declares `container-type: inline-size`: below 50rem. The host must declare it; without one the secondary actions never collapse, and with no `overflow` items the menu button stays visible with nothing in it, so always give this mode a host container. There is no container name and no threshold prop, because a container condition cannot read a variable. Pure CSS in both cases, so there is no flash on first paint. |
| `hideBelow` | `"medium"` | no |  | `"medium"` hides the whole row below 60rem, for a page whose app shell shows the actions elsewhere on narrow screens. Pure CSS, so there is no flash on first paint. Omit it to keep the row at every width. |
| `primaryPlacement` | `"inline" \| "external"` | no | `"inline"` | Where the primary action is rendered. `"inline"` (default) keeps it in the row. `"external"` hides it in the row below 60rem (the `medium` breakpoint), because the app shell renders it there, for example in a floating bar; it stays inline on wider screens. The secondary actions and the menu are not affected. |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `PageActionItem`: `{ key: string; label: string; icon?: ReactNode; href?: string | undefined; onSelect?: (() => void) | undefined; disabled?: boolean | undefined; hint?: string | undefined; attributes?: Record<'data-${string}', string> | undefined; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { PageActions } from "@lufia/design-system/components/PageActions";

<PageActions
  moreLabel="More actions"
  primary={{ key: "new", label: "New report", onSelect: create }}
  secondary={[{ key: "share", label: "Share", onSelect: share }]}
  overflow={[{ key: "del", label: "Delete all", tone: "danger", onSelect: confirmDeleteAll }]}
/>;
```

### Accessibility

Keyboard:

Buttons follow `Button`; the menu follows `MoreActions` (arrow keys, Home, End, typeahead, Escape). See both pages.

- Every control is a native button or link, or the menu from `MoreActions`; the menu button is named by `moreLabel`.
- On narrow screens an action is reachable in the menu only, so keep labels meaningful out of context.
- A hinted disabled action is `aria-disabled`, not `disabled`, so it takes focus and announces its reason.
- The row does not wrap, so it never pushes content around when it collapses.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Its stylesheet reads no `--lufia-*` tokens directly (no CSS module, or it composes other components).

### Content guidelines

Verbs first, one to three words. Put the destructive action last in the menu and label it explicitly.

### Stories

- `components-actions-pageactions--default`
- `components-actions-pageactions--primary-only`
- `components-actions-pageactions--secondary-only`
- `components-actions-pageactions--overflow-only`
- `components-actions-pageactions--primary-as-link`
- `components-actions-pageactions--disabled`
- `components-actions-pageactions--disabled-with-hint`
- `components-actions-pageactions--small`
- `components-actions-pageactions--external-primary`
- `components-actions-pageactions--hidden-below-medium`
- `components-actions-pageactions--container-narrow`
- `components-actions-pageactions--container-wide`
- `components-actions-pageactions--with-data-attributes`
- `components-actions-pageactions--in-page-header`
- `components-actions-pageactions--phone-320`
- `components-actions-pageactions--phone-390`
- `components-actions-pageactions--right-to-left`
- `components-actions-pageactions--all-themes`

## PageHeader

> The title row of a page with eyebrow, description and actions.

- Status: beta
- Category: Navigation
- Import: `import { PageHeader } from "@lufia/design-system/components/PageHeader"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/PageHeader](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/PageHeader)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-navigation-pageheader--docs)

### Purpose

The top of a page: an optional eyebrow, the title as a heading, a description, and the page's actions.

### When to use

- The first element of the main content of a page.
- A section heading with its own actions (`headingLevel={2}`).

### When not to use

- The heading of a card or dialog: `Card` and `Modal` have their own.
- A marketing hero.

### API

#### `PageHeader`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eyebrow` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Small line above the title: the section or the parent record. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | yes |  |  |
| `headingLevel` | `2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6 \| 1` | no | `1` | Heading level of `title`. Defaults to 1: a page has one. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` | no |  |  |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Page-level actions, usually a `PageActions`. They wrap under the text on narrow screens. |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `PageHeaderProps`: `Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>, "title"> & { eyebrow?: ReactNode; title: ReactNode; headingLevel?: 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 1 | undefined; description?: ReactNode; actions?: ReactNode; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { PageHeader } from "@lufia/design-system/components/PageHeader";

<PageHeader
  eyebrow="Reports"
  title="Quarterly overview"
  description="Totals for the period."
  actions={<Button variant="primary">New report</Button>}
/>;
```

### Accessibility

Keyboard:

The header is not interactive. Its actions follow the keyboard behaviour of the controls you pass.

- The title is a real heading. A page should have one level 1; use `headingLevel` for secondary headers so the outline stays in order.
- The eyebrow is a paragraph above the heading, not part of its name.
- Text contrast is checked in every theme. At 320px the title wraps instead of overflowing.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-border-width-thin`, `--lufia-color-text-default`, `--lufia-color-text-muted`, `--lufia-color-text-subtle`, `--lufia-font-family-display`, `--lufia-font-family-mono`, `--lufia-font-line-height-normal`, `--lufia-font-line-height-tight`, `--lufia-font-size-2xl`, `--lufia-font-size-3xl`, `--lufia-font-size-sm`, `--lufia-font-size-xs`, `--lufia-font-weight-bold`, `--lufia-font-weight-semibold`, `--lufia-page-header-eyebrow-color`, `--lufia-page-header-eyebrow-dash-gap`, `--lufia-page-header-eyebrow-dash-size`, `--lufia-page-header-eyebrow-dash-thickness`, `--lufia-page-header-eyebrow-tracking`, `--lufia-page-header-eyebrow-weight`, `--lufia-page-header-title-size`, `--lufia-page-header-title-tracking`.

### Content guidelines

A title names the page in one to four words. The description is one sentence of context, not instructions. Put at most one
primary action in `actions`.

### Stories

- `components-navigation-pageheader--default`
- `components-navigation-pageheader--title-only`
- `components-navigation-pageheader--without-actions`
- `components-navigation-pageheader--without-eyebrow`
- `components-navigation-pageheader--section-heading`
- `components-navigation-pageheader--long-text`
- `components-navigation-pageheader--themed-by-tokens`
- `components-navigation-pageheader--phone-320`
- `components-navigation-pageheader--phone-390`
- `components-navigation-pageheader--right-to-left`
- `components-navigation-pageheader--all-themes`

## Pagination

> Previous, next and numbered pages for long lists.

- Status: beta
- Category: Navigation
- Import: `import { Pagination } from "@lufia/design-system/components/Pagination"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/Pagination](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/Pagination)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-navigation-pagination--docs)

### Purpose

Page navigation for a list or table: previous and next, numbered pages that collapse into an ellipsis, and a status line.
It is the view for `usePagination`.

### When to use

- Long lists or tables that are paged. Prefer it to infinite scroll when people need to return to a position.

### When not to use

- Fewer than two pages, or feeds without a known end.

### API

#### `Pagination`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page` | `number` | yes |  | Current page, starting at 1. Controlled. |
| `totalPages` | `number` | yes |  |  |
| `total` | `number` | no |  | Total item count, handed to `labels.summary`. |
| `onPageChange` | `(page: number) => void` | yes |  |  |
| `hrefFor` | `(page: number) => string` | no |  | Makes every control a real link (through the configured `linkComponent`) so pages can be opened in a new tab and crawled. `onPageChange` still fires on a plain click; call `event.preventDefault()` there to handle it in place. |
| `siblingCount` | `number` | no | `1` | Page numbers shown on each side of the current one. Default 1. |
| `labels` | `PaginationLabels` | yes |  |  |
| `variant` | `"default" \| "compact"` | no | `"default"` | `default` shows the numbered pages (they give way to previous and next in containers under 40rem). `compact` is previous and next only, with the status line; the status line then carries the position at every width. |
| `buttonClassName` | `string` | no |  | A class for every control (previous, next and the page numbers), for an app that already has a button look. When set, the built-in control look is left out (layout, the current-page and disabled states stay), so your class is not fighting it. |
| `disabledMode` | `"aria" \| "native"` | no | `"aria"` | How an unavailable previous or next control is marked. `"aria"` (default) sets `aria-disabled` only, so the control keeps keyboard focus and the person is not thrown off it. `"native"` renders a real `disabled` attribute on the button (out of the tab order, and matched by `:disabled` selectors and test queries). Controls that are links (`hrefFor`) always use `aria-disabled`, since a link cannot be disabled. |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `PaginationLabels`: `{ nav: string; previous: string; next: string; page: (page: number) => string; summary: (page: number, totalPages: number, total?: number | undefined) => string; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { Pagination } from "@lufia/design-system/components/Pagination";
import { usePagination } from "@lufia/design-system/components/usePagination";

const { slice, page, totalPages, total, setPage } = usePagination(rows, 10);

<Pagination
  page={page}
  totalPages={totalPages}
  total={total}
  onPageChange={setPage}
  labels={{
    nav: "Results",
    previous: "Previous",
    next: "Next",
    page: (n) => `Page ${n}`,
    summary: (n, count, all) => `Page ${n} of ${count}, ${all} results`,
  }}
/>;
```

### Accessibility

Keyboard:

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves between previous, the page numbers and next |
| Enter (and Space on buttons) | Goes to the focused page |

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-border-width-thick`, `--lufia-border-width-thin`, `--lufia-color-accent-border`, `--lufia-color-accent-subtle`, `--lufia-color-bg-surface-raised`, `--lufia-color-border-subtle`, `--lufia-color-focus-ring`, `--lufia-color-text-accent`, `--lufia-color-text-default`, `--lufia-color-text-muted`, `--lufia-color-text-subtle`, `--lufia-font-size-sm`, `--lufia-font-weight-semibold`, `--lufia-motion-duration-instant`, `--lufia-motion-easing-out`, `--lufia-opacity-disabled`, `--lufia-radius-control`, `--lufia-space-1`, `--lufia-space-2`, `--lufia-space-3`, `--lufia-space-4`.

### Content guidelines

Keep the status line short and say what is paged: "Page 3 of 12, 118 results".

### Stories

- `components-navigation-pagination--default`
- `components-navigation-pagination--first-page`
- `components-navigation-pagination--last-page`
- `components-navigation-pagination--few-pages`
- `components-navigation-pagination--many-pages`
- `components-navigation-pagination--without-total`
- `components-navigation-pagination--more-siblings`
- `components-navigation-pagination--native-disabled`
- `components-navigation-pagination--compact`
- `components-navigation-pagination--compact-links`
- `components-navigation-pagination--custom-button-class`
- `components-navigation-pagination--as-links`
- `components-navigation-pagination--phone-320`
- `components-navigation-pagination--phone-390`
- `components-navigation-pagination--with-use-pagination`
- `components-navigation-pagination--all-themes`

## PeerNav

> Links or tabs for moving between sibling views of the same page.

- Status: beta
- Category: Navigation
- Import: `import { PeerNav } from "@lufia/design-system/components/PeerNav"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/PeerNav](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/PeerNav)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-navigation-peernav--docs)

### Purpose

A horizontal set of sibling views of one page, such as an overview and a work queue. Each item has a label and, optionally,
a description and an icon. An indicator slides to the chosen one.

### When to use

- Two to six peer views of one screen that share a heading and data.

### When not to use

- Page-level site navigation (use the app shell), steps in order (use `Stepper`), or a switch between two display modes.

### API

#### `PeerNav`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | yes |  | Accessible name of the navigation or the tablist. Required: there is usually more than one on a page. |
| `items` | `readonly PeerNavItem<Href>[]` | yes |  |  |
| `value` | `string` | no |  | Key of the current item. Controlled. For links it is the page being shown. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | no |  | Initial key when `value` is not given (tabs only; links follow the page). |
| `onValueChange` | `(key: string, event?: MouseEvent<HTMLElement, MouseEvent> \| undefined) => void` | no |  | Called when the person chooses another item. For links it fires on an unmodified primary click, before the browser navigates; call `event.preventDefault()` to take over (it is `undefined` for keyboard-selected tabs). |
| `layout` | `"auto" \| "fit" \| "scroll"` | no | `"auto"` | `"fit"` shares the width between the items; `"scroll"` keeps them readable and scrolls sideways with a fade on the edge that hides more. `"auto"` (default) scrolls from five items. |
| `onItemClick` | `(key: string, event: MouseEvent<HTMLElement, MouseEvent>) => void` | no |  | Called for every click on an enabled item: the current one and modified clicks (Ctrl, Cmd, Shift, Alt, middle button) included, before `onValueChange` and before the browser navigates. `onValueChange` only reports a real change. Call `event.preventDefault()` to take over: `onValueChange` is not called, the indicator stays where it is, a link is not followed and a tab is not selected. Links and tabs. |
| `phoneGrid` | `"row" \| "2x2"` | no | `"row"` | What four items do on a phone (narrower than 35rem, `fit` layout). `"row"` (default) keeps them in one row with the icon above the label; `"2x2"` wraps them into two rows of two so each label keeps its width. |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `PeerNavItem`: `{ key: string; label: string; description?: string | undefined; icon?: ReactNode; href?: Href | undefined; controls?: string | undefined; disabled?: boolean | undefined; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { PeerNav } from "@lufia/design-system/components/PeerNav";

<PeerNav
  label="Dashboard views"
  value="overview"
  items={[
    { key: "overview", label: "Overview", description: "Totals", icon: <GridIcon />, href: "/dashboard" },
    {
      key: "work",
      label: "Work",
      description: "Needs attention",
      icon: <InboxIcon />,
      href: "/dashboard/work",
    },
  ]}
/>;
```

### Accessibility

Follows the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices pattern: [Tabs](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tabs/).

Keyboard:

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves between links \| Enters and leaves the tablist (one stop) |
| Enter | Follows the focused link \| Selects the focused tab (it is a button) |
| Left / Right arrow | Not used \| Previous / next tab, wrapping; reversed in RTL |
| Home / End | Not used \| First / last tab |

- Always give `label`: a page often has several navigations or tablists.
- Icons are decorative. The description is part of the link's or tab's name.
- A click on a link moves the indicator and the chosen styling at once, but `aria-current` stays on the page shown until the route changes. Modified clicks (open in new tab) change nothing.
- Five or more items scroll sideways instead of shrinking; the current one is brought into view and a fade marks the edge that hides more. On narrow screens the description is hidden and the icon moves above the label.
- Target height is at least 3rem. Focus shows a 2px ring. The indicator slide uses `transform` only and is a no-op under `prefers-reduced-motion`. In forced-colors mode the active item keeps a `Highlight` border.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has a `prefers-reduced-motion` branch.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-border-width-thick`, `--lufia-border-width-thin`, `--lufia-color-accent-border`, `--lufia-color-accent-subtle`, `--lufia-color-bg-surface`, `--lufia-color-bg-surface-raised`, `--lufia-color-border-subtle`, `--lufia-color-focus-ring`, `--lufia-color-text-accent`, `--lufia-color-text-default`, `--lufia-color-text-muted`, `--lufia-color-text-subtle`, `--lufia-font-line-height-tight`, `--lufia-font-size-sm`, `--lufia-font-size-xs`, `--lufia-font-weight-bold`, `--lufia-motion-duration-enter`, `--lufia-motion-duration-instant`, `--lufia-motion-easing-out`, `--lufia-opacity-disabled`, `--lufia-peer-nav-active-icon-color`, `--lufia-peer-nav-description-line-height`, `--lufia-peer-nav-description-size`, `--lufia-peer-nav-disabled-opacity`, `--lufia-peer-nav-focus-width`, `--lufia-peer-nav-indicator-border`, `--lufia-peer-nav-indicator-shadow`, `--lufia-peer-nav-item-radius`, `--lufia-peer-nav-label-line-height`, `--lufia-peer-nav-label-size`, `--lufia-peer-nav-label-size-phone`, `--lufia-peer-nav-max-inline-size`, `--lufia-peer-nav-radius`, `--lufia-radius-card`, `--lufia-radius-control`, `--lufia-radius-md`, `--lufia-shadow-md`, `--lufia-space-2`.

### Content guidelines

Labels are one or two words. Descriptions are a short phrase and may be omitted; they disappear on phones.

### Stories

- `components-navigation-peernav--links`
- `components-navigation-peernav--tabs`
- `components-navigation-peernav--object-href`
- `components-navigation-peernav--without-descriptions`
- `components-navigation-peernav--without-icons`
- `components-navigation-peernav--two-views`
- `components-navigation-peernav--disabled-item`
- `components-navigation-peernav--many-items`
- `components-navigation-peernav--long-text`
- `components-navigation-peernav--phone-320`
- `components-navigation-peernav--phone-two-by-two`
- `components-navigation-peernav--themed-by-variables`
- `components-navigation-peernav--phone-390`
- `components-navigation-peernav--right-to-left`
- `components-navigation-peernav--all-themes`
- `components-navigation-peernav--all-themes-tabs`

## PendingSubmit

> A submit button that reads the pending state of its form and prevents double submits.

- Status: beta
- Category: Forms
- Import: `import { PendingSubmit } from "@lufia/design-system/components/PendingSubmit"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/PendingSubmit](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/PendingSubmit)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-forms-pendingsubmit--docs)

### Purpose

The submit button of a form that takes a moment. While the form is pending it cannot be submitted again, shows a ring and a
pending label, and for a long wait moves through further labels.

### When to use

- The primary submit action of any form that waits for a server, so it never looks idle while it works.

### When not to use

- A button that is not a form submit: it does not read form state. Use a regular button.
- Actions that need a determinate progress bar (uploads): show the bar next to the form and use `pending` for the button.

### API

#### `PendingSubmit`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | The label while idle ("Save changes"). |
| `pendingLabel` | `string` | yes |  | The label while the form is submitting ("Saving…"). It is announced to assistive technology. |
| `progress` | `PendingProgress` | no | `[]` | Labels that replace `pendingLabel` after a delay, for actions that can take long. |
| `pending` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Treat the button as pending although the form is not (yet). Use it to drive the button from `useActionState`, a `useTransition` or your own request state. It is combined with the form's own pending state. |
| `variant` | `"primary" \| "secondary" \| "ghost" \| "danger"` | no | `"primary"` | Look of the underlying `Button`. Default `"primary"`. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | no |  |  |
| `fullWidth` | `boolean` | no |  |  |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLButtonElement>` | no |  |  |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `PendingProgress`: `readonly (readonly [afterMs: number, label: string])[]`

### Example

```tsx
import { PendingSubmit } from "@lufia/design-system/components/PendingSubmit";

<form action={saveProject}>
  {/* fields */}
  <PendingSubmit pendingLabel="Saving…" progress={[[4000, "Still saving, this can take a moment…"]]}>
    Save changes
  </PendingSubmit>
</form>;
```

### Accessibility

- `aria-busy` and `aria-disabled` are set while pending (Button dims it, which is right while it waits). The button keeps its accessible name (the idle label).
- A live region next to the button (`role="status"`) announces `pendingLabel` when the wait starts and clears afterwards. It sits outside the button because a live region inside a button is often ignored.
- The ring and the progress labels are `aria-hidden`; the status carries the meaning. The ring stops under `prefers-reduced-motion` and the label still changes.
- The button keeps the width of its longest label (invisible copies reserve it), so it does not jump when the label changes.
- Target height is at least 44px; focus is a 2px ring.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-space-2`.

### Content guidelines

The idle label says what happens ("Save changes"), the pending label is the same verb in progress ("Saving…"), and a
progress label reassures ("Still saving, this can take a moment…"). Do not change the meaning between them, and do not leave the
button without a pending label.

### Stories

- `components-forms-pendingsubmit--default`
- `components-forms-pendingsubmit--secondary`
- `components-forms-pendingsubmit--pending`
- `components-forms-pendingsubmit--pending-secondary`
- `components-forms-pendingsubmit--with-progress`
- `components-forms-pendingsubmit--disabled`
- `components-forms-pendingsubmit--in-a-form`
- `components-forms-pendingsubmit--long-text`
- `components-forms-pendingsubmit--phone-320`
- `components-forms-pendingsubmit--right-to-left`
- `components-forms-pendingsubmit--all-themes`

## ProgressBar

> A determinate progress bar with a native progressbar role.

- Status: beta
- Category: Data display
- Import: `import { ProgressBar } from "@lufia/design-system/components/ProgressBar"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/ProgressBar](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/ProgressBar)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-data-display-progressbar--docs)

### Purpose

A determinate progress bar: a native `progressbar` role with its value, drawn as a track and a fill.

### When to use

- A known fraction of a whole: storage used, steps done, a quota.

### When not to use

- Work of unknown length: use a spinner or a `Skeleton`.
- A value against a target tick: use `BulletBar`.

### API

#### `ProgressBar`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `number` | yes |  | Current value, from 0 to `max`. Values outside the range are clamped. |
| `max` | `number` | no | `100` | The value that means done. Defaults to 100. |
| `label` | `string` | yes |  | Accessible name of the bar ("Storage used"). Required: a progress bar without a name is announced as a bare number. |
| `valueText` | `string` | no |  | Spoken instead of the percentage when the number alone is not enough ("12 of 40 steps"). |
| `tone` | `"accent" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "danger" \| "neutral"` | no | `"accent"` |  |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md"` | no | `"md"` |  |
| `animateChanges` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Animate later changes of `value` with a `transform: scaleX` transition. Off by default: `value` then applies at once. The fill keeps its full width and is scaled, so no layout property animates. A non-zero value never draws thinner than 2% of the track. The end cap is scaled with the fill, so it flattens slightly for small values. Removed under reduced motion. |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `ProgressBarProps`: `Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>, "children" | "role"> & { value: number; max?: number | undefined; label: string; valueText?: string | undefined; tone?: ChartTone | undefined; size?: "sm" | "md" | undefined; animateChanges?: boolean | undefined; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { ProgressBar } from "@lufia/design-system/components/ProgressBar";

<ProgressBar value={45} label="Storage used" />
<ProgressBar value={12} max={40} label="Steps done" valueText="12 of 40 steps" />
```

### Accessibility

- `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and `aria-valuenow`. `label` is required: without a name a progress bar is announced as a bare number.
- Use `valueText` when the percentage alone says too little ("12 of 40 steps").
- It states a fraction, so print the figure beside it as text; colour alone must not carry a warning.
- The fill draws in once on mount and is removed under `prefers-reduced-motion`. Later changes of `value` apply at once by default. With `animateChanges` the fill keeps its full width and is scaled with a `transform` transition (`--lufia-motion-duration-enter`), never width; reduced motion applies the new value at once.
- In `forced-colors` mode the track gets a border and the fill is `Highlight`.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has a `prefers-reduced-motion` branch.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-border-width-thin`, `--lufia-color-accent-default`, `--lufia-color-border-subtle`, `--lufia-color-status-danger-solid`, `--lufia-color-status-success-fg`, `--lufia-color-status-warning-fg`, `--lufia-color-text-subtle`, `--lufia-motion-duration-enter`, `--lufia-motion-duration-medium`, `--lufia-motion-easing-out`, `--lufia-radius-full`.

### Stories

- `components-data-display-progressbar--default`
- `components-data-display-progressbar--small`
- `components-data-display-progressbar--empty`
- `components-data-display-progressbar--complete`
- `components-data-display-progressbar--warning`
- `components-data-display-progressbar--danger`
- `components-data-display-progressbar--custom-range`
- `components-data-display-progressbar--with-visible-figure`
- `components-data-display-progressbar--animated-changes`
- `components-data-display-progressbar--animated-at-rest`
- `components-data-display-progressbar--right-to-left`
- `components-data-display-progressbar--all-themes`

## RadioGroup

> A set of radios where exactly one choice applies.

- Status: beta
- Category: Forms
- Import: `import { RadioGroup } from "@lufia/design-system/components/RadioGroup"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/RadioGroup](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/RadioGroup)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-forms-radiogroup--docs)

### Purpose

One choice from a short, visible list. Each option has a label and may have a description. The group has a roving tab stop
and arrow-key navigation.

### When to use

- Two to six mutually exclusive options, where seeing them all helps the decision.

### When not to use

- Seven or more options: use `Select` or `Combobox`.
- On/off: use `Switch` or `Checkbox`.
- A compact two-or-three-way view switch: use `SegmentedToggle`.

### API

#### `RadioGroup`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | Names the group, like a `<legend>`. |
| `options` | `readonly RadioOption[]` | yes |  |  |
| `hint` | `ReactNode` | no |  |  |
| `error` | `ReactNode` | no |  |  |
| `required` | `boolean` | no |  |  |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | no |  |  |
| `value` | `string` | no |  | Controlled value. `""` means nothing chosen. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | no | `""` |  |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` | no |  |  |
| `name` | `string` | no |  | Submitted with the form as `name=value`. |
| `orientation` | `"vertical" \| "horizontal"` | no | `"vertical"` | `"vertical"` (default) stacks the options; `"horizontal"` wraps them in a row. |
| `variant` | `"default" \| "card"` | no | `"default"` | `"default"` draws the options as plain rows. `"card"` draws each as a bordered, selectable row (a card when it carries `meta` or `content`), with the chosen one outlined in the accent colour. The radio semantics and the keyboard are the same. Defaults to `"default"`. |
| `requiredLabel` | `string` | no |  | Text read after the label when `required`. Aria-only: the visible mark is a glyph. Defaults to the `required` label of `LufiaProvider`. |
| `requiredMessage` | `string` | no |  | Shown when a required group is submitted with nothing chosen. Defaults to the browser's own message. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` | no |  |  |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `RadioOption`: `{ value: string; label: ReactNode; description?: ReactNode; meta?: ReactNode; content?: ReactNode; disabled?: boolean | undefined; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { RadioGroup } from "@lufia/design-system/components/RadioGroup";

<RadioGroup
  label="Payment method"
  name="payment"
  value={method}
  onValueChange={setMethod}
  options={[
    { value: "card", label: "Card", description: "Charged today." },
    { value: "transfer", label: "Bank transfer" },
  ]}
  error={errors.payment}
/>;
```

### Accessibility

Follows the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices pattern: [Radio group](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/radio/).

- In right-to-left layouts Left and Right swap.
- `role="radiogroup"` named by the label; each option is `role="radio"` with `aria-checked`, named by its label and described by its description.
- A required group blocks form submission until an option is chosen, with the browser's own message: an invisible, unsubmitted input mirrors the value for that. A form `reset` returns the group to `defaultValue`.
- The card variant changes the look only: the same roving focus, arrow keys and `radio` semantics. `meta` and `content` join the option's `aria-describedby`.
- Required adds an asterisk, the text `required` for screen readers (the `required` label of `LufiaProvider`, or `requiredLabel`), and `aria-required`.
- The error is in the group's description, with `role="alert"` and `aria-invalid`.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-border-width-thick`, `--lufia-border-width-thin`, `--lufia-color-accent-default`, `--lufia-color-accent-subtle`, `--lufia-color-bg-field`, `--lufia-color-bg-surface`, `--lufia-color-border-strong`, `--lufia-color-focus-ring`, `--lufia-color-status-danger-fg`, `--lufia-color-text-default`, `--lufia-color-text-muted`, `--lufia-color-text-on-accent`, `--lufia-font-line-height-normal`, `--lufia-font-line-height-tight`, `--lufia-font-size-md`, `--lufia-font-size-sm`, `--lufia-font-size-xs`, `--lufia-font-weight-semibold`, `--lufia-motion-duration-instant`, `--lufia-motion-easing-out`, `--lufia-opacity-disabled`, `--lufia-radius-card`, `--lufia-radius-control`, `--lufia-radius-full`, `--lufia-space-1`, `--lufia-space-2`, `--lufia-space-3`, `--lufia-space-4`, `--lufia-space-6`.

### Content guidelines

The group label is the question or the noun ("Payment method"). Options are parallel, short and sentence case. Describe the
consequence in the description, not the label. Pre-select the safe default when there is one; otherwise leave nothing chosen
and require a choice.

### Stories

- `components-forms-radiogroup--default`
- `components-forms-radiogroup--nothing-chosen`
- `components-forms-radiogroup--with-hint`
- `components-forms-radiogroup--required`
- `components-forms-radiogroup--invalid`
- `components-forms-radiogroup--card-variant`
- `components-forms-radiogroup--card-horizontal`
- `components-forms-radiogroup--card-invalid`
- `components-forms-radiogroup--card-long-text`
- `components-forms-radiogroup--card-phone-320`
- `components-forms-radiogroup--disabled`
- `components-forms-radiogroup--horizontal`
- `components-forms-radiogroup--long-text`
- `components-forms-radiogroup--phone-320`
- `components-forms-radiogroup--right-to-left`
- `components-forms-radiogroup--all-themes`

## Reveal

> Fades and lifts content in as it enters, once.

- Status: beta
- Category: Motion
- Import: `import { Reveal } from "@lufia/design-system/motion"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/motion/Reveal](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/motion/Reveal)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-motion-reveal--docs)

### Purpose

Mounts and unmounts content with an enter and an exit animation. Entrances use `--lufia-motion-duration-enter`, exits the
shorter `--lufia-motion-duration-exit`.

### When to use

- A notice, panel or row that appears or disappears because of something the person did.

### When not to use

- Content that changes height in place: use [Collapse](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-motion-collapse--docs).
- Content that is on screen from the first paint. `Reveal` does not animate on mount unless you set `appear`: only real state changes animate.
- Dialogs and popovers. They need focus management that belongs to their own components.

### API

#### `Reveal`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `show` | `boolean` | yes |  | Whether the content is shown. Toggling it plays the enter or exit animation. |
| `variant` | `"scale" \| "fade" \| "rise"` | no | `"fade"` | `fade` changes opacity only, `rise` also moves the content up, `scale` grows it slightly. |
| `appear` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Play the enter animation when the component mounts already shown. Off by default: only real changes animate. |
| `onExited` | `() => void` | no |  | Called once the content is gone after a hide: the exit animation ended, or there was none. Not called when it re-opens first. |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `RevealProps`: `HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement> & { show: boolean; variant?: "scale" | "fade" | "rise" | undefined; appear?: boolean | undefined; onExited?: (() => void) | undefined; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { Reveal } from "@lufia/design-system/motion";

<Reveal show={saved} variant="rise">
  <Banner>Changes saved</Banner>
</Reveal>;
```

### Accessibility

- Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the content appears and disappears at once.
- Nothing is conveyed by the motion alone: the content is in the DOM and the accessibility tree whenever it is shown.
- If the content is an important status, put it in (or wrap it with) a live region so it is announced. `Reveal` adds no roles.
- During the exit the content is no longer clickable (`pointer-events: none`), but it is still focusable for the 160 ms it takes to leave. Move focus yourself if the focused element is inside.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has a `prefers-reduced-motion` branch.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-motion-distance-rise`, `--lufia-motion-duration-enter`, `--lufia-motion-duration-exit`, `--lufia-motion-easing-in`, `--lufia-motion-easing-out`.

### Stories

- `components-motion-reveal--default`
- `components-motion-reveal--fade`
- `components-motion-reveal--scale`
- `components-motion-reveal--starts-hidden`
- `components-motion-reveal--appears-on-mount`
- `components-motion-reveal--all-themes`

## RouteTransition

> Fades the content region in when the page changes, with no router dependency.

- Status: beta
- Category: Motion
- Import: `import { RouteTransition } from "@lufia/design-system/motion"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/motion/RouteTransition](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/motion/RouteTransition)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-motion-routetransition--docs)

### Purpose

The content region of an app: when the page changes, the new content enters with a short fade and rise. It does not depend on any router.

### When to use

- The main content region of an app, keyed by the pathname.
- Tabbed or stepped content that behaves like pages.

### When not to use

- Persistent chrome such as headers and sidebars: keep them outside the region.
- Content that changes with search params or data refreshes: keep the key stable.
- Single elements that appear and disappear: use `Reveal`.

### API

#### `RouteTransition`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `transitionKey` | `string \| number` | yes |  | Identifies the page being shown, usually the pathname. When it changes after the first render, the region's content enters. Anything that keeps the same key (a search-param change, a refresh, the first load) plays nothing. |
| `variant` | `"fade" \| "rise"` | no | `"rise"` | `rise` fades in and lifts a few pixels, `fade` only changes opacity (for a page that replaces a skeleton). |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `RouteTransitionProps`: `HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement> & { transitionKey: string | number; variant?: "fade" | "rise" | undefined; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { RouteTransition } from "@lufia/design-system/motion";

// With any router: pass the current path as the key.
<RouteTransition transitionKey={pathname}>
  <Banner data-route-static="" />
  {children}
</RouteTransition>;
```

### Accessibility

- Nothing is remounted: the region, its layouts and providers (toasts, filters, form state) keep their state. Only a marker attribute is set on the direct children, after React commits and before the browser paints, so the old page never animates.
- The first render, a refresh and any change that keeps the same `transitionKey` play nothing.
- Children with `data-route-static` and `position: fixed` children are skipped: a transform on them would restart a banner or change what a fixed element is fixed to.
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion` nothing is marked, so the page is simply there.
- Focus and scroll are not touched. Move focus to the new page yourself, as your router recommends.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has a `prefers-reduced-motion` branch.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-motion-distance-rise`, `--lufia-motion-duration-enter`, `--lufia-motion-easing-out`.

### Stories

- `components-motion-routetransition--rise`
- `components-motion-routetransition--fade`
- `components-motion-routetransition--all-themes`

## SearchInput

> A search field with a clear button, optional debounce and a shortcut hint.

- Status: beta
- Category: Forms
- Import: `import { SearchInput } from "@lufia/design-system/components/SearchInput"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/SearchInput](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/SearchInput)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-forms-searchinput--docs)

### Purpose

A search box: a magnifier, a native `type="search"` input, a clear button, an optional shortcut hint and a debounced
`onSearch`.

### When to use

- Filtering or finding items in a list, a table or a whole product.

### When not to use

- Choosing one value from a list of known options: use `Combobox`, which keeps the choice and its keyboard model.
- A form field whose text is data, not a query: use `TextInput`.

### API

#### `SearchInput`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string` | no |  | Controlled text. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | no | `""` |  |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` | no |  | Called on every keystroke with the current text. |
| `onSearch` | `(value: string) => void` | no |  | Called with the text once the person stops typing for `debounceMs`, at once on Enter, and at once when the text is cleared. It does not fire for the initial value, or twice for the same text in a row. |
| `debounceMs` | `number` | no | `300` | Quiet time before `onSearch` fires while typing, in milliseconds. Default 300. |
| `clearLabel` | `string` | no | `"Clear search"` | Accessible name of the clear button. Aria-only. |
| `shortcut` | `string` | no |  | A hint for the key that focuses the field, such as "/" or "Ctrl K". Display only: the app binds the key. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | no | `false` | A search is running. Shows a ring, sets `aria-busy` and announces `loadingLabel`. |
| `loadingLabel` | `string` | no | `"Searching"` | Text announced while `loading`. Aria-only. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | no |  | Marks the control invalid without a `FormField`. |
| `className` | `string` | no |  | Goes on the box that draws the border; the native input gets the rest props. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLInputElement>` | no |  |  |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Example

```tsx
import { SearchInput } from "@lufia/design-system/components/SearchInput";

<SearchInput
  placeholder="Search customers"
  clearLabel="Clear search"
  shortcut="/"
  onSearch={(text) => load(text)}
  loading={isLoading}
/>;
```

### Accessibility

- Needs a name: put it in a `FormField`, pass `aria-label`, or the placeholder is used as a last resort.
- The clear button has its own accessible name (`clearLabel`) and is 32px square inside a 44px box.
- While `loading`, the input has `aria-busy` and a status region announces `loadingLabel`. The ring stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Results are not announced by this component: the list you update should announce its own count (a live region).

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-border-width-thick`, `--lufia-border-width-thin`, `--lufia-color-bg-surface-raised`, `--lufia-color-border-subtle`, `--lufia-color-focus-ring`, `--lufia-color-text-default`, `--lufia-color-text-muted`, `--lufia-font-family-mono`, `--lufia-font-line-height-normal`, `--lufia-font-size-xs`, `--lufia-motion-duration-instant`, `--lufia-motion-easing-out`, `--lufia-radius-full`, `--lufia-radius-xs`, `--lufia-space-2`.

### Content guidelines

The placeholder says what can be searched ("Search customers"), not "Search...". Put the scope in it when there is more than one
search on a page. `clearLabel` and `loadingLabel` are read aloud: "Clear search", "Searching customers".

### Stories

- `components-forms-searchinput--default`
- `components-forms-searchinput--with-value`
- `components-forms-searchinput--with-shortcut`
- `components-forms-searchinput--inside-form-field`
- `components-forms-searchinput--invalid`
- `components-forms-searchinput--loading`
- `components-forms-searchinput--disabled`
- `components-forms-searchinput--read-only`
- `components-forms-searchinput--debounced`
- `components-forms-searchinput--long-text`
- `components-forms-searchinput--phone-320`
- `components-forms-searchinput--right-to-left`
- `components-forms-searchinput--all-themes`

## SectionHeader

> The title row of one section of a page: heading, description and actions.

- Status: beta
- Category: Navigation
- Import: `import { SectionHeader } from "@lufia/design-system/components/SectionHeader"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/SectionHeader](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/SectionHeader)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-navigation-sectionheader--docs)

### Purpose

The title row of one section of a page: a heading, an optional description and the section's actions. `PageHeader` is for the top of a page, this is for the blocks inside it.

### When to use

- Above a list, a chart or a table inside a page.
- To pair a title with a "View all" link or a few actions.

### When not to use

- The title of a page: use `PageHeader`.
- The title of a bordered surface: use `Card` with `title`, `description` and `headerAction`.

### API

#### `SectionHeader`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | yes |  |  |
| `headingLevel` | `2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6` | no | `2` | Heading level of `title` (2 to 6). Defaults to 2: pick the one that keeps the page outline in order. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` | no |  | One short line under the title. |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Links or controls at the end of the row ("View all"). They wrap under the text on narrow screens. |
| `titleId` | `string` | no |  | Id of the heading, so a `<section aria-labelledby>` can point at it. |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `SectionHeaderProps`: `Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>, "title"> & { title: ReactNode; headingLevel?: 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | undefined; description?: ReactNode; actions?: ReactNode; titleId?: string | undefined; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { SectionHeader } from "@lufia/design-system/components/SectionHeader";

<section aria-labelledby="recent-title">
  <SectionHeader
    title="Recent activity"
    titleId="recent-title"
    description="The last five changes."
    actions={<Link href="/activity">View all</Link>}
  />
  {/* the section content */}
</section>;
```

### Accessibility

- `title` is a heading, level 2 by default. Set `headingLevel` to keep the page outline in order (a section inside a card is usually a 3).
- Give the heading an id with `titleId` and point the section at it with `aria-labelledby`, so the section is a named region.
- Actions follow the heading in the reading order and wrap under the text on narrow screens.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-color-text-default`, `--lufia-color-text-muted`, `--lufia-font-family-display`, `--lufia-font-line-height-normal`, `--lufia-font-line-height-tight`, `--lufia-font-size-lg`, `--lufia-font-size-sm`, `--lufia-font-weight-semibold`.

### Stories

- `components-navigation-sectionheader--default`
- `components-navigation-sectionheader--with-description`
- `components-navigation-sectionheader--with-link`
- `components-navigation-sectionheader--with-buttons`
- `components-navigation-sectionheader--long-title`
- `components-navigation-sectionheader--phone-320`
- `components-navigation-sectionheader--right-to-left`
- `components-navigation-sectionheader--all-themes`

## SegmentedToggle

> A compact single-choice control for switching between a few views or modes.

- Status: beta
- Category: Forms
- Import: `import { SegmentedToggle } from "@lufia/design-system/components/SegmentedToggle"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/SegmentedToggle](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/SegmentedToggle)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-forms-segmentedtoggle--docs)

### Purpose

Two to four compact choices in one bordered group, where one is chosen (always, unless `value` is `null`). An indicator slides behind the chosen
segment.

### When to use

- Switching how the same content is shown or sourced: list or board, upload or link, monthly or yearly.

### When not to use

- Moving between pages or sibling views with their own content: use `PeerNav` (links or tabs).
- On and off: use `Switch`.
- More than four options, or long labels: use `RadioGroup` or `Select`.

### API

#### `SegmentedToggle`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | yes |  | Accessible name of the group ("Display mode"). Required: the visible segments do not say what they choose. |
| `options` | `readonly SegmentedToggleOption[]` | yes |  |  |
| `value` | `string \| null` | no |  | Controlled value. `null` is controlled with nothing chosen: no segment is checked and the indicator is hidden. The first enabled segment is still the tab stop, and an arrow key chooses (selection follows focus) as it does with a value. |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| null` | no |  | Initial value when `value` is not given; `null` starts with nothing chosen. Defaults to the first enabled option. A form reset goes back to it (to `null` when a controlled `value` started as `null`). |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` | no |  | Called with the value the user chose. Never `null`: a deselect is reported by `onDeselect`. |
| `allowDeselect` | `boolean` | no |  | When true, activating the chosen segment again clears the choice and calls `onDeselect`. With a controlled `value`, set it to `null` there; an uncontrolled toggle clears itself. |
| `onDeselect` | `() => void` | no |  | Called when `allowDeselect` is on and the user clears the choice, or when a form reset returns to nothing chosen. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | no |  |  |
| `name` | `string` | no |  | Submitted with the form as `name=value`. |
| `width` | `"fill" \| "fit"` | no | `"fit"` | `"fit"` (default) shrinks to its content; `"fill"` shares the full width between the segments. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md"` | no | `"md"` | `"md"` (default) or the denser `"sm"` for rows in a list or a table. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` | no |  |  |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `SegmentedToggleOption`: `{ value: string; label: ReactNode; icon?: ReactNode; disabled?: boolean | undefined; tone?: SegmentedToggleTone | undefined; }`
- `SegmentedToggleTone`: `"neutral" | "success" | "warning" | "danger"`

### Example

```tsx
import { SegmentedToggle } from "@lufia/design-system/components/SegmentedToggle";

<SegmentedToggle
  label="View"
  value={view}
  onValueChange={setView}
  options={[
    { value: "list", label: "List" },
    { value: "board", label: "Board" },
  ]}
/>;
```

### Accessibility

Follows the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices pattern: [Radio group](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/radio/).

- `label` names the group and is required. Icons are decorative.
- The indicator animates `transform` only, jumps on resize, and does not animate under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Before scripts run the chosen segment paints its own border and fill, so the choice is visible without the indicator.
- Under `forced-colors` the chosen segment keeps a `Highlight` border.
- Selection follows focus: an arrow key moves focus and chooses, also when nothing was chosen. Space or a click on a focused segment chooses it.
- `tone` is never the only cue: the chosen segment also has the selected border and the indicator. Text and fill pairs are the status `fg` on `bg` pairs checked by `npm run contrast`.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens
