Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-border-width-thick`, `--lufia-border-width-thin`, `--lufia-color-accent-border`, `--lufia-color-accent-subtle`, `--lufia-color-bg-surface`, `--lufia-color-border-strong`, `--lufia-color-focus-ring`, `--lufia-color-status-danger-bg`, `--lufia-color-status-danger-border`, `--lufia-color-status-danger-fg`, `--lufia-color-status-neutral-bg`, `--lufia-color-status-success-bg`, `--lufia-color-status-success-border`, `--lufia-color-status-success-fg`, `--lufia-color-status-warning-bg`, `--lufia-color-status-warning-border`, `--lufia-color-status-warning-fg`, `--lufia-color-text-accent`, `--lufia-color-text-default`, `--lufia-color-text-muted`, `--lufia-font-line-height-tight`, `--lufia-font-size-sm`, `--lufia-font-size-xs`, `--lufia-font-weight-semibold`, `--lufia-motion-duration-enter`, `--lufia-motion-duration-instant`, `--lufia-motion-easing-out`, `--lufia-opacity-disabled`, `--lufia-radius-control`, `--lufia-radius-md`, `--lufia-shadow-sm`, `--lufia-space-2`, `--lufia-space-3`, `--lufia-space-4`.

### Content guidelines

Labels are one or two words and parallel ("List", "Board"). They name what is shown, not the action. The group `label` names
the dimension being chosen ("View", "Billing period").

### Stories

- `components-forms-segmentedtoggle--default`
- `components-forms-segmentedtoggle--two-choices`
- `components-forms-segmentedtoggle--with-icons`
- `components-forms-segmentedtoggle--disabled-segment`
- `components-forms-segmentedtoggle--disabled`
- `components-forms-segmentedtoggle--fill`
- `components-forms-segmentedtoggle--long-text`
- `components-forms-segmentedtoggle--phone-320`
- `components-forms-segmentedtoggle--right-to-left`
- `components-forms-segmentedtoggle--all-themes`
- `components-forms-segmentedtoggle--status-picker`

## Select

> A native select (dropdown) styled with tokens, for choosing one option from a short list.

- Status: beta
- Category: Forms
- Import: `import { Select } from "@lufia/design-system/components/Select"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/Select](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/Select)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-forms-select--docs)

### Purpose

A native `<select>` in the shared field box, with a drawn chevron. The browser keeps its own list, keyboard handling,
typeahead and mobile picker.

### When to use

- Three to about fifteen options the person can recognise by name, where a native picker is a feature (phones).

### When not to use

- Fewer than four options that matter equally: a `RadioGroup` shows them all at once.
- Long lists, search, async data or options with more than text: use `Combobox`.

### API

#### `Select`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `readonly SelectOption[]` | no |  | The choices. Use `groups` for `<optgroup>`s. |
| `groups` | `readonly SelectOptionGroup[]` | no |  | Labelled groups of choices, rendered as `<optgroup>`s after `options`. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | no |  | `<option>` and `<optgroup>` elements, when `options` is not enough. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | no |  | Text of the empty first choice ("Choose a country"). It is selectable only before a choice is made: once chosen, the person cannot go back to nothing unless the field is optional, so set `allowEmpty` for that. |
| `allowEmpty` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Keeps the placeholder choosable after a value is picked, for optional fields. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | no |  | Marks the control invalid without a `FormField`. Inside a field the error does it. |
| `className` | `string` | no |  | Goes on the box that draws the border; the native select gets the rest props. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLSelectElement>` | no |  |  |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `SelectOption`: `{ value: string; label: string; disabled?: boolean | undefined; }`
- `SelectOptionGroup`: `{ label: string; options: readonly SelectOption[]; disabled?: boolean | undefined; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { FormField } from "@lufia/design-system/components/FormField";
import { Select } from "@lufia/design-system/components/Select";

<FormField label="Country" error={errors.country}>
  <Select
    name="country"
    placeholder="Choose a country"
    defaultValue=""
    options={[
      { value: "pt", label: "Portugal" },
      { value: "es", label: "Spain" },
    ]}
  />
</FormField>;
```

### Accessibility

- Always inside a `FormField`, or give `aria-label`.
- The chevron is decorative and does not take clicks; the whole box opens the list.
- Under `forced-colors` the box and focus ring use system colours.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-color-bg-surface-solid`, `--lufia-color-text-default`, `--lufia-opacity-disabled`, `--lufia-space-3`.

### Content guidelines

Options are sentence case, parallel and sorted in a way that fits the data (alphabetical for names, natural order for
ranges). The placeholder is an instruction, "Choose a country", never the label again.

### Stories

- `components-forms-select--default`
- `components-forms-select--with-placeholder`
- `components-forms-select--optional-with-empty-choice`
- `components-forms-select--with-hint`
- `components-forms-select--required`
- `components-forms-select--invalid`
- `components-forms-select--disabled`
- `components-forms-select--with-groups`
- `components-forms-select--with-child-groups`
- `components-forms-select--long-text`
- `components-forms-select--phone-320`
- `components-forms-select--right-to-left`
- `components-forms-select--all-themes`

## Skeleton

> A placeholder with the shape of the content that is loading.

- Status: beta
- Category: Motion
- Import: `import { Skeleton } from "@lufia/design-system/motion"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/motion/Skeleton](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/motion/Skeleton)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-motion-skeleton--docs)

### Purpose

A placeholder that holds the shape of content while it loads, with a calm shimmer.

### When to use

- A region whose layout is known while its data is pending: cards, lists, table rows, profile headers.

### When not to use

- Unknown shape or very short waits (under about 300 ms): show nothing, or a spinner on the triggering control.
- Errors or empty results: use an error message or [EmptyState](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-feedback-emptystate--docs).

### API

#### `Skeleton`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `"text" \| "rect" \| "circle"` | no | `"text"` | `text` is one line of text, `rect` a block, `circle` an avatar. |
| `width` | `string` | no |  | CSS length. Give the size of the content that will replace the placeholder so nothing jumps. |
| `height` | `string` | no |  | CSS length. Text defaults to one line height. |
| `still` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Turn the shimmer off. It also stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`. |
| `label` | `string` | no |  | Accessible name for the loading state, for example "Loading invoices". Set it on one skeleton per loading region: it renders a polite status message. Without it the skeleton is hidden from assistive technology. |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `SkeletonProps`: `Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLSpanElement>, "children"> & { variant?: "text" | "rect" | "circle" | undefined; width?: string | undefined; height?: string | undefined; still?: boolean | undefined; label?: string | undefined; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { Skeleton } from "@lufia/design-system/motion";

<div aria-busy={loading}>
  {loading ? (
    <>
      <Skeleton width="60%" />
      <Skeleton variant="rect" height="6rem" label="Loading profile" />
    </>
  ) : (
    <Profile />
  )}
</div>;
```

### Accessibility

- Skeletons are `aria-hidden` by default. Set `label` on **one** skeleton per loading region: it renders a polite `role="status"` message ("Loading profile"). The string is yours, so it can be translated.
- Mark the region `aria-busy="true"` while loading.
- The shimmer is `transform` only, and it stops under `prefers-reduced-motion` (the shape stays). `still` turns it off everywhere.
- In `forced-colors` mode the skeleton becomes an outlined box and the shimmer is removed.
- No information is carried by the motion.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has a `prefers-reduced-motion` branch.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-color-bg-surface-solid`, `--lufia-color-border-subtle`, `--lufia-radius-card`, `--lufia-radius-full`, `--lufia-radius-sm`.

### Stories

- `components-motion-skeleton--text`
- `components-motion-skeleton--rect`
- `components-motion-skeleton--circle`
- `components-motion-skeleton--still`
- `components-motion-skeleton--composed`
- `components-motion-skeleton--all-themes`

## SortableTh

> A table header cell that sorts a column and announces the order.

- Status: beta
- Category: Data display
- Import: `import { SortableTh } from "@lufia/design-system/components/SortableTh"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/SortableTh](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/SortableTh)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-data-display-sortableth--docs)

### Purpose

A sortable table column header. It renders a `<th>` containing a real `<button>`, so the column can be sorted from the
keyboard, and keeps `aria-sort` on the `<th>`.

### When to use

- Table columns the user can reorder by.

### When not to use

- Columns that are not sortable (use a plain `<th scope="col">`) or card layouts without a header row.

### API

#### `SortableTh`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dir` | `"asc" \| "desc"` | yes |  |  |
| `label` | `string` | yes |  |  |
| `active` | `boolean` | yes |  | Whether the table is currently sorted by this column. |
| `onSort` | `() => void` | yes |  |  |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `SortDirection`: `"asc" | "desc"`
- `SortableThProps`: `Omit<ThHTMLAttributes<HTMLTableCellElement>, "children" | "onClick"> & { label: string; active: boolean; dir: SortDirection; onSort: () => void; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { SortableTh } from "@lufia/design-system/components/SortableTh";

<SortableTh label="Name" active={sort.key === "name"} dir={sort.dir} onSort={() => toggle("name")} />;
```

### Accessibility

Follows the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices pattern: [Sortable table](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/table/).

- Follows the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices **sortable table** pattern: `aria-sort="ascending" | "descending" | "none"` is set on the column header, the control inside is a native button (Tab to focus, Enter or Space to activate).
- The direction arrow is `aria-hidden`; `aria-sort` is what assistive technology announces, so the arrow does not pollute the button's name.
- A visible focus ring (2px, `--lufia-color-focus-ring`) is always present and the target is at least 24px tall.
- The button inherits header typography, so it looks like plain text until focused.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-border-width-thick`, `--lufia-color-focus-ring`, `--lufia-radius-xs`.

### Content guidelines

`label` is the localised column name. Keep it to one or two words; the header does not wrap by default.

### Stories

- `components-data-display-sortableth--ascending`
- `components-data-display-sortableth--descending`
- `components-data-display-sortableth--inactive`
- `components-data-display-sortableth--interactive-sort`
- `components-data-display-sortableth--all-themes`

## Sparkline

> A word-sized trend chart with no axes, drawn in SVG.

- Status: beta
- Category: Data display
- Import: `import { Sparkline } from "@lufia/design-system/components/Sparkline"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/Sparkline](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/Sparkline)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-data-display-sparkline--docs)

### Purpose

A word-sized chart with no axes: the trend that sits next to a figure. Drawn in SVG, with no chart library.

### When to use

- The trend next to a figure, in a `StatTile` or a table row.
- A comparison of a few short series at a glance.

### When not to use

- Reading exact values or axes: print a table or use `BarList`.
- Long series that need a scale, gridlines or tooltips.

### API

#### `Sparkline`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `values` | `readonly number[]` | yes |  | The series, oldest first. Non-finite numbers count as 0. |
| `variant` | `"columns" \| "line"` | no | `"columns"` | `columns` draws one bar per value from a zero baseline, `line` a trend line scaled to the range. |
| `tone` | `"accent" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "danger" \| "neutral"` | no | `"accent"` |  |
| `label` | `string \| null` | yes |  | Accessible name: a sentence that carries the numbers ("Deliveries per week: 3, 5, 4, 8"). Pass `null` to hide the drawing from assistive technology, only when the numbers are printed as text next to it. |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `SparklineProps`: `Omit<SVGAttributes<SVGSVGElement>, "children" | "role" | "values" | "aria-label"> & { values: readonly number[]; variant?: SparklineVariant | undefined; tone?: ChartTone | undefined; label: string | null; }`
- `SparklineVariant`: `"columns" | "line"`

### Example

```tsx
import { Sparkline } from "@lufia/design-system/components/Sparkline";

<Sparkline values={[3, 5, 4, 8, 6, 9, 12]} label="Deliveries per week: 3, 5, 4, 8, 6, 9, 12" />;

{
  /* The numbers are already printed as text beside it. */
}
<Sparkline values={[3, 5, 4, 8]} variant="line" label={null} />;
```

### Accessibility

- `label` is required. With a string, the drawing is `role="img"` named by that sentence, so put the numbers in it. With `null`, it is hidden from assistive technology: do that only when the numbers are printed as text next to it.
- The tone only reinforces. Never use a tone as the only way to tell good from bad.
- The draw-in is `transform` and stroke only and plays once, on mount. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` it is removed and the finished drawing is there at once.
- In `forced-colors` mode the marks use `CanvasText`.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has a `prefers-reduced-motion` branch.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-color-accent-default`, `--lufia-color-border-strong`, `--lufia-color-status-danger-solid`, `--lufia-color-status-success-fg`, `--lufia-color-status-warning-fg`, `--lufia-color-text-subtle`, `--lufia-motion-duration-instant`, `--lufia-motion-duration-medium`, `--lufia-motion-easing-out`.

### Stories

- `components-data-display-sparkline--columns`
- `components-data-display-sparkline--line`
- `components-data-display-sparkline--tones`
- `components-data-display-sparkline--with-zeros`
- `components-data-display-sparkline--single-value`
- `components-data-display-sparkline--constant-line`
- `components-data-display-sparkline--many-values`
- `components-data-display-sparkline--empty`
- `components-data-display-sparkline--decorative`
- `components-data-display-sparkline--right-to-left`
- `components-data-display-sparkline--all-themes`

## StackedBar

> One bar split into proportional segments, with a legend and a text alternative.

- Status: beta
- Category: Data display
- Import: `import { StackedBar } from "@lufia/design-system/components/StackedBar"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/StackedBar](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/StackedBar)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-data-display-stackedbar--docs)

### Purpose

One bar split into proportional segments, with a legend. It shows how a whole divides into parts, such as a plan mix or
accounts by status.

### When to use

- A part-of-whole breakdown of one total, with a handful of segments.
- A compact composition next to a figure or inside a card.

### When not to use

- Several measures per period: use `ColumnChart`.
- One value against a target: use `BulletBar`; one completion fraction: use `ProgressBar`.
- Values that are compared across rows on a shared scale: use `BarList`.
- Many segments (more than about five): the tones run out and the slices become unreadable. Use `BarList`.

### API

#### `StackedBar`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `segments` | `readonly StackedBarSegment[]` | yes |  | The parts of the whole, in drawing order. Segments with no value are not drawn but stay in the legend and the text. |
| `label` | `string` | yes |  | Accessible name of the whole bar ("Plan mix"). Required: the bar is a group that a screen reader reads by its parts. |
| `formatValue` | `(value: number) => string` | no | `String` | Formats each value for the legend and the text alternative ("1,240", "3 sites"). Defaults to `String(value)`. |
| `formatPercent` | `(percent: number) => string` | no | `defaultPercent` | Formats each share, given as a number from 0 to 100, for the legend and the text alternative. Defaults to the rounded number and `%` ("38%"), and to "<1%" for a segment with a value whose share rounds to 0. Rounded shares may not add up to 100. Pass it to localise the number or the symbol. |
| `legend` | `"hidden" \| "auto"` | no | `"auto"` | `"auto"` prints the legend under the bar: a swatch, the label and the value of every segment. `"hidden"` keeps the same list in the page for screen readers only, so the bar never loses its text alternative. Defaults to `"auto"`. |
| `showPercent` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Prints each share next to its value in the legend. Off by default; the share is always read by assistive technology. |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `StackedBarSegment`: `{ key: string; label: string; value: number; tone?: ChartTone | undefined; pattern?: "hatch" | undefined; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { StackedBar } from "@lufia/design-system/components/StackedBar";

<StackedBar
  label="Accounts by status"
  segments={[
    { key: "active", label: "Active", value: 48, tone: "accent" },
    { key: "trial", label: "Trial", value: 21, tone: "success" },
    { key: "expired", label: "Expired", value: 9, tone: "warning" },
  ]}
  formatValue={(value) => value.toLocaleString("en")}
/>;
```

### Accessibility

- The root is a `role="group"` named by `label` (required). The drawing is `aria-hidden`; the text alternative is a list with one item per segment: its label, its value and its share ("Active 48 (62%)").
- `legend="hidden"` hides the legend visually and keeps that list for screen readers. `showPercent` only changes whether the share is printed.
- Colour is never the only cue: every segment is named in the list, neighbours are separated by a gap, and a `pattern` adds stripes.
- A zero total draws an empty track and every share reads 0%. Zero segments are not drawn but stay in the list.
- A segment with a value whose share rounds to 0 reads `"<1%"` by default. Rounded shares may not add up to 100.
- A negative or non-finite value is drawn as 0 and its share reads 0, but the list shows the number as given, so bad data stays visible to assistive technology.
- The draw-in is `transform` only and plays once, on mount; it is removed under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- In `forced-colors` mode each segment, and its legend swatch, gets its own fill pattern in `CanvasText`.
- Layout uses logical properties and the draw-in starts from the inline start, so right-to-left works.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has a `prefers-reduced-motion` branch.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-border-width-thin`, `--lufia-color-accent-default`, `--lufia-color-bg-surface`, `--lufia-color-border-subtle`, `--lufia-color-status-danger-solid`, `--lufia-color-status-success-fg`, `--lufia-color-status-warning-fg`, `--lufia-color-text-default`, `--lufia-color-text-muted`, `--lufia-color-text-subtle`, `--lufia-font-size-xs`, `--lufia-font-weight-semibold`, `--lufia-motion-duration-medium`, `--lufia-motion-easing-out`, `--lufia-radius-full`.

### Stories

- `components-data-display-stackedbar--default`
- `components-data-display-stackedbar--with-percent`
- `components-data-display-stackedbar--formatted-values`
- `components-data-display-stackedbar--legend-hidden`
- `components-data-display-stackedbar--zero-segment`
- `components-data-display-stackedbar--zero-total`
- `components-data-display-stackedbar--single-segment`
- `components-data-display-stackedbar--hatched`
- `components-data-display-stackedbar--many-segments`
- `components-data-display-stackedbar--right-to-left`
- `components-data-display-stackedbar--all-themes`

## Stagger

> Children that enter one after another, capped in length and still under reduced motion.

- Status: beta
- Category: Motion
- Import: `import { Stagger } from "@lufia/design-system/motion"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/motion/Stagger](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/motion/Stagger)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-motion-stagger--docs)

### Purpose

Children that enter in sequence on mount: each fades in and rises a few pixels, one step after the previous.

### When to use

- A grid of tiles or cards that appear together when a page opens.
- A short list entering after a skeleton.

### When not to use

- Long lists or tables: the stagger is capped, and a wall of motion is noise.
- Content people are already aiming at, such as controls that were visible before.
- A whole page changing: use `RouteTransition`.

### API

#### `Stagger`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | `number` | no | `5` | How many children get their own step. Children after the limit enter together with the last one, so the whole sequence is at most `limit - 1` steps long (about 120 ms of delay at the default). Defaults to 5, and values above 8 are treated as 8, so the total delay stays short whatever is passed. |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `StaggerProps`: `HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement> & { limit?: number | undefined; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { Stagger } from "@lufia/design-system/motion";

<Stagger style={{ display: "grid", gap: "0.75rem" }}>
  <StatTile label="Open" value="12" />
  <StatTile label="Overdue" value="4" />
  <StatTile label="Done" value="96%" />
</Stagger>;
```

### Accessibility

- Only `opacity` and `transform` move. The layout is final from the first frame, so nothing shifts (no layout shift) and focus order is untouched.
- Each step is a quarter of the instant duration token (about 30 ms), and children past `limit` enter together with the last step, so a long list never makes people wait: the default total is about 120 ms of delay plus the 240 ms enter.
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the children are simply there: no animation, no delay.
- Content is in the DOM and readable at once; screen readers are not affected by the entrance.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has a `prefers-reduced-motion` branch.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-motion-distance-rise`, `--lufia-motion-duration-enter`, `--lufia-motion-duration-instant`, `--lufia-motion-easing-out`.

### Stories

- `components-motion-stagger--default`
- `components-motion-stagger--long-list`
- `components-motion-stagger--low-limit`
- `components-motion-stagger--as-list`
- `components-motion-stagger--all-themes`

## StatTile

> A key figure with its label, change and hint, optionally a link to its detail.

- Status: beta
- Category: Data display
- Import: `import { StatTile } from "@lufia/design-system/components/StatTile"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/StatTile](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/StatTile)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-data-display-stattile--docs)

### Purpose

A key figure with its label, an optional change and hint, and a slot for a small chart: the tile of a dashboard. With `href` or `onClick` the whole tile is one link or button.

### When to use

- A figure people scan first on a dashboard: a count, a rate, an amount.
- A shortcut to the filtered list behind the figure.

### When not to use

- A figure inside a sentence or a table cell: format it as text.
- Several figures in one tile: use one tile per figure.
- A tile whose destination is unrelated to the figure: use a `Card`.

### API

#### `StatTile`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | What the figure measures. With `href` or `onClick` it is also the text of the tile's single link or button. |
| `value` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | The figure, already formatted. Pass an `AnimatedNumber` to count it up. |
| `tone` | `"neutral" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "danger"` | no | `"neutral"` | `warning` and `danger` tint the whole tile for a figure that needs attention. The label always says why. |
| `delta` | `ReactNode` | no |  | The change, already formatted ("+12% vs last week"). |
| `trend` | `"up" \| "down" \| "flat"` | no |  | Direction arrow shown before `delta`. The arrow is decorative: say the direction in `trendLabel` or in `delta`. |
| `trendLabel` | `string` | no |  | Direction in words for screen readers ("Up"). Read before `delta`. |
| `deltaTone` | `"neutral" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "danger"` | no | `"neutral"` | Colour of `delta`. A rise is not always good news, so it is independent of `trend`. |
| `hint` | `ReactNode` | no |  | A line of context under the figure. |
| `sparkline` | `ReactNode` | no |  | A chart beside the figure, usually a `Sparkline`. Give it `label={null}` or a label of its own. |
| `href` | `string` | no |  | Makes the whole tile a link: the label becomes the link and its hit area is stretched over the tile. |
| `onClick` | `MouseEventHandler<HTMLElement>` | no |  | Called on press. Alone, it makes the whole tile a button. Together with `href` it runs before navigation. |
| `pressed` | `boolean` | no |  | Turns a button tile into a toggle, for a row of tiles that filters a list: the button exposes `aria-pressed` and the tile shows a selected state (accent border and background, a thicker inset border and a check mark, so it is not colour alone). Ignored unless the tile is a button, so a link tile, a plain tile and a `loading` tile never get it. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Shows skeletons in place of the figure, the change, the hint and the chart, and disables the link or button. Each skeleton has the line box of the content it stands for, so the loaded tile has exactly the same height. Pass the same `delta`, `hint` and `sparkline` you will pass once loaded (placeholders are fine): they decide which lines are held. |
| `loadingLabel` | `string` | no |  | Accessible name of the loading state ("Loading pending items"). Without it the skeleton is silent. |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `StatTileTone`: `"neutral" | "success" | "warning" | "danger"`
- `StatTileTrend`: `"up" | "down" | "flat"`

### Example

```tsx
import { StatTile } from "@lufia/design-system/components/StatTile";
import { AnimatedNumber } from "@lufia/design-system/motion";
import { Sparkline } from "@lufia/design-system/components/Sparkline";

<StatTile
  label="Open items"
  value={<AnimatedNumber value={128} />}
  delta="12% vs last week"
  trend="up"
  trendLabel="Up"
  hint="Across all teams"
  sparkline={<Sparkline values={[3, 5, 4, 8, 6, 9, 12]} label={null} />}
  href="/items"
/>

<StatTile label="Open items" value="--" loading loadingLabel="Loading open items" />
```

### Accessibility

Keyboard:

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Interactive tile: focuses the link or button |
| Enter | Follows the link, or presses the button |
| Space | Presses the button |

- The accessible name of an interactive tile is its `label`. The figure, change and hint are its description.
- `trend` draws a decorative arrow. Say the direction in words with `trendLabel` ("Up") or inside `delta`, so the direction never rests on the arrow or the colour.
- `tone="warning"` and `"danger"` tint the tile. The label and hint must say why it needs attention.
- While `loading`, the tile is `aria-busy`, the link or button is removed and each skeleton takes the line box of what it replaces (the figure, the change, the hint, the chart), so the loaded tile has exactly the same height. Pass the same `delta`, `hint` and `sparkline` while loading as you will once loaded: they decide which lines are held. Set `loadingLabel` to announce it once.
- With `pressed`, the button is a toggle: screen readers announce "Open items, toggle button, pressed". Name the filter in the `label`, not in the state.
- In `forced-colors` mode the border is `CanvasText` (`Highlight` when pressed, with the check mark) and the focus ring `Highlight`.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has a `prefers-reduced-motion` branch.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-border-width-thick`, `--lufia-border-width-thin`, `--lufia-color-accent-border`, `--lufia-color-accent-default`, `--lufia-color-accent-subtle`, `--lufia-color-bg-surface`, `--lufia-color-border-subtle`, `--lufia-color-focus-ring`, `--lufia-color-status-danger-bg`, `--lufia-color-status-danger-border`, `--lufia-color-status-danger-fg`, `--lufia-color-status-success-fg`, `--lufia-color-status-warning-bg`, `--lufia-color-status-warning-border`, `--lufia-color-status-warning-fg`, `--lufia-color-text-default`, `--lufia-color-text-muted`, `--lufia-font-family-display`, `--lufia-font-family-mono`, `--lufia-font-line-height-normal`, `--lufia-font-size-2xl`, `--lufia-font-size-2xs`, `--lufia-font-size-3xl`, `--lufia-font-size-xs`, `--lufia-font-weight-bold`, `--lufia-font-weight-semibold`, `--lufia-motion-distance-nudge`, `--lufia-motion-duration-instant`, `--lufia-motion-easing-out`, `--lufia-radius-md`, `--lufia-shadow-md`, `--lufia-shadow-sm`, `--lufia-stat-tile-label-color`, `--lufia-stat-tile-label-font`, `--lufia-stat-tile-label-size`, `--lufia-stat-tile-label-tracking`, `--lufia-stat-tile-value-size`, `--lufia-stat-tile-value-size-narrow`.

### Stories

- `components-data-display-stattile--default`
- `components-data-display-stattile--themed-by-tokens`
- `components-data-display-stattile--with-delta`
- `components-data-display-stattile--falling-is-good`
- `components-data-display-stattile--flat`
- `components-data-display-stattile--with-sparkline`
- `components-data-display-stattile--warning`
- `components-data-display-stattile--danger`
- `components-data-display-stattile--success`
- `components-data-display-stattile--as-link`
- `components-data-display-stattile--as-button`
- `components-data-display-stattile--as-filters`
- `components-data-display-stattile--loading`
- `components-data-display-stattile--loading-keeps-height`
- `components-data-display-stattile--long-label`
- `components-data-display-stattile--with-animated-number`
- `components-data-display-stattile--in-flex-row`
- `components-data-display-stattile--grid`
- `components-data-display-stattile--phone-320`
- `components-data-display-stattile--right-to-left`
- `components-data-display-stattile--all-themes`

## StatusTimeline

> A vertical timeline of states with their dates.

- Status: beta
- Category: Data display
- Import: `import { StatusTimeline } from "@lufia/design-system/components/StatusTimeline"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/StatusTimeline](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/StatusTimeline)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-data-display-statustimeline--docs)

### Purpose

A vertical, connected timeline of obligations or steps grouped into tracks. Each node has an icon, a state pill, an
optional timestamp or deadline, a hint, and an optional inline action.

### When to use

- Tracking dated obligations or a multi-party process where order and status both matter.

### When not to use

- A simple progress indicator (use `Stepper`) or an activity feed.

### API

#### `StatusTimeline`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tracks` | `StatusTimelineTrack[]` | yes |  |  |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `StatusTimelineNode`: `{ id: string; label: string; state: StatusTimelineNodeState; stateLabel: string; timestampLabel?: string | undefined; deadlineLabel?: string | undefined; hint?: string | undefined; action?: ReactNode; }`
- `StatusTimelineNodeState`: `"needsTimestamp" | "pending" | "overdue" | "done" | "notApplicable"`
- `StatusTimelineProps`: `HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement> & { tracks: StatusTimelineTrack[]; }`
- `StatusTimelineTrack`: `{ id: string; title: string; nodes: StatusTimelineNode[]; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { StatusTimeline } from "@lufia/design-system/components/StatusTimeline";

<StatusTimeline
  tracks={[
    {
      id: "review",
      title: "Review",
      nodes: [
        {
          id: "n1",
          label: "Notify the team",
          state: "done",
          stateLabel: "Done",
          timestampLabel: formatted,
        },
      ],
    },
  ]}
/>;
```

### Accessibility

- Each track is a `<section>` with an `<h3>`; each node list is an ordered list, so order and count are announced.
- **State is named in words** through `stateLabel` in the pill; colour and icon are reinforcement only. Always pass a meaningful `stateLabel`.
- Overdue uses a solid fill, never a tint, so it cannot be read as pending. The danger fill uses a dedicated `on-solid` text token that passes AA in light and dark.
- Layout stays vertical at every width: no horizontal scrolling or truncated text at 320px.
- Actions are slots; keep them keyboard operable and labelled.
- In forced-colors mode the pill keeps a visible border.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-color-bg-surface-raised`, `--lufia-color-border-strong`, `--lufia-color-border-subtle`, `--lufia-color-status-danger-bg`, `--lufia-color-status-danger-fg`, `--lufia-color-status-danger-on-solid`, `--lufia-color-status-danger-solid`, `--lufia-color-status-neutral-bg`, `--lufia-color-status-neutral-fg`, `--lufia-color-status-success-bg`, `--lufia-color-status-success-fg`, `--lufia-color-status-warning-bg`, `--lufia-color-status-warning-border`, `--lufia-color-status-warning-fg`, `--lufia-color-text-muted`, `--lufia-color-text-subtle`, `--lufia-font-family-display`, `--lufia-font-family-mono`, `--lufia-font-weight-semibold`, `--lufia-radius-sm`, `--lufia-space-1`, `--lufia-space-2`, `--lufia-space-3`, `--lufia-space-4`, `--lufia-space-5`.

### Content guidelines

All text arrives formatted and localised (dates in the user's locale: `5 Nov 2026` vs `05/11/2026`). Avoid colour words
("red") in labels.

### Stories

- `components-data-display-statustimeline--default`
- `components-data-display-statustimeline--single-track`
- `components-data-display-statustimeline--empty-track-omitted`
- `components-data-display-statustimeline--long-content`
- `components-data-display-statustimeline--all-themes`

## Stepper

> Shows progress through a short, ordered flow.

- Status: beta
- Category: Navigation
- Import: `import { Stepper } from "@lufia/design-system/components/Stepper"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/Stepper](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/Stepper)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-navigation-stepper--docs)

### Purpose

A mobile-first step indicator. Below 600px it shows a compact "2 / 4" caption with the active label; from 600px it
expands into a numbered row with connectors that fill as the user progresses.

### When to use

- Short linear flows (wizards, multi-step forms) of 3 to 7 steps.

### When not to use

- Non-linear navigation (use tabs) or dated process tracking (use `StatusTimeline`).

### API

#### `Stepper`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `steps` | `StepDef[]` | yes |  |  |
| `current` | `number` | yes |  | Index of the active step (0-based). |
| `onStepClick` | `(index: number) => void` | no |  | Optional: jump to an already-visited step. |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `StepDef`: `{ key: string; label: string; }`
- `StepperProps`: `Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>, "children"> & { steps: StepDef[]; current: number; onStepClick?: ((index: number) => void) | undefined; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { Stepper } from "@lufia/design-system/components/Stepper";

<Stepper steps={steps} current={index} onStepClick={setIndex} />;
```

### Accessibility

- A visually hidden `role="status"` live region announces "2 / 4: Review" when `current` changes, at every viewport.
- The active step's list item has `aria-current="step"`; every step exposes the name "2. Review" (visually hidden text, or the button's `aria-label`).
- Only already-visited steps are rendered as buttons, and only when `onStepClick` is given. Upcoming and current steps are plain text, so there are no disabled controls to Tab past. Without a handler the component is purely informational.
- Dots are 32px; focus shows a 2px ring. The connector fill is a transform transition and stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`. In forced-colors mode connectors use `CanvasText`.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has a `prefers-reduced-motion` branch.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-border-width-thick`, `--lufia-color-accent-default`, `--lufia-color-bg-surface-solid`, `--lufia-color-border-subtle`, `--lufia-color-focus-ring`, `--lufia-color-text-accent`, `--lufia-color-text-default`, `--lufia-color-text-muted`, `--lufia-color-text-on-accent`, `--lufia-font-family-mono`, `--lufia-motion-duration-enter`, `--lufia-motion-easing-out`, `--lufia-space-1`, `--lufia-space-2`, `--lufia-space-3`.

### Content guidelines

Step labels are short nouns (one or two words). The mobile caption shows the full active label, so it may be longer than
what fits under a dot.

### Stories

- `components-navigation-stepper--default`
- `components-navigation-stepper--first-step`
- `components-navigation-stepper--last-step`
- `components-navigation-stepper--read-only`
- `components-navigation-stepper--long-labels`
- `components-navigation-stepper--mobile`
- `components-navigation-stepper--interactive`
- `components-navigation-stepper--all-themes`

## SuccessCheck

> An animated check mark for a completed action.

- Status: beta
- Category: Feedback
- Import: `import { SuccessCheck } from "@lufia/design-system/components/SuccessCheck"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/SuccessCheck](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/SuccessCheck)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-feedback-successcheck--docs)

### Purpose

A check mark whose stroke draws in once as it appears. The shared "it worked" mark: toasts use it for the success tone.

### When to use

- Confirming that something completed, next to text that says what.

### When not to use

- As the only signal of success, or as a status icon in a list (it animates every time it mounts). Use a status badge.

### API

#### `SuccessCheck`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `number` | no | `16` | Rendered width and height, in px. |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `SuccessCheckProps`: `Omit<SVGAttributes<SVGSVGElement>, "width" | "height" | "viewBox" | "children"> & { size?: number | undefined; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { SuccessCheck } from "@lufia/design-system/components/SuccessCheck";

<p style={{ color: "var(--lufia-color-status-success-fg)" }}>
  <SuccessCheck /> Changes saved
</p>;
```

### Accessibility

- Decorative: `aria-hidden="true"` and `focusable="false"`. The adjacent text carries the meaning, so the check is never the only cue.
- The draw uses `--lufia-motion-duration-enter` and stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`, leaving the finished check.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has a `prefers-reduced-motion` branch.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-motion-duration-enter`, `--lufia-motion-easing-out`.

### Stories

- `components-feedback-successcheck--default`
- `components-feedback-successcheck--large`
- `components-feedback-successcheck--all-themes`

## Switch

> An on/off control whose change takes effect immediately.

- Status: beta
- Category: Forms
- Import: `import { Switch, SwitchInput } from "@lufia/design-system/components/Switch"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/Switch](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/Switch)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-forms-switch--docs)

### Purpose

An on/off control for a setting that takes effect immediately: a `role="switch"` button with a label, an optional hint and
error, and a thumb that slides.

### When to use

- A setting that applies at once, with no Save button: notifications, dark mode, a feature flag.

### When not to use

- A choice that is submitted later with a form: use `Checkbox`, or `SwitchInput` when an on/off switch reads better.
- A choice between two named options that are not on and off ("Monthly" or "Yearly"): use `SegmentedToggle`.

### Exports

| Name | Kind |
| --- | --- |
| `Switch` | component |
| `SwitchInput` | component |

### API

#### `Switch`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | no |  | Submitted as `name=value` while on, like a checkbox. Without `name` nothing is submitted. |
| `defaultChecked` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Initial state when `checked` is not given. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | The visible label. Clicking it toggles the switch. |
| `hint` | `ReactNode` | no |  |  |
| `error` | `ReactNode` | no |  |  |
| `checked` | `boolean` | no |  | Controlled state. |
| `onCheckedChange` | `(checked: boolean) => void` | no |  |  |
| `value` | `string` | no | `"on"` |  |
| `className` | `string` | no |  | Goes on the root element. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLButtonElement>` | no |  |  |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

#### `SwitchInput`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | The visible label. Clicking it toggles the switch. |
| `hint` | `ReactNode` | no |  |  |
| `error` | `ReactNode` | no |  |  |
| `value` | `string` | no | `"on"` | Submitted as `name=value` while on. Defaults to `"on"`, like a checkbox. |
| `onCheckedChange` | `(checked: boolean) => void` | no |  | Called with the new state. A plain `onChange` also works; both fire. |
| `className` | `string` | no |  | Goes on the root element. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLInputElement>` | no |  |  |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Example

```tsx
import { Switch } from "@lufia/design-system/components/Switch";

<Switch label="Email alerts" hint="One message a day, at most." checked={on} onCheckedChange={save} />;
```

### Accessibility

Follows the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices pattern: [Switch](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/switch/).

- `SwitchInput` is a native checkbox with `role="switch"`, so the checked state is exposed natively and Space toggles it (Enter does not, as on any checkbox); the label, hint and error wiring is the same.
- `role="switch"` with `aria-checked`, on a `<button>`. The label is a real `<label for>`; the track is 44 by 28px.
- If saving can fail, do the optimistic update, and on failure set the state back and pass `error`.
- Under `forced-colors` the on track uses `Highlight` and the thumb `HighlightText`. The thumb slides with `transform`, mirrored in right-to-left, and stays still under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-border-width-thick`, `--lufia-color-accent-default`, `--lufia-color-bg-surface-raised`, `--lufia-color-border-strong`, `--lufia-color-focus-ring`, `--lufia-color-status-danger-fg`, `--lufia-color-text-default`, `--lufia-color-text-muted`, `--lufia-color-text-on-accent`, `--lufia-font-line-height-normal`, `--lufia-font-size-md`, `--lufia-motion-duration-fast`, `--lufia-motion-duration-instant`, `--lufia-motion-easing-out`, `--lufia-opacity-disabled`, `--lufia-radius-full`, `--lufia-space-1`, `--lufia-space-3`.

### Content guidelines

Name the setting as a noun phrase ("Email alerts", "Dark mode"). The hint says what happens when it is on. Do not use a verb
that flips meaning with the state ("Enable alerts").

### Stories

- `components-forms-switch--default`
- `components-forms-switch--on`
- `components-forms-switch--with-hint`
- `components-forms-switch--invalid`
- `components-forms-switch--disabled`
- `components-forms-switch--disabled-on`
- `components-forms-switch--controlled`
- `components-forms-switch--in-form`
- `components-forms-switch--input-states`
- `components-forms-switch--input-right-to-left`
- `components-forms-switch--long-text`
- `components-forms-switch--phone-320`
- `components-forms-switch--right-to-left`
- `components-forms-switch--all-themes`

## TableToolbar

> The search, filter and action row above a table.

- Status: beta
- Category: Data display
- Import: `import { TableToolbar } from "@lufia/design-system/components/TableToolbar"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/TableToolbar](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/TableToolbar)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-data-display-tabletoolbar--docs)

### Purpose

Filter chips plus an optional search box for the top of a table or list. Extra controls (for example a dropdown for an
open-ended filter) go in as children.

### When to use

- Narrowing a list by a handful of mutually exclusive statuses, and free-text search.

### When not to use

- Many-valued filters (use a dropdown in `children`) or multi-select faceting (a different pattern).

### API

#### `TableToolbar`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `filters` | `FilterOption[]` | no |  |  |
| `activeFilter` | `string` | no |  |  |
| `onFilterChange` | `(key: string) => void` | no |  |  |
| `search` | `string` | no |  |  |
| `onSearchChange` | `(value: string) => void` | no |  | The search field renders only when this handler is provided. |
| `searchPlaceholder` | `string` | no |  |  |
| `clearSearchLabel` | `string` | no | `"Clear search"` | Accessible name of the search field's clear button. Required whenever search is shown. |
| `variant` | `"inline" \| "standalone"` | no | `"inline"` | Layout variant: "inline" sits inside a surface (bottom border); "standalone" has outer spacing. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Extra controls, such as dropdowns for open-ended lists, rendered before the search box. |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `FilterOption`: `{ key: string; label: string; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { TableToolbar } from "@lufia/design-system/components/TableToolbar";

<TableToolbar
  filters={[
    { key: "all", label: "All" },
    { key: "open", label: "Open" },
  ]}
  activeFilter={filter}
  onFilterChange={setFilter}
  search={query}
  onSearchChange={setQuery}
  searchPlaceholder="Search items"
  clearSearchLabel="Clear search"
/>;
```

### Accessibility

- Chips are toggle buttons with `aria-pressed`; the group has `role="group"` (add `aria-label` through props to name it).
- The search input is `type="search"` and named by its placeholder text. **Always pass `searchPlaceholder`** (localised); it doubles as the accessible name. The clear button needs `clearSearchLabel`; the default is English.
- The search wrapper shows the focus ring through `:focus-within`, so the native outline is replaced, never removed.
- Chips are at least 44px tall on coarse pointers and narrow screens; the row wraps instead of scrolling at 320px.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-border-width-thick`, `--lufia-border-width-thin`, `--lufia-color-accent-subtle`, `--lufia-color-bg-surface`, `--lufia-color-border-strong`, `--lufia-color-border-subtle`, `--lufia-color-focus-ring`, `--lufia-color-text-accent`, `--lufia-color-text-default`, `--lufia-color-text-muted`, `--lufia-color-text-subtle`, `--lufia-font-family-mono`, `--lufia-motion-duration-instant`, `--lufia-radius-md`, `--lufia-space-2`, `--lufia-space-3`, `--lufia-space-4`.

### Content guidelines

Chip labels are one or two words. Do not put counts in colour alone; include them in the label text if useful.

### Stories

- `components-data-display-tabletoolbar--default`
- `components-data-display-tabletoolbar--with-search-value`
- `components-data-display-tabletoolbar--filters-only`
- `components-data-display-tabletoolbar--search-only`
- `components-data-display-tabletoolbar--standalone`
- `components-data-display-tabletoolbar--with-extra-controls`
- `components-data-display-tabletoolbar--many-filters`
- `components-data-display-tabletoolbar--interactive`
- `components-data-display-tabletoolbar--all-themes`

## TextInput

> A single-line text field with optional prefix and suffix.

- Status: beta
- Category: Forms
- Import: `import { TextInput } from "@lufia/design-system/components/TextInput"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/TextInput](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/TextInput)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-forms-textinput--docs)

### Purpose

A single-line text control: a native `<input>` in a bordered box, with optional prefix and suffix slots for units, signs and
icons.

### When to use

- Short free text, numbers, e-mail, URLs, passwords: anything that fits on one line.
- Set `type`, `inputMode` and `autoComplete` for the data: they pick the on-screen keyboard and enable autofill.

### When not to use

- More than one line of text: use `Textarea`.
- A choice from a known list: use `Select` or `Combobox`.
- Searching: use `SearchInput`, which adds a clear button and debouncing.

### API

#### `TextInput`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `prefix` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Content before the text: a unit, a currency sign, a decorative icon (give an icon `aria-hidden`). |
| `suffix` | `ReactNode` | no |  | Content after the text: a unit, a button. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | no |  | Marks the control invalid without a `FormField`. Inside a field the error does it. |
| `className` | `string` | no |  | Goes on the box that draws the border; the native input gets the rest props. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLInputElement>` | no |  |  |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Types

- `TextInputProps`: `Omit<InputHTMLAttributes<HTMLInputElement>, "className" | "prefix" | "size"> & { prefix?: ReactNode; suffix?: ReactNode; invalid?: boolean | undefined; className?: string | undefined; ref?: Ref<HTMLInputElement> | undefined; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { FormField } from "@lufia/design-system/components/FormField";
import { TextInput } from "@lufia/design-system/components/TextInput";

<FormField label="Amount" hint="Without tax." error={errors.amount}>
  <TextInput name="amount" prefix="EUR" inputMode="decimal" />
</FormField>;
```

### Accessibility

- Always inside a `FormField`, or give `aria-label`. A placeholder is not a label.
- The box draws a 2px focus ring around the whole control; the native outline is replaced, not removed. Under `forced-colors` the ring uses `Highlight`, and an invalid control gets a thicker border.
- Height is at least 44px; the text is 16px so iOS does not zoom on focus.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Its stylesheet reads no `--lufia-*` tokens directly (no CSS module, or it composes other components).

### Content guidelines

Placeholders show an example ("Quarterly report"), never an instruction and never the label again. Units go in the prefix or
suffix, not in the label. Keep error text next to the field, in the `FormField`.

### Stories

- `components-forms-textinput--default`
- `components-forms-textinput--with-value`
- `components-forms-textinput--with-hint`
- `components-forms-textinput--required`
- `components-forms-textinput--invalid`
- `components-forms-textinput--disabled`
- `components-forms-textinput--read-only`
- `components-forms-textinput--prefix`
- `components-forms-textinput--suffix`
- `components-forms-textinput--prefix-and-suffix`
- `components-forms-textinput--with-icon`
- `components-forms-textinput--password`
- `components-forms-textinput--long-text`
- `components-forms-textinput--phone-320`
- `components-forms-textinput--right-to-left`
- `components-forms-textinput--all-themes`

## Textarea

> A multi-line text field that can show a character count.

- Status: beta
- Category: Forms
- Import: `import { Textarea } from "@lufia/design-system/components/Textarea"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/Textarea](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/Textarea)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-forms-textarea--docs)

### Purpose

A multi-line text control with the same box as `TextInput`, vertical resizing and an optional character count.

### When to use

- Free text that may run past one line: notes, descriptions, messages.

### When not to use

- A short value: use `TextInput`. Do not stretch a textarea to look like an input.
- Formatted text. This is plain text only.

### API

#### `Textarea`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | no |  | Marks the control invalid without a `FormField`. Inside a field the error does it. |
| `showCount` | `boolean` | no |  | Shows a character count under the box. With `maxLength` it reads "12 / 200". |
| `formatCount` | `(length: number, max: number \| undefined) => ReactNode` | no | `defaultCount` | Text of the count. Defaults to `12 / 200` with a limit and `12` without. Pass it to localise or reword. |
| `formatCountAnnouncement` | `(length: number, max: number) => string` | no | `defaultAnnouncement` | Text read out when the person is close to the limit (the last tenth) or over it. Aria-only. |
| `className` | `string` | no |  | Goes on the box that draws the border; the native textarea gets the rest props. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLTextAreaElement>` | no |  |  |

Other native element attributes pass through to the root element.

### Example

```tsx
import { FormField } from "@lufia/design-system/components/FormField";
import { Textarea } from "@lufia/design-system/components/Textarea";

<FormField label="Notes" hint="Visible to everyone on the project.">
  <Textarea name="notes" rows={5} maxLength={500} showCount />
</FormField>;
```

### Accessibility

- The resize handle is vertical only, so the box cannot grow wider than its container at 320px.
- Focus ring, forced-colors and invalid styling match `TextInput`.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-color-status-warning-fg`, `--lufia-color-text-muted`, `--lufia-font-size-xs`, `--lufia-font-weight-bold`, `--lufia-space-1`.

### Content guidelines

Say how much is expected in the hint ("A sentence or two is enough"). Show the count only when a limit exists or matters.
Phrase `formatCount` as what is left ("12 characters left") when the limit is tight.

### Stories

- `components-forms-textarea--default`
- `components-forms-textarea--with-hint`
- `components-forms-textarea--required`
- `components-forms-textarea--invalid`
- `components-forms-textarea--disabled`
- `components-forms-textarea--read-only`
- `components-forms-textarea--with-count`
- `components-forms-textarea--near-limit`
- `components-forms-textarea--count-without-limit`
- `components-forms-textarea--custom-count`
- `components-forms-textarea--controlled`
- `components-forms-textarea--long-text`
- `components-forms-textarea--phone-320`
- `components-forms-textarea--right-to-left`
- `components-forms-textarea--all-themes`

## Toast

> A transient message that confirms an action without taking focus.

- Status: beta
- Category: Feedback
- Import: `import { ToastProvider, useOptionalToast, useToast } from "@lufia/design-system/components/Toast"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/Toast](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/Toast)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-feedback-toast--docs)

### Purpose

Short, non-blocking notifications that stack in a corner of the screen, are announced to screen readers, close by
themselves and wait while they are hovered or focused. Mount `ToastProvider` once, call `useToast()` anywhere below.

### When to use

- Confirming something the person just did that needs no decision: saved, copied, sent, restored.
- Reporting a background result they might have missed: sync finished, upload failed.
- Offering **Undo** right after a reversible action. It is better than a confirmation dialog.

### When not to use

- Anything that must be answered or read before moving on: use [ConfirmDialog](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-overlays-confirmdialog--docs) or an inline message. A toast disappears, so a form's validation errors do not belong in one.
- Information the person will need again (instructions, a long explanation). Put it on the page.
- More than one at a time for the same outcome: identical string messages are de-duplicated, and `limit` caps the stack.

### Exports

| Name | Kind |
| --- | --- |
| `ToastProvider` | component |
| `useOptionalToast` | hook |
| `useToast` | hook |

### API

#### `ToastProvider`

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | yes |  |  |
| `placement` | `"bottom-end" \| "bottom-start" \| "top-end" \| "top-start"` | no | `"bottom-end"` | Corner of the viewport the stack sits in. Default `bottom-end`. |
| `limit` | `number` | no | `5` | The most toasts shown at once; older ones leave first. Default 5. |
| `duration` | `number` | no | `DEFAULT_DURATION_MS` | Default time before a toast closes, in ms. Default 5000. Errors and toasts with an action stay until dismissed. |
| `container` | `Element \| "auto" \| null` | no | `"auto"` | Where the notification region is rendered. `"auto"` (default) hosts it inside the topmost open modal `<dialog>` while there is one, so toasts stay visible above a native top-layer dialog (a `Modal` with `renderAs="dialog"`), and in `document.body` otherwise. Pass an element to always render there, or `null` for `document.body` only. |
| `toneAliases` | `Readonly<Record<string, ToastTone>>` | no |  | Names an app uses for tones, mapped to built-in ones: `{ ok: "success", warn: "warning" }`. |
| `viewportClassName` | `string` | no |  | A class for the notification region (the fixed viewport that holds the stacks), for an app's own placement or width rules. |

#### `useOptionalToast`

The toast API when rendered inside a `ToastProvider`, otherwise `null`: for code that may run outside one.

```ts
useOptionalToast(): ToastApi | null
```

Returned members:

| Member | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `show` | `(options: ToastOptions) => string` | yes | Shows a toast and returns its id. A string message with the same tone as a visible toast is not shown twice. |
| `info` | `(message: ReactNode, options?: Omit<ToastOptions, "message" \| "tone"> \| undefined) => string` | yes |  |
| `success` | `(message: ReactNode, options?: Omit<ToastOptions, "message" \| "tone"> \| undefined) => string` | yes |  |
| `warning` | `(message: ReactNode, options?: Omit<ToastOptions, "message" \| "tone"> \| undefined) => string` | yes |  |
| `error` | `(message: ReactNode, options?: Omit<ToastOptions, "message" \| "tone"> \| undefined) => string` | yes |  |
| `dismiss` | `(id: string) => void` | yes |  |
| `clear` | `() => void` | yes | Dismisses every toast. |

#### `useToast`

Show and dismiss notifications. Must be used inside a `ToastProvider`.

```ts
useToast(): ToastApi
```

Returned members:

| Member | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `show` | `(options: ToastOptions) => string` | yes | Shows a toast and returns its id. A string message with the same tone as a visible toast is not shown twice. |
| `info` | `(message: ReactNode, options?: Omit<ToastOptions, "message" \| "tone"> \| undefined) => string` | yes |  |
| `success` | `(message: ReactNode, options?: Omit<ToastOptions, "message" \| "tone"> \| undefined) => string` | yes |  |
| `warning` | `(message: ReactNode, options?: Omit<ToastOptions, "message" \| "tone"> \| undefined) => string` | yes |  |
| `error` | `(message: ReactNode, options?: Omit<ToastOptions, "message" \| "tone"> \| undefined) => string` | yes |  |
| `dismiss` | `(id: string) => void` | yes |  |
| `clear` | `() => void` | yes | Dismisses every toast. |

### Types

- `ToastAction`: `{ label: string; onAction: () => void; }`
- `ToastOptions`: `{ message: ReactNode; tone?: ToastToneName | undefined; action?: ToastAction | undefined; duration?: number | null | undefined; id?: string | undefined; }`
- `ToastPlacement`: `"bottom-end" | "bottom-start" | "top-end" | "top-start"`
- `ToastProviderProps`: `{ children: ReactNode; placement?: ToastPlacement | undefined; limit?: number | undefined; duration?: number | undefined; container?: Element | "auto" | null | undefined; toneAliases?: Readonly<Record<string, ToastTone>> | undefined; viewportClassName?: string | undefined; }`
- `ToastTone`: `"info" | "success" | "warning" | "error"`
- `ToastToneName`: `(string & {}) | ToastTone`

### Example

```tsx
import { ToastProvider, useToast } from "@lufia/design-system/components/Toast";

// once, near the root (inside LufiaProvider if you translate the aria labels)
<ToastProvider placement="bottom-end">{children}</ToastProvider>;

// anywhere below
const toast = useToast();
toast.success("Changes saved.");
toast.error("Upload failed.");
toast.info("Invoice moved to the trash.", { action: { label: "Undo", onAction: restore } });
```

### Accessibility

Follows the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices pattern: [Alert](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/alert/).

- Announcing is separate from showing. Visually hidden live regions (`role="alert"` for errors, `role="status"` for the rest) hold a text copy of each message. One pair lives in `document.body`; another is created inside each open modal `<dialog>` for as long as it is open, because the browser makes the body inert behind it. A message goes to the announcer of the topmost open dialog, or the body's, and each one exists before anything is added to it. The visible stack is a labelled `region` that moves into the topmost dialog and back. Errors interrupt, the rest wait.
- The announcer regions keep `role="alert"` and `role="status"` while empty, on purpose. A live region only announces content added after it exists, so both must be mounted first. `aria-live` alone is meant to be enough, but the explicit role is what the screen reader and browser pairs we know of announce most reliably (older VoiceOver and JAWS builds are the usual failures with a bare `aria-live`), and `role="alert"` is what marks the assertive region as errors. An empty live region is not read out, so the node costs nothing to users. We kept the roles rather than risk a silent toast.
- In tests the copy means `getByText` can find the message twice. Assert what is announced with `getByRole("status")` (`"alert"` for errors) and query the visible toast inside the `Notifications` region.
- Keyboard: toasts are reached in DOM order with Tab; each has its action (if any) and a dismiss button. Escape on a focused toast dismisses it. While a toast has focus its timer is paused.
- The notification region stays live while a [Modal](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-overlays-modal--docs) is open (the modal marks the rest of the page `inert`, except `data-lufia-inert-exempt`), though Tab cycles only inside the modal while it is open.
- Targets: the dismiss button and action are at least 28 px tall (WCAG 2.5.8 asks for 24 px).
- Motion: enter 240 ms and exit 160 ms, `transform` and `opacity` only, direction follows the placement. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` toasts appear and disappear at once. The success check (`SuccessCheck`) stops drawing.
- Colour is never the only signal: each tone has its own icon, and the message says what happened. Under `forced-colors` the border uses system colours.
- Not recorded yet: a manual VoiceOver and NVDA pass (required before `stable`).

### Motion

| Toast                         | Closes by itself?                                       |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `info`, `success`, `warning`  | After `duration` (5 s).                                 |
| `error`                       | Never, unless `duration` says so.                       |
| Any toast with an `action`    | Never, unless `duration` says so.                       |
| Any toast, hovered or focused | Paused; resumes with at least 1.5 s left when released. |

This follows WCAG 2.2.1 (Timing Adjustable): errors carry the most important and often the longest text, and an action
needs time to be found.

Its stylesheet has a `prefers-reduced-motion` branch.

### Tokens

Reads these semantic tokens: `--lufia-border-width-thin`, `--lufia-color-accent-default`, `--lufia-color-accent-subtle`, `--lufia-color-bg-surface-raised`, `--lufia-color-bg-surface-solid`, `--lufia-color-border-strong`, `--lufia-color-focus-ring`, `--lufia-color-status-danger-bg`, `--lufia-color-status-danger-fg`, `--lufia-color-status-neutral-bg`, `--lufia-color-status-success-bg`, `--lufia-color-status-success-fg`, `--lufia-color-status-warning-bg`, `--lufia-color-status-warning-fg`, `--lufia-color-text-accent`, `--lufia-color-text-default`, `--lufia-color-text-muted`, `--lufia-font-line-height-normal`, `--lufia-font-size-md`, `--lufia-font-weight-semibold`, `--lufia-motion-distance-slide`, `--lufia-motion-duration-enter`, `--lufia-motion-duration-exit`, `--lufia-motion-duration-instant`, `--lufia-motion-easing-in`, `--lufia-motion-easing-out`, `--lufia-radius-card`, `--lufia-radius-full`, `--lufia-radius-md`, `--lufia-shadow-md`, `--lufia-space-3`, `--lufia-space-4`, `--lufia-space-5`, `--lufia-space-6`, `--lufia-toast-align-items`, `--lufia-toast-border-width`, `--lufia-toast-gap`, `--lufia-toast-icon-size`, `--lufia-toast-line-height`, `--lufia-toast-max-width`, `--lufia-toast-min-width`, `--lufia-toast-offset-block`, `--lufia-toast-padding-block`, `--lufia-toast-padding-inline`, `--lufia-toast-padding-inline-end`, `--lufia-toast-padding-inline-start`, `--lufia-toast-radius`, `--lufia-toast-width`, `--lufia-z-toast`.

### Content guidelines

One sentence, past tense for results ("Changes saved."), the object for failures ("Upload failed. Check your connection
and try again."). Say what to do after an error. Actions are a verb ("Undo", "Retry"). Never put a link that leads
somewhere in a toast that vanishes.

### Stories

- `components-feedback-toast--default`
- `components-feedback-toast--all-tones`
- `components-feedback-toast--top-start`
- `components-feedback-toast--long-message`
- `components-feedback-toast--phone`
- `components-feedback-toast--above-a-native-dialog`
- `components-feedback-toast--themed-by-tokens`
- `components-feedback-toast--tone-aliases`
- `components-feedback-toast--above-a-modal`

## VisuallyHidden

> Hides text visually and keeps it for assistive technology.

- Status: beta
- Category: Utilities
- Import: `import { VisuallyHidden } from "@lufia/design-system/components/VisuallyHidden"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/VisuallyHidden](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/VisuallyHidden)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/components-utilities-visuallyhidden--docs)

### Purpose

Text for assistive technology that is not drawn on screen.

### When to use

- A longer or more specific name than the visible text (which row does "Delete" act on?).
- Status text announced from a live region without a visible counterpart.

### When not to use

- Instead of `aria-label` on an element that has no text of its own: the attribute is simpler.
- To hide content that should be visible. Never put focusable elements inside it: they would be reachable but invisible.

### API

#### `VisuallyHidden`

No props of its own. Native element attributes pass through.

### Types

- `VisuallyHiddenProps`: `HTMLAttributes<HTMLSpanElement>`

### Example

```tsx
import { VisuallyHidden } from "@lufia/design-system/components/VisuallyHidden";

<button type="button">
  <span aria-hidden="true">Delete</span>
  <VisuallyHidden>Delete invoice 2041</VisuallyHidden>
</button>;
```

### Accessibility

- It uses the clip pattern (not `display: none`), so the text stays in the accessibility tree.
- WCAG 2.5.3 (Label in Name): when the visible label differs from the accessible name, the accessible name must contain the visible text.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Its stylesheet reads no `--lufia-*` tokens directly (no CSS module, or it composes other components).

### Stories

- `components-utilities-visuallyhidden--default`
- `components-utilities-visuallyhidden--all-themes`

## useBodyScrollLock

> Locks page scrolling while an overlay is open, without layout shift.

- Status: beta
- Category: Hooks
- Import: `import { isBodyScrollLocked, useBodyScrollLock } from "@lufia/design-system/components/useBodyScrollLock"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/useBodyScrollLock](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/useBodyScrollLock)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/hooks-usebodyscrolllock--docs)

### Purpose

A hook that locks page scroll while an overlay (modal, drawer, sheet) is open, and restores the scroll position when it
closes. Locks are reference counted, so stacked overlays are safe.

### When to use

- See the Storybook page.

### When not to use

- See the Storybook page.

### Exports

| Name | Kind |
| --- | --- |
| `isBodyScrollLocked` | function |
| `useBodyScrollLock` | hook |

### API

#### `isBodyScrollLocked`

Whether any overlay currently holds the lock. For consumers outside the component tree that rendered the overlay (for example a document-level gesture handler). It reads a counter rather than sniffing styles, because the two lock strategies leave different style fingerprints.

```ts
isBodyScrollLocked(): boolean
```

#### `useBodyScrollLock`

```ts
useBodyScrollLock(locked: boolean, options?: UseBodyScrollLockOptions): void
```

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `locked` | `boolean` | yes |  |
| `options` | `UseBodyScrollLockOptions` | no |  |

### Types

- `UseBodyScrollLockOptions`: `{ scrollContainerSelectors?: readonly string[] | undefined; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { useBodyScrollLock } from "@lufia/design-system/components/useBodyScrollLock";

function Modal({ open }: { open: boolean }) {
  useBodyScrollLock(open);
  // ...
}
```

### Accessibility

- Locking scroll does not move focus or trap it. Pair it with a focus trap and `aria-modal` on the dialog.
- The previous scroll position is restored on release, so keyboard and screen-reader users return to where they were.
- It only touches inline styles (`overflow`, `position`, `top`, `width`, `padding-right`, `overscroll-behavior`) and removes them on cleanup, including on unmount.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Its stylesheet reads no `--lufia-*` tokens directly (no CSS module, or it composes other components).

### Stories

- `hooks-usebodyscrolllock--document-scroll`
- `hooks-usebodyscrolllock--inner-scroll-shell`

## useDismiss

> Calls back on Escape or an outside press, for popovers and menus.

- Status: beta
- Category: Hooks
- Import: `import { useDismiss } from "@lufia/design-system/components/useDismiss"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/useDismiss](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/useDismiss)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/hooks-usedismiss--docs)

### Purpose

Closes a non-modal popup (dropdown, menu, popover) when Escape is pressed or the pointer presses outside it.

### When to use

- Menus, dropdowns, popovers and disclosure panels that sit over the page without blocking it.

### When not to use

- Modal overlays. They trap focus and own Escape: use `Modal` or `useFocusTrap`.

### API

#### `useDismiss`

Closes a non-modal popup (dropdown, menu, popover) on Escape or a pointer press outside it. Escape returns focus to the `toggle` that opened it. A copy with no layout boxes (a desktop and a phone instance of the same control, one hidden by CSS) never listens, so the two do not close each other.

```ts
useDismiss(open: boolean, close: () => void, root: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>, toggle?: RefObject<HTMLElement | null> | undefined, portalled?: RefObject<HTMLElement | null> | undefined): void
```

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` | `boolean` | yes |  |
| `close` | `() => void` | yes |  |
| `root` | `RefObject<HTMLElement \| null>` | yes |  |
| `toggle` | `RefObject<HTMLElement \| null>` | no |  |
| `portalled` | `RefObject<HTMLElement \| null>` | no | A second element that counts as inside, for a popup portalled out of `root`. |

### Example

```tsx
import { useDismiss } from "@lufia/design-system/components/useDismiss";

useDismiss(open, () => setOpen(false), rootRef, toggleRef);
```

### Accessibility

- Escape closes and returns focus to the control that opened the popup (WAI-ARIA APG menu button pattern). The key is ignored when another handler already used it (`defaultPrevented`), so a nested control can claim it first.
- Tab is not intercepted: leaving the popup by keyboard is allowed, and the consumer decides whether that closes it.
- A hidden copy of the control (same component rendered for desktop and phone, one hidden by CSS) never listens, because it has no layout boxes.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Its stylesheet reads no `--lufia-*` tokens directly (no CSS module, or it composes other components).

### Stories

- `hooks-usedismiss--default`

## useFocusTrap

> Keeps Tab inside a container and restores focus when it closes.

- Status: beta
- Category: Hooks
- Import: `import { getFocusableElements, hasOpenOverlay, isTopOverlayLayer, overlayDepth, registerOverlayLayer, useFocusTrap } from "@lufia/design-system/components/useFocusTrap"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/useFocusTrap](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/useFocusTrap)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/hooks-usefocustrap--docs)

### Purpose

Keeps keyboard focus inside an overlay while it is open: Tab and Shift+Tab wrap, Escape can close it, focus moves in when
it opens and returns to the opener when it closes. It is what `Modal` and `ConfirmDialog` are built on.

### When to use

- Any overlay that blocks the page behind it: dialogs, drawers, sheets.

### When not to use

- Non-modal popovers, menus and dropdowns. They close on Escape or an outside press and let Tab leave; use a dismiss helper instead.
- A native `<dialog>` opened with `showModal()`. The browser already traps focus.

### Exports

| Name | Kind |
| --- | --- |
| `getFocusableElements` | function |
| `hasOpenOverlay` | function |
| `isTopOverlayLayer` | function |
| `overlayDepth` | function |
| `registerOverlayLayer` | function |
| `useFocusTrap` | hook |

### API

#### `getFocusableElements`

The tabbable descendants of `root`, in keyboard Tab order. Not `offsetParent`-based: that is `null` for fixed-position children. Positive tabindex values precede the natural DOM order; negative tabindex values are only programmatically focusable.

```ts
getFocusableElements(root: HTMLElement): HTMLElement[]
```

#### `hasOpenOverlay`

Whether any layer is open on the shared overlay stack. The same as `overlayDepth() > 0`. Use it to leave a global shortcut or an outside-press handler alone while a dialog or popup is open. Read-only and not reactive.

```ts
hasOpenOverlay(): boolean
```

#### `isTopOverlayLayer`

Whether `layer` is the topmost registered layer. Same as `layer.isTop()`.

```ts
isTopOverlayLayer(layer: OverlayLayer): boolean
```

#### `overlayDepth`
