How many layers are open on the shared overlay stack right now: package modals and traps, dismissable popups that registered through `useDismiss`, and any layer an app registered with `registerOverlayLayer`. `0` when nothing is open. A read-only snapshot, not reactive: call it when you need it (in an event handler, in a key handler), not during render. Read it here instead of reaching for the `globalThis.__lufiaOverlayStack` key, which is an implementation detail.

```ts
overlayDepth(): number
```

#### `registerOverlayLayer`

Pushes a layer onto the stack shared by `useFocusTrap`, `useDismiss` and every other overlay that registers here, and returns a handle. Use it to make an overlay the package does not own (an app's legacy modal or trap) take part: the package's traps then leave Escape and Tab alone while it is on top, and it can ask `isTop()` before handling them itself. Release it when the overlay closes. Registering again moves a layer to the top, so register once per open (an effect keyed on `open` only), not on every render. A legacy overlay portaled into `document.body` above a package `Modal` must carry `data-lufia-inert-exempt`, otherwise the Modal makes it `inert` with the rest of the page.

```ts
registerOverlayLayer(): OverlayLayer
```

#### `useFocusTrap`

Contains Tab and Shift+Tab inside `ref`'s subtree while `open` is true, optionally closes on Escape, moves focus in when it opens and puts it back where it was when it closes. Follows the WAI-ARIA APG "Dialog (Modal)" pattern. Only the topmost layer reacts (see `useDismiss`: a popup inside the overlay counts as a layer), so nested overlays and popups close one at a time.

```ts
useFocusTrap(open: boolean, ref: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>, { onEscape, initialFocus, restoreFocus, inertBackground: inert, }?: UseFocusTrapOptions): void
```

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` | `boolean` | yes |  |
| `ref` | `RefObject<HTMLElement \| null>` | yes |  |
| `__2` | `UseFocusTrapOptions` | no |  |

### Types

- `OverlayLayer`: `{ isTop: () => boolean; release: () => void; }`
- `UseFocusTrapOptions`: `{ onEscape?: (() => void) | undefined; initialFocus?: "container" | "first" | RefObject<HTMLElement | null> | undefined; restoreFocus?: boolean | undefined; inertBackground?: boolean | undefined; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { useFocusTrap } from "@lufia/design-system/components/useFocusTrap";

function Panel({ open, onClose }: { open: boolean; onClose: () => void }) {
  const ref = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  useFocusTrap(open, ref, { onEscape: onClose });
  return open ? (
    <div ref={ref} role="dialog" aria-label="Filters" tabIndex={-1}>
      ...
    </div>
  ) : null;
}
```

### Accessibility

- The default `initialFocus` is the container, which needs a name (`aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`) and `tabIndex={-1}`. It avoids opening a mobile keyboard and never picks an action for the person. For a destructive confirmation, point `initialFocus` at the safe button.
- Tabbable elements are found by selector and visibility (`hidden`, `inert`, `display: none`, `visibility: hidden` are skipped). Fixed-position children count.
- On close, whatever is focused is blurred first (iOS Safari resets its zoom on a real blur), then focus is restored. If something moved focus elsewhere on purpose in the meantime, it is left alone.
- Pair it with `aria-modal="true"` on the dialog; `inertBackground` makes the effect real for browsers and assistive technologies that ignore `aria-modal`.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Its stylesheet reads no `--lufia-*` tokens directly (no CSS module, or it composes other components).

### Stories

- `hooks-usefocustrap--focus-container`
- `hooks-usefocustrap--focus-first-element`
- `hooks-usefocustrap--no-focus-restore`

## useMediaQuery

> Subscribes a component to a CSS media query, safe for server rendering.

- Status: beta
- Category: Hooks
- Import: `import { useMediaQuery } from "@lufia/design-system/components/useMediaQuery"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/useMediaQuery](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/useMediaQuery)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/hooks-usemediaquery--docs)

### Purpose

Whether a CSS media query matches right now, updated when it changes. Safe to server-render.

### When to use

- Behaviour that depends on the viewport or the input device: choosing a different interaction, not a different look.

### When not to use

- Styling. A CSS media or container query has no flash, no hydration pass and no JavaScript.
- Reduced motion. Use `usePrefersReducedMotion`.

### API

#### `useMediaQuery`

Whether a CSS media query currently matches, following changes. SSR-safe: the server renders `defaultValue`, and React re-reads the real value on hydration without a mismatch warning. Without `matchMedia` it returns `defaultValue`. Prefer CSS media queries for styling; use this when behaviour, not appearance, depends on the viewport.

```ts
useMediaQuery(query: string, { defaultValue }?: UseMediaQueryOptions): boolean
```

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `query` | `string` | yes |  |
| `__1` | `UseMediaQueryOptions` | no |  |

### Types

- `UseMediaQueryOptions`: `{ defaultValue?: boolean | undefined; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { useMediaQuery } from "@lufia/design-system/components/useMediaQuery";

const compact = useMediaQuery("(max-width: 40rem)");
const finePointer = useMediaQuery("(pointer: fine)", { defaultValue: true });
```

### Accessibility

- The server cannot know the query, so it renders `defaultValue` (default `false`). On the client React re-reads the real value during hydration, which can cause one extra render but never a hydration mismatch. Pick the default that is safest without JavaScript.
- Do not hide content from assistive technology based on a media query; hide it with CSS so the accessibility tree and the visual result stay in step.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Its stylesheet reads no `--lufia-*` tokens directly (no CSS module, or it composes other components).

### Stories

- `hooks-usemediaquery--narrow`
- `hooks-usemediaquery--dark-colour-scheme`
- `hooks-usemediaquery--hover-capable`

## useModalState

> Open, close and the element to return focus to, for a controlled modal.

- Status: beta
- Category: Hooks
- Import: `import { browserHistoryAdapter, decodeModalId, useModalState } from "@lufia/design-system/components/useModalState"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/useModalState](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/useModalState)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/hooks-usemodalstate--docs)

### Purpose

Keeps "which modal is open" in the URL, so a refresh or a shared link reopens it and the browser's back button closes it.
Router-agnostic: it talks to the URL through a small adapter.

### When to use

- Modals people link to, refresh on, or expect the back button to close: record details, edit forms.

### When not to use

- Transient confirmations and menus. A confirmation should not survive a refresh; use `useConfirmDialog` or plain state.
- Anything that must not appear in the URL (personal data belongs in the `id`'s lookup, not in the address).

### Exports

| Name | Kind |
| --- | --- |
| `browserHistoryAdapter` | constant |
| `decodeModalId` | function |
| `useModalState` | hook |

### API

#### `decodeModalId`

Decodes a composite modal id (`item::42`) that was stored URI-encoded; malformed input is returned as is.

```ts
decodeModalId(id: string | null): string | null
```

#### `useModalState`

Keeps "which modal is open" in the URL, so a refresh or a shared link reopens it and the back button closes it. When one modal opens from another (a detail view opening its history), the parent is remembered and shown again when the child closes. It owns four query parameters (`modal`, `id`, `returnModal`, `returnId`) and keeps every other one untouched. Works with any router through {@link ModalStateAdapter}; with none it uses the browser History API.

```ts
useModalState({ adapter, keys, onNavigate, }?: UseModalStateOptions): { readonly modal: string | null; readonly id: string | null; readonly returnModal: string | null; readonly returnId: string | null; readonly open: (name: string, itemId?: string | undefined, options?: ModalOpenOptions | undefined) => void; readonly close: () => void; }
```

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `__0` | `UseModalStateOptions` | no |  |

Returned members:

| Member | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `modal` | `string \| null` | yes |  |
| `id` | `string \| null` | yes |  |
| `returnModal` | `string \| null` | yes |  |
| `returnId` | `string \| null` | yes |  |
| `open` | `(name: string, itemId?: string \| undefined, options?: ModalOpenOptions \| undefined) => void` | yes |  |
| `close` | `() => void` | yes |  |

### Types

- `ModalOpenOptions`: `{ consumeKeys?: readonly string[] | undefined; }`
- `ModalStateAdapter`: `{ get: () => SearchParamsReader; set: (params: URLSearchParams, mode: "push" | "replace") => void; subscribe?: ((onChange: () => void) => () => void) | undefined; }`
- `ModalStateKeys`: `{ modal: string; id: string; returnModal: string; returnId: string; }`
- `SearchParamsReader`: `{ get(name: string): string | null; forEach(callback: (value: string, key: string) => void): void; toString(): string; }`
- `UseModalStateOptions`: `{ adapter?: ModalStateAdapter | undefined; keys?: Partial<ModalStateKeys> | undefined; onNavigate?: (() => void) | undefined; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { useModalState } from "@lufia/design-system/components/useModalState";

const { modal, id, open, close } = useModalState();

<Modal open={modal === "detail"} onClose={close} title="Detail">
  ...
</Modal>;
```

### Accessibility

- A refresh reopens the modal, and there is no opener to return focus to. Focus then goes back to the page body when it closes. If that matters, manage focus in the consumer.
- `open` pushes a history entry and `close` replaces it, so Back closes the modal and does not stack closed states.
- Opening and closing are real navigations: in a routed app, let `onNavigate` drive the same loading indication as other navigations.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Its stylesheet reads no `--lufia-*` tokens directly (no CSS module, or it composes other components).

### Stories

- `hooks-usemodalstate--default`
- `hooks-usemodalstate--opens-from-the-url`
- `hooks-usemodalstate--returns-to-the-parent`

## usePagination

> Computes the page range with ellipses for a paginator.

- Status: beta
- Category: Hooks
- Import: `import { DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE, usePagination } from "@lufia/design-system/components/usePagination"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/usePagination](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/usePagination)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/hooks-usepagination--docs)

### Purpose

State for paginating a list that is already in memory: the visible slice, the page, and previous/next handlers.

### When to use

- Tables and lists of up to a few thousand rows that the client already holds.

### When not to use

- Server-paginated data: keep the page in the URL and fetch it. This hook slices, it does not fetch.

### Exports

| Name | Kind |
| --- | --- |
| `DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE` | constant |
| `usePagination` | hook |

### API

#### `usePagination`

Client-side pagination of an in-memory list. Page numbers start at 1. Resets to page 1 when `resetKey` changes (pass the active filter or query), and stays inside the valid range when the list shrinks.

```ts
usePagination<T>(items: readonly T[], pageSize?: number, resetKey?: string): { page: number; pageSize: number; total: number; totalPages: number; slice: T[]; setPage: Dispatch<SetStateAction<number>>; hasPrev: boolean; hasNext: boolean; goPrev: () => void; goNext: () => void; show: boolean; }
```

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `readonly T[]` | yes |  |
| `pageSize` | `number` | no |  |
| `resetKey` | `string` | no |  |

Returned members:

| Member | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page` | `number` | yes |  |
| `pageSize` | `number` | yes |  |
| `total` | `number` | yes |  |
| `totalPages` | `number` | yes |  |
| `slice` | `T[]` | yes |  |
| `setPage` | `Dispatch<SetStateAction<number>>` | yes |  |
| `hasPrev` | `boolean` | yes |  |
| `hasNext` | `boolean` | yes |  |
| `goPrev` | `() => void` | yes |  |
| `goNext` | `() => void` | yes |  |
| `show` | `boolean` | yes | False when everything fits on one page, so a pager can be left out. |

### Example

```tsx
import { usePagination } from "@lufia/design-system/components/usePagination";

const { slice, page, totalPages, hasPrev, hasNext, goPrev, goNext, show } = usePagination(rows, 10, filter);
```

### Accessibility

- Render the controls in a `nav` with a label, disable (not hide) Previous/Next at the ends, and announce the position with a polite live region ("Page 2 of 3").
- The page is clamped, so a list that shrinks while on the last page shows the new last page instead of an empty one.
- When the page changes, keep keyboard focus on the control that was activated; do not move it into the list.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Its stylesheet reads no `--lufia-*` tokens directly (no CSS module, or it composes other components).

### Stories

- `hooks-usepagination--default`
- `hooks-usepagination--single-page`

## usePrefersReducedMotion

> Reads the reduced-motion preference, for code that animates in JavaScript.

- Status: beta
- Category: Hooks
- Import: `import { usePrefersReducedMotion } from "@lufia/design-system/motion"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/motion/usePrefersReducedMotion](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/motion/usePrefersReducedMotion)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/hooks-useprefersreducedmotion--docs)

### Purpose

Returns `true` while the operating system asks for reduced motion (`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`) and follows the
setting when it changes.

### When to use

- Motion CSS cannot switch off by itself: `requestAnimationFrame` loops, the Web Animations API, scroll-driven effects, or waiting for an exit animation before unmounting.

### When not to use

- Plain CSS transitions and keyframes. Give them `--lufia-motion-*` tokens, which collapse by themselves, or add a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` rule. See [Motion](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/foundations-motion--docs).

### API

#### `usePrefersReducedMotion`

Whether the user asked the system for reduced motion (`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`). Follows runtime changes. Use it for motion that CSS cannot switch off by itself: `requestAnimationFrame` loops, the Web Animations API, or deciding whether to wait for an exit animation before unmounting.

```ts
usePrefersReducedMotion(): boolean
```

### Example

```tsx
import { usePrefersReducedMotion } from "@lufia/design-system/motion";

const reduced = usePrefersReducedMotion();
if (reduced) showFinalState();
```

### Accessibility

- Reduced motion means _less_ motion, not none of the information: render the final state, do not hide the change.
- On the server the hook returns `false` (full motion), because the preference is unknown. React re-reads the real value on hydration, and CSS has already collapsed durations through the tokens.
- Without `matchMedia` (old environments, some test runners) it returns `false`.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Its stylesheet reads no `--lufia-*` tokens directly (no CSS module, or it composes other components).

### Stories

- `hooks-useprefersreducedmotion--default`

## useSlidingIndicator

> Measures the active item so an indicator can slide to it.

- Status: beta
- Category: Hooks
- Import: `import { useSlidingIndicator } from "@lufia/design-system/components/useSlidingIndicator"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/useSlidingIndicator](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/useSlidingIndicator)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/hooks-useslidingindicator--docs)

### Purpose

Slides a decorative indicator behind the active item of a tab-like row. Only `transform` animates; the items never move.

### When to use

- A small row of peer items where the chosen one should feel like it moved, not like it was swapped.

### When not to use

- Lists that wrap onto several lines or scroll in both axes: the indicator follows one box.

### API

#### `useSlidingIndicator`

Slides a decorative indicator behind the active item of `container`. Only `transform` animates; the items themselves never move, so their markup, focus and state are untouched. - `container` must be `position: relative`; the indicator is `position: absolute` at its top-left corner. Positions are measured physical coordinates, so the indicator uses `left: 0` rather than a logical inset. - `activeSelector` finds the active item inside the container. `key` re-measures when it changes (usually the active id). - The indicator starts `hidden` (server render, no script): the active item keeps its own styling until the hook shows the indicator, and CSS can hand the chrome over with `:has(> .indicator:not([hidden]))`. - The slide is enabled by `data-ready` after the first position, so the indicator never glides in from the corner. A resize jumps to the new spot instead of sliding, which would leave it at the old layout's offset for a moment. Returns the ref to put on the indicator element. Give the indicator a `transition` on `transform` under `[data-ready]`, with `--lufia-motion-*` tokens.

```ts
useSlidingIndicator(container: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>, activeSelector: string, key: unknown, { stretch }?: UseSlidingIndicatorOptions): RefObject<HTMLSpanElement | null>
```

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `container` | `RefObject<HTMLElement \| null>` | yes |  |
| `activeSelector` | `string` | yes |  |
| `key` | `unknown` | yes |  |
| `__3` | `UseSlidingIndicatorOptions` | no |  |

### Types

- `UseSlidingIndicatorOptions`: `{ stretch?: boolean | undefined; }`

### Example

```tsx
import { useSlidingIndicator } from "@lufia/design-system/components/useSlidingIndicator";

const nav = useRef<HTMLElement>(null);
const indicator = useSlidingIndicator(nav, `[data-key="${active}"]`, active);

<nav ref={nav} style={{ position: "relative" }}>
  {/* the items, one with data-key={active} */}
  <span ref={indicator} className={styles.indicator} hidden aria-hidden="true" />
</nav>;
```

### Accessibility

- The indicator is decorative: give it `aria-hidden="true"`. State stays on the items (`aria-current`, `aria-pressed`).
- It starts `hidden`, so with no script or before the first measure the active item keeps its own styling.
- The slide is switched on one frame after the first position, so it never glides in from the corner. A resize jumps instead of sliding. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the duration tokens collapse and the indicator simply appears in place.
- Positions are measured, physical coordinates; the indicator uses `left: 0` on purpose and follows the items in RTL layouts too.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Its stylesheet reads no `--lufia-*` tokens directly (no CSS module, or it composes other components).

### Stories

- `hooks-useslidingindicator--default`
- `hooks-useslidingindicator--stretch`
- `hooks-useslidingindicator--all-themes`

## useStepDirection

> Tells a stepper whether it is moving forward or back.

- Status: beta
- Category: Hooks
- Import: `import { useStepDirection } from "@lufia/design-system/components/useStepDirection"`
- Also from: `@lufia/design-system`
- Source: [src/components/useStepDirection](https://github.com/luizgabriellf/lufia-design-system/blob/main/src/components/useStepDirection)
- Storybook: [docs](https://luizgabriellf.github.io/lufia-design-system/?path=/docs/hooks-usestepdirection--docs)

### Purpose

Tells a multi-step flow which way it just moved, so the new step can slide in from the matching side.

### When to use

- Wizards and stepped dialogs, where direction helps people keep their place ("one direction language": forward is right, back is left).

### When not to use

- Tabs or other non-linear navigation, where there is no forward.

### API

#### `useStepDirection`

Which way a multi-step flow just moved: `"next"` when `step` increased, `"back"` when it decreased, `undefined` until the first change (so opening a wizard never plays a slide) and again once the flow is no longer `active`. Render it as `data-step-direction` on the step container and let CSS slide the new step in from that side: forward comes from the right, back from the left.

```ts
useStepDirection(step: number, active?: boolean): StepDirection | undefined
```

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `step` | `number` | yes |  |
| `active` | `boolean` | no |  |

### Types

- `StepDirection`: `"next" | "back"`

### Example

```tsx
import { useStepDirection } from "@lufia/design-system/components/useStepDirection";

const direction = useStepDirection(step, open);

<div data-step-direction={direction}>{current}</div>;
```

### Accessibility

- The hook only returns a value; it moves nothing. Keep the keyframes `from`-only and driven by `--lufia-motion-*` tokens so they collapse under `prefers-reduced-motion` (see Motion).
- The direction must never be the only signal of the new step: announce it (`Stepper` does) and keep the heading current.
- Opening the flow returns `undefined`, so a wizard never slides on first paint.

### Motion

Its stylesheet has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch of its own; any motion comes from the motion tokens, which collapse under reduced motion.

### Tokens

Its stylesheet reads no `--lufia-*` tokens directly (no CSS module, or it composes other components).

### Stories

- `hooks-usestepdirection--default`
